11.02.010.title: Generally
11.02.010.text:
Whenever the words and phrases which are defined in this Chapter are used in this
Title, they shall have the meanings respectively ascribed to them in this Chapter,
unless the context otherwise requires or a specific definition elsewhere is made to
apply.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.02.020.title: Undefined words or phrases—State definitions
11.02.020.text:
Whenever any word or phrase used in this Title is not defined by this Chapter or by
another provision of this Title applicable thereto, but is defined in NRS Chapters
484A to 484E, inclusive, regulating the operation of vehicles, the definition contained
in those chapters shall apply to that word or phrase.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.02.030.title: Access aisle
11.02.030.text:
"Access aisle" means an area that is:
(1)
Adjacent to a parking space designated for the handicapped;
(2)
Designed to allow for unobstructed ingress, egress and access between a vehicle and
an accessible route of travel; and
(3)
Marked by spaced, crosshatched or diagonal stripes of a color that contrasts with
the paving material or by a distinctive change in paving material.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.02.032.title: Central Traffic District—Defined
11.02.032.text:
"Central Traffic District" means the entirety of the discrete area depicted by a Central
Traffic District map to be produced by the Department of Public Works, the boundaries
of which shall conform initially with the map provided as an attachment to Ordinance
No. 6555. Such map may be amended by resolution of the City Council, after receiving
a recommendation from the Traffic and Parking Commission to amend the boundaries of
such district in conformance with Subsection B of Section 11.39.055.
(Ord. No. 6555, § 2, 11-2-16)

11.02.040.title: Circulatory roadway
11.02.040.text:
"Circulatory roadway" means that portion of a highway within a roundabout, not including
any crosswalk, that is used by vehicles to travel counterclockwise around a central
island.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.02.050.title: City parking facility
11.02.050.text:
"City parking facility" includes a parking lot, parking garage, or other parking structure
or facility which the City owns, operates or maintains, or in which the City enforces
the provisions of this Title.
(Ord. No. 6703, § 1, 10-2-19; Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.02.060.title: Code enforcement authority
11.02.060.text:
"Code enforcement authority" means any department or function of the City assigned
to the enforcement of the nuisance ordinances or zoning ordinances of the City.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.02.070.title: Commercial vehicle
11.02.070.text:
"Commercial vehicle" means a motor vehicle or combination of motor vehicle and trailer
maintained or used primarily for the furtherance of a commercial enterprise.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.02.080.title: Construction zone
11.02.080.text:
"Construction zone" means that portion of a public street which, because of the construction
activities occurring thereon or in proximity thereto, has been designated by the City
Traffic Engineer for a temporary reduction in the normal speed limit for a redirection
of the normal flow of traffic, or both, in order to protect the public health, safety
and welfare.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.02.082.title: Electric bicycle
11.02.082.text:
"Electric bicycle" means a device upon which a person may ride, having two or three
wheels, or every such device generally recognized as a bicycle that has fully operable
pedals, a seat or saddle for the rider, an electric motor which produces not more
than seven hundred fifty watts and meets the requirements of one of the following
three classes:
(1)
Class 1 electric bicycle;
(2)
Class 2 electric bicycle; or
(3)
Class 3 electric bicycle.
The term does not include a moped, a motorcycle, an all-terrain motorcycle, or an
electric scooter.
"Class 1 electric bicycle" means an electric bicycle equipped with a motor that provides
assistance only when the rider is pedaling and ceases to provide assistance when the
bicycle reaches the speed of twenty miles per hour.
"Class 2 electric bicycle" means an electric bicycle equipped with a motor that may
be used exclusively to propel the bicycle and is not capable of providing assistance
when the bicycle reaches the speed of twenty miles per hour.
"Class 3 electric bicycle" means an electric bicycle equipped with a motor that provides
assistance only when the rider is pedaling and ceases to provide assistance when the
bicycle reaches the speed of twenty-eight miles per hour.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 1, 8-6-25)

11.02.083.title: Electric scooter
11.02.083.text:
"Electric scooter" means a device with handlebars and an electric motor that is designed
to be ridden on in an upright or seated position and propelled by its electric motor
or by propulsion provided by the rider. Such a device must not weigh more than one
hundred pounds without a rider and must have a maximum speed of not more than twenty
miles per hour when powered solely by its electric motor. The term does not include
a scooter that is designed or intended by its manufacturer to be used primarily as
an assistive device to increase, maintain, or improve the mobility of an individual
with a disability or other physical condition that limits or impairs the individual's
ability to walk.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 2, 8-6-25)

11.02.085.title: Immobilization device
11.02.085.text:
"Immobilization device," "immobilizing device" or "immobilizer" means a device that
immobilizes a parked motor vehicle or otherwise renders it incapable of being driven
away from a particular location. The term includes without limitation any device or
mechanism that attaches to:
(1)
The tire, wheel or any other exterior part of a vehicle so as to make the vehicle
inoperable; or
(2)
The front windshield of a vehicle so as to obstruct the driver's view through the
windshield.
(Ord. No. 6703, § 2, 10-2-19)

11.02.090.title: Limousine or limo
11.02.090.text:
"Limousine" or "limo" means a lengthened motor vehicle which is designed, maintained
and used on a commercial basis to accommodate and transport up to ten persons, including
the driver, and which is properly licensed to provide limousine service.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.02.100.title: Muffler
11.02.100.text:
"Muffler" means a device consisting of a series of chambers or baffle plates, or other
mechanical design for the purpose of receiving exhaust gas from an internal combustion
engine, and effective in reducing noise.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.02.110.title: Recreational vehicle
11.02.110.text:
"Recreational vehicle" means any vehicle or trailer designed, maintained and used
as a travel trailer, camper, motor home, tent trailer, boat, boat trailer, snowmobile,
snowmobile trailer, personal watercraft, personal watercraft trailer, camping trailer
or other vehicle of a similar nature.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.02.120.title: RTC bus
11.02.120.text:
"RTC bus" means a vehicle which is owned or operated by the Regional Transportation
Commission of Southern Nevada or another governmental entity, provides transportation
for at least eleven persons, including the driver, and is marked so as to identify
it as an RTC bus.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.02.130.title: Roundabout
11.02.130.text:
"Roundabout" means an intersection characterized by a circulatory roadway, channelized
approaches and yield control of entering traffic. A roundabout encompasses the area
bounded by the outermost curb line or, if there is no curb, the edge of the pavement,
and includes the crosswalks on any entering or exiting roadway.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.02.140.title: Taxicab
11.02.140.text:
"Taxicab" means a motor vehicle which is properly licensed under State and local law
to provide taxicab service for a charge or fee.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.02.150.title: Tour bus
11.02.150.text:
"Tour bus" or "shuttle bus" means a motor vehicle, other than a limousine, which is
designed, maintained and used to transport more than six persons, including the driver,
to or from hotels, motels, casinos, cultural or athletic events or other tourist attractions
or points of interest.
(Ord. No. 6629, § 4, 8-15-18; Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.02.160.title: Traffic Bureau
11.02.160.text:
"Traffic Bureau" means the Traffic Bureau of the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.02.170.title: Trailer
11.02.170.text:
"Trailer" means a vehicle, other than a commercial vehicle or recreational vehicle,
that is without motor power, is designed and constructed to be drawn by a motor vehicle,
and is designed and constructed and used for carrying persons, property, equipment
or other items on its own structure, including, but not limited to semitrailers, utility
trailers, flatbed trailers, and hauling trailers.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 2, 6-18-14)

11.04.010.title: Traffic engineer—Established—Qualifications
11.04.010.text:
The position of City Traffic Engineer is established. The City Traffic Engineer shall
be a qualified engineer and shall be appointed under civil service and he shall exercise
the powers and duties as provided in this Title and in the traffic regulations of
this City.
(Prior code § 10-6-1(A))

11.04.020.title: Traffic engineer—General duty
11.04.020.text:
It shall be the general duty of the City Traffic Engineer to:
(A)
Determine the installation and proper timing and maintenance of traffic-control devices;
(B)
Conduct engineering analysis of traffic accidents and to devise remedial measures;
(C)
Conduct engineering investigations of traffic conditions;
(D)
Plan the operation of traffic on the streets and the highways of this City; and
(E)
Cooperate with other City officials in the development of ways and means to improve
traffic conditions; and
(F)
Carry out the additional powers and duties imposed by ordinances of this City.
(Prior code § 10-6-1(B))

11.04.025.title: Traffic engineer—Right to delegate
11.04.025.text:
The City Traffic Engineer may delegate or assign to another department, division,
function or officer or employee of the City any power or duty that:
(A)
Is assigned to the City Traffic Engineer under this Title; and
(B)
Relates to the stopping, standing, parking or loading of vehicles.
(Ord. No. 6184, § 2, 3-21-12)

11.04.030.title: Traffic Bureau duties
11.04.030.text:
It shall be the duty of the Traffic Bureau, with such aid as may be rendered by other
members of the Metropolitan Police Department, to:
(A)
Enforce the street traffic regulations of the City and all of the State vehicle laws
applicable to the street traffic in the City;
(B)
Make arrests for traffic violations;
(C)
Investigate accidents;
(D)
Cooperate with the City Engineer and other officers of the City in the administration
of the traffic laws and in developing means to improve traffic conditions; and
(E)
Carry out those duties specially imposed upon said Bureau by this Title.
(Ord. 2203 § 16, 1981: prior code § 10-6-4)

11.04.040.title: Police—Enforcement duty generally
11.04.040.text:
It is the duty of the officers of the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department and
such other officers as are assigned by the Sheriff to enforce, and, to the extent
consistent with State law, officers of the City's Deputy Marshal Unit are authorized
to enforce, all street traffic laws of the City and all of the State vehicle laws
applicable to street traffic in the City.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 3, 6-18-14; Ord. 5870 § 2, 2006: Ord. 3484 § 1, 1990: Ord. 2203
§ 15 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-6-3(A))

11.04.050.title: Police—Traffic direction
11.04.050.text:
Officers of the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department and such officers as are
assigned by the Sheriff, and officers of the City's Deputy Marshal Unit, are authorized
to direct all traffic by voice, hand or signal in conformance with traffic laws; provided
that, in the event of a fire or other emergency or to expedite traffic or to safeguard
pedestrians, such officers may direct traffic as conditions may require, notwithstanding
the provisions of the traffic laws.
(Ord. 5870 § 3, 2006: Ord. 3484 § 2, 1990: Ord. 2203 § 15 (part), 1981: prior code
§ 10-6-3(B))

11.04.060.title: Department of Fire and Rescue
11.04.060.text:
Officers of the Department of Fire and Rescue, when at the scene of a fire, may direct
or assist police officers in directing traffic thereat or in the immediate vicinity.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 4, 6-18-14; Ord. 2203 § 15 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-6-3(C))

11.04.070.title: Temporary or experimental regulations
11.04.070.text:
The Sheriff of the Metropolitan Police Department and the Director of the Department
of Public Safety, by and with the approval of the City Traffic Engineer, are empowered
to make regulations necessary to make effective the provisions of the City relating
to traffic control, and to make and enforce temporary or experimental regulations
to cover emergencies or special conditions. No such temporary or experimental regulation
shall remain in effect for more than one hundred eighty days.
(Ord. No. 6518, § 16, 4-6-16; Ord. No. 6326, § 5, 6-18-14; Ord. 3484 § 3, 1990: Ord.
2203 § 14 (part), 1981: Ord. 1278 § 7, 1967: prior code § 10-6-2(A))

11.04.080.title: Testing traffic-control devices
11.04.080.text:
The City Traffic Engineer may test traffic-control devices under actual conditions
of traffic.
(Ord. 2203 § 14 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-6-2(B))

11.04.090.title: Schedules—Request to amend
11.04.090.text:
Unless otherwise provided, upon receipt of a written request to amend a Schedule in
this Title, the City Traffic Engineer in the exercise of his or her authority must:
(A)
If such request will not affect anyone other than the requestor, grant or deny the
request within thirty days of the receipt of the request.
(B)
If such request will affect persons other than the requestor, send written notice
within thirty days of the receipt of the request to the property owners, residents
and businesses within the area potentially affected by the requested amendment; which
notice shall state:
(1)
The nature of the requested amendment; and
(2)
That the person notified has fifteen days from the date of the notice to file with
the City Traffic Engineer's office written opposition to the request.
(C)
Absent the receipt of a protest pursuant to Subsection (B) of this Section, grant
or deny the request within forty-five (45) days of the receipt of the request.
(D)
Upon receipt of a protest to the request pursuant to Subsection (B) of this Section,
schedule a public hearing regarding the request at the next available regularly scheduled
meeting of the City Traffic and Parking Commission.
(E)
Send requestor and persons filing written opposition to the request written notice
of the public hearing scheduled before the City Traffic and Parking Commission pursuant
to Subsection (D) of this Section not later than five working days prior to the hearing.
(F)
If the City Traffic and Parking Commission and the City Traffic Engineer both agree
that the request should be granted, grant the request by written finding.
(G)
If the City Traffic Engineer and the City Traffic and Parking Commission cannot both
agree that the request should be granted, deny the request.
(Ord. 3990 § 1, 1996)

11.04.100.title: Schedules—Request to amend—Denial
11.04.100.text:
(A)
If a request to amend a schedule in this Title is denied pursuant to Section 11.04.090, the City Traffic Engineer must send a written notice of this fact to the requestor
within fifteen days of the decision, and such notice must further state that the requestor
has the right to appeal the decision of the City Traffic Engineer to the City Council
by filing a written notice of appeal with the City Clerk's office within forty-five
days of the date of the written notice of decision.
(B)
At the conclusion of an appeal hearing held pursuant to this Section, the City Council
may either affirm, reverse or modify the decision of the City Traffic Engineer, or
take such other action as it deems warranted.
(Ord. 3990 § 2, 1996)

11.04.110.title: Schedules—Request to amend—Written findings—Council agenda
11.04.110.text:
Any member of the City Council may request that a written finding of the City Traffic
Engineer regarding a Schedule in this Title be placed on the City Council agenda for
discussion and action. The City Council may either affirm, reverse or modify the written
finding, or take such other action as it deems warranted.
(Ord. 3990 § 3, 1996)

11.06.010.title: Conformance required
11.06.010.text:
Unless otherwise provided, it is a misdemeanor for any person to do any act forbidden
or fail to perform any act required in this Title.
(Ord. 3989 § 1, 1996: prior code § 10-7-1)

11.06.020.title: Responsibility of owners, employers, supervisors
11.06.020.text:
It is unlawful for the owner, or any other person, employing, supervising or otherwise
directing the driver of any vehicle to cause or knowingly permit the operation of
the vehicle upon a highway in any manner contrary to law.
(Ord. 2203 § 17, 1981: prior code § 10-7-2)

11.06.030.title: Orders or directions of officials
11.06.030.text:
No person shall wilfully fail or refuse to comply with any lawful order or direction
of any Officer or official who is authorized to enforce the provisions of this Chapter.
(Ord. 5870 § 4, 2006: Ord. 3090 § 1, 1983: prior code § 10-7-3)

11.06.040.title: Pushcarts—Riding animals—Animal-drawn vehicles
11.06.040.text:
Every person propelling any pushcart or riding an animal upon a roadway, and every
person driving any animal-drawn vehicle, shall be subject to the provisions of this
Code applicable to the driver of any vehicle, except those provisions of this Code
which by their very nature can have no application.
(Prior code § 10-7-4)

11.10.010.title: Violation—Infraction—Handicapped parking—Definitions
11.10.010.text:
(A)
It is a civil infraction, for which both the registered owner and the operator of
a vehicle are liable, for such vehicle to be parked or found in violation of any of
the parking laws which are set forth in this Title.
(B)
Nothing in this Title shall prohibit the parking of a vehicle, consistent with public
safety, by a physically handicapped person, a disabled veteran or a person transporting
a physically handicapped person or disabled veteran in compliance with NRS 484B.463.
(C)
For purposes of the provisions of this Title that pertain to the parking, stopping,
standing or loading of vehicles, unless otherwise indicated:
(1)
"Operator" means and includes every individual who operates a vehicle as the owner
thereof, or as the agent, employee or permittee of the owner, or is in actual physical
control of a vehicle.
(2)
"Park" or "parking" means the standing, stopping or halting of a vehicle, whether
occupied or not, upon a street, including temporarily for the purpose of, and while
engaged in, receiving or discharging passengers or loading or unloading freight, cargo,
merchandise or other goods, but not including in obedience to traffic regulations,
signs or signals or an involuntary stopping of the vehicle by reason of causes beyond
the control of the operator of the vehicle.
(3)
"Parking meter" means and includes any mechanical device or meter not inconsistent
with this Title placed or erected for the regulation of parking by authority of this
Title.
(4)
"Parking meter space" means any space within a parking meter zone that is assigned
to or governed by a parking meter, duly designated for the parking of a single vehicle,
and marked as such by painted lines or other durable markings on the curb, street
surface, or other location for the space.
(5)
"Parking meter zone" includes any street or City parking facility upon or in which
parking meters are installed and in operation.
(6)
"Registered owner" means a person whose name appears in the records of the Nevada
Department of Motor Vehicles as the person to whom a vehicle is registered.
(7)
"Street" means any public street, avenue, road, alley, highway, lane, path or other
public place located in the City and established for the conveyance of vehicular traffic.
(8)
"Vehicle" means any device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be
transported upon a highway, except a device which is operated upon rails or tracks.
(D)
For purposes of this Chapter:
(1)
"Level 1 appeal" means the initial process for appealing a Notice of Infraction under
this Chapter, as described in LVMC 11.10.080.
(2)
"Level 2 appeal" means the process for further appealing the decision made in a Level
1 appeal, as described in LVMC 11.10.100.
(3)
"Parking Services Division" means the Parking Services Division of the Department
of Economic and Urban Development.
(4)
"Schedule of fines and penalties" means the schedule adopted pursuant to LVMC 11.10.140.
(Ord. No. 6703, § 3, 10-2-19; Ord. No. 6437, § 1, 8-5-15; Ord. No. 6326, § 6, 6-18-14;
Ord. No. 6184, § 3, 3-21-12; Ord. 3829 § 1 (part), 1994)

11.10.020.title: Violation—Notice of Infraction
11.10.020.text:
Whenever any vehicle is found in violation of the parking laws which are set forth
in this Title, a Notice of Infraction may be issued in accordance with this Chapter.
(Ord. 5870 § 5, 2006: Ord. 3829 § 1 (part), 1994)

11.10.030.title: Notice of Infraction—Contents
11.10.030.text:
(A)
A Notice of Infraction issued under this Chapter must contain the following information:
(1)
The state and license number and the make of the vehicle which is parked in violation
of the provisions of this Code;
(2)
The location at which the violation occurred;
(3)
The date and time of the violation;
(4)
The location and number of the parking space, if the vehicle is violating a parking
regulation respecting the use of parking meters, as provided for in Chapter 11.54;
(5)
The name of the person who issues the Notice of Infraction;
(6)
The section of this Code which allegedly is being violated;
(7)
Information which advises of the manner in which, and the time within which, the Notice
of Infraction must be answered;
(8)
Such other information as the Parking Services Division may prescribe.
(B)
No error concerning or omission of any of the above-described information is grounds
for the dismissal of an action relating to a Notice of Infraction unless the person
requesting such a disposition demonstrates substantial prejudice therefrom by a preponderance
of the evidence.
(C)
Where the Notice of Infraction data is entered into and stored in a computer or similar
device, any printout or other output readable by sight which accurately reflects such
data is an "original" Notice of Infraction for purposes of this Chapter. Any such
recording which is moved or copied into another computer or similar device and is
intended to have the same effect by the issuing officer is also an "original" Notice
of Infraction for purposes of this Chapter.
(D)
Any Notice of Infraction issued pursuant to this Chapter, shall constitute a declaration
which is subject to the penalty of perjury.
(Ord. No. 6437, § 2, 8-5-15; Ord. No. 6326, § 7, 6-18-14; Ord. No. 6184, § 4, 3-21-12;
Ord. 5870 § 6, 2006: Ord. 3829 § 1 (part), 1994)

11.10.040.title: Notice of Infraction—Issuance
11.10.040.text:
The Notice of Infraction may be issued by any peace officer or by any officer of the
unit of the Department of Economic and Urban Development assigned to parking enforcement.
(Ord. No. 6184, § 5, 3-21-12; Ord. 3829 § 1 (part), 1994)

11.10.050.title: Notice of Infraction—Filing
11.10.050.text:
An original Notice of Infraction, or a facsimile thereof, must be filed with and retained
by the Parking Services Division of the Department of Economic and Urban Development
and is deemed to be a public record of matters which are observed pursuant to a duty
which is imposed by law and is prima facie evidence of the facts which are alleged
therein. An original or duplicate of the Notice of Infraction must be served on the
person to whom it is issued as provided in Section 11.10.060.
(Ord. No. 6184, § 6, 3-21-12; Ord. 5870 § 7, 2006: Ord. 3829 § 1 (part), 1994)

11.10.060.title: Notice of Infraction—Service
11.10.060.text:
(A)
The Notice of Infraction must be served upon the owner and/or operator of the vehicle
by affixing the Notice to the vehicle in a conspicuous place. Service of the Notice
of Infraction by affixation has the same force and effect and is subject to the same
penalties for the disregard thereof as if the Notice of Infraction were personally
served on the owner and/or operator of the vehicle. In lieu of service by affixation
the Notice of Infraction may be personally served upon the owner and/or operator of
the vehicle. In lieu of personal service or service by affixation, the Notice of Infraction
may be mailed by regular mail to the owner and/or operator of the vehicle where the
operator of the vehicle successfully resists affixation and immediate personal service
of the Notice of Infraction, and such service has the same force and effect and is
subject to the same penalties for the disregard thereof as if the Notice of Infraction
were personally served upon the owner and/or operator of the vehicle.
(B)
For the purposes of this Chapter, an operator of a vehicle who is not the owner thereof
but who uses or operates the vehicle with the permission of the owner, express or
implied, is deemed to be the agent of the owner to receive a Notice of Infraction,
whether it is personally served on the operator or served by affixation, and service
made in either manner is also deemed to be lawful service upon the owner.
(Ord. 3829 § 1 (part), 1994)

11.10.070.title: Liability—Leased or rented vehicles
11.10.070.text:
(A)
The operator of a vehicle is liable for the civil fines and civil penalties which
are imposed pursuant to this Chapter. The registered owner of the vehicle, even if
not the operator thereof, is also liable for such civil fines and civil penalties
unless the owner is able to demonstrate that the vehicle was used without permission,
express or implied. A registered owner who pays any civil fine and/or civil penalty
pursuant to this Chapter has the right to recover from the operator of the vehicle
the civil fine and/or civil penalty so paid and has a cause of action in any court
which has appropriate jurisdiction against the operator of the vehicle for the amount
so paid.
(B)
In order to hold the operator of a leased or rented vehicle primarily responsible
for the issuance of the Notice of Infraction, the name, address and phone number of
the person renting or leasing a vehicle found parked in violation of this Title must
be provided by the rental or leasing agent or agency to the Parking Services Division
within thirty calendar days of receiving notice of such infraction. Nothing in this
provision shall absolve the owner of responsibility for the issuance of the Notice
of Infraction as provided in this Chapter.
(Ord. No. 6437, § 1, 8-5-15; Ord. 6007 § 1, 2008: Ord. 5870 § 8, 2006: Ord. 3829 §
1 (part), 1994)

11.10.080.title: Notice of Infraction—Duties of respondent—Appeal
11.10.080.text:
(A)
The owner or operator of a vehicle concerning which a Notice of Infraction has been
issued and served in accordance with this Chapter must do one of the following:
(1)
"Admit" responsibility for the commission of the infraction and liability for the
penalty imposed and pay the appropriate civil fine and penalty;
(2)
Contact the Parking Services Division, "admit" responsibility and liability for the
commission of the infraction and any penalties thereon and arrange a schedule for
the payment of such fines and penalties; or
(3)
Appeal the Notice of Infraction, as provided for in Subsections (B) to (E), inclusive,
of this Section in order to disclaim responsibility as the owner or operator, or to
dispute the propriety of the issuance of the Notice of Infraction and any penalties
related thereto.
→The time periods within which such actions must be taken are set forth in LVMC 11.10.090.
(B)
A person may initiate an appeal pursuant to Paragraph (3) of Subsection (A) of this
Section (a Level 1 appeal) by submitting an appeal to the Parking Services Division.
The appeal shall be submitted on a form provided by the Parking Services Division,
which form shall require the person initiating the appeal (the "Level 1 appellant")
to indicate, among other things, his or her name, current address, a reference to
the Notice of Infraction appealed from and the associated penalties, and the grounds
for appeal.
(C)
The Level 1 appeal shall be decided administratively by the Parking Services Division
based on a review of the Notice of Infraction, the circumstances surrounding its issuance,
and any grounds or evidence provided by the appellant. The Parking Services Division
may decide in favor of the Level 1 appellant by finding no liability, may find liability
but impose a fine in an amount less than that set forth in this Title, or may waive
late fees and penalties for any one or more of the following reasons:
(1)
The owner of the vehicle is able to demonstrate that the vehicle had been stolen or
was displaying stolen license plates at the time it was parked;
(2)
In connection with an alleged violation of an ordinance pertaining to a meter, the
meter was mechanically malfunctioning to the extent that its reliability was questionable;
(3)
Compliance with the ordinance provision alleged to have been violated would have presented
an imminent danger to persons or property;
(4)
The area of the alleged violation was so inadequately marked or lit as to fail to
give sufficient notice that access to the area was restricted or prohibited;
(5)
A mechanical malfunction of the vehicle caused it to be parked in the area alleged
and it was removed as soon as could be reasonably expected thereafter;
(6)
At the time of the issuance of the Notice of Infraction, the vehicle was parked consistent
with and in compliance with NRS 484B.463 pertaining to persons with a disability or
handicap;
(7)
The Level 1 appellant establishes by a preponderance of the evidence that, through
no fault of himself or his agent, he or she failed to receive notice of the issuance
of the Notice of Infraction as provided in this Chapter;
(8)
The operator of the vehicle experienced a medical or other emergency;
(9)
The Notice of Infraction was issued in error;
(10)
The violation relates to the parking of a law enforcement vehicle while on official
business;
(11)
The existence of unclear transfer of ownership of a vehicle;
(12)
Bankruptcy or death of an owner;
(13)
Payment was made for the wrong parking space;
(14)
The vehicle in question was registered even though the current registration was not
displayed;
(15)
The vehicle in question was eligible to park in a handicapped space even though placard
not displayed;
(16)
The vehicle in question was ineligible to park in a handicap access aisle but was
eligible to park in a handicap space; or
(17)
Financial hardship—living below federally designated poverty level.
(D)
Notwithstanding any other provision of this Chapter, the Parking Services Division
has the discretion, but is under no obligation, to decide in favor of a particular
appellant by finding no liability, finding liability but imposing a fine less than
that set forth in this Title, waiving late fees and penalties otherwise accruing,
or converting a Notice of Infraction to a warning upon a determination that, considering
all the circumstances, unfairness would otherwise result. Examples include the issuance
of a Notice of Infraction:
(1)
Under circumstances or in a manner contrary to one or more policies duly adopted by
the Parking Services Division; or
(2)
At a location concerning which motorists have been mistakenly led to believe that
parking at that location and time is not subject to the parking restrictions otherwise
in force.
→Any disposition under the authority of this Subsection (D) must be properly documented.
(E)
Notice of the decision made by the Parking Services Division in connection with a
Level 1 appeal shall be provided to the Level 1 appellant by:
(1)
Mailing such notice to the appellant at the address provided by the Level 1 appellant;
(2)
Mailing such notice to the address of the Level 1 appellant on file with the Nevada
Department of Motor Vehicles; or
(3)
Sending such notice to the Level 1 appellant by electronic mail, if such appellant
has requested communication by means of electronic mail.
(F)
Within thirty days after notice of a decision has been provided pursuant to Subsection
(E) of this Section, the Level 1 appellant must:
(1)
Pay or cause to be paid in full all fines and penalties remaining to be paid regarding
the Notice of Violation;
(2)
Make arrangements with the City regarding a schedule for the payment of such fines
and penalties; or
(3)
Request an appeal hearing (a Level 2 appeal) in accordance with LVMC 11.10.100.
(Ord. No. 6437, § 5, 8-5-15)
Editor's note—
Ord. No. 6437, § 4, adopted August 5, 2015, repealed the former § 11.10.080, and §
5 of Ord. No. 6437 enacted a new § 11.10.080 as set out herein. The former § 11.10.080
pertained to notice of infraction—duties of respondent—hearing and derived from Ord.
3829, 1994; Ord. No. 5334, 2001; Ord. No. 6096, adopted June 2, 2010; Ord. No. 6184,
adopted March 21, 2012 and Ord. No. 6326, adopted June 18, 2014.

11.10.090.title: Notice of Infraction—Response—Supplementary notice
11.10.090.text:
(A)
Subject to the provisions of Subsection (C), a response to a Notice of Infraction
that is intended to admit liability, in accordance with LVMC 11.10.080(A)(1) or 11.10.080(A)(2), must be made within thirty calendar days after the date on which the Notice
of Infraction is served. If no response is received during such thirty-day period,
the Notice of Infraction is subject to an additional civil penalty as set forth in
the schedule of fines and penalties, identified under the heading "Late 1."
(B)
After the expiration of the thirty-day response period described in Subsection (A),
the Parking Services Division must send a Notice of Delinquency by regular mail to
the registered owner of the vehicle at the registered owner's last known address,
as indicated by the vehicle registration which is maintained by the Nevada Department
of Motor Vehicles. The Notice of Delinquency must contain the date of the infraction,
the amount of the civil fine and the amount of any penalty which is associated therewith.
The registered owner will have fifteen calendar days after the date of the Notice
of Delinquency in which to respond thereto in the manner which is provided in LVMC
11.10.080. If no response is made to the Notice of Delinquency within such additional fifteen-day
period, an additional civil penalty will be assessed in an amount set forth in the
schedule of fines and penalties, identified under the heading "Late 2".
(C)
A person who wishes to appeal a Notice of Infraction in accordance with LVMC 11.10.080(A)(3) must do so within ninety calendar days after the date on which the Notice is
served. To the extent the appeal is filed after any of the response periods set forth
in Subsections (A) and (B) of this Section, the additional civil penalties shall attach
to the Notice of Infraction and the appeal will include those penalties in addition
to the amount of the initial civil fine.
(D)
In addition to and independent of any notice required by this Chapter, the Parking
Services Division is authorized to provide supplementary notice of the existence of
and duties regarding a Notice of Infraction, including without limitation an additional
notice fourteen days after the issuance and service of a Notice of Infraction. Such
supplementary notice is provided as a courtesy only, and any failure or irregularity
regarding such supplementary notice provides no defense or recourse under this Chapter.
(E)
If a person fails to respond to a Notice of Infraction or a Notice of Delinquency
in accordance with this Chapter, the City is entitled to collect the amount of any
fines and penalties by means of any remedy available under applicable law, including
without limitation filing a notice of nonpayment with the Nevada Department of Motor
Vehicles and referring the matter to a collection agency.
(Ord. No. 6437, § 6, 8-5-15)
Editor's note—
Ord. No. 6437, § 4, adopted August 5, 2015, repealed the former § 11.10.090, and §
5 of Ord. No. 6437 enacted a new § 11.10.090 as set out herein. The former § 11.10.090
pertained to notice of infraction—response and derived from Ord. 3829, 1994; Ord.
No. 5595, 2003 and Ord. No. 6096, adopted June 2, 2010.

11.10.100.title: Level 2 appeals
11.10.100.text:
(A)
A Level 2 appeal referred to in Paragraph (3) of Subsection (F) of LVMC 11.10.080 is initiated by:
(1)
Contacting the offices of the Parking Services Division within the thirty-day period
referred to;
(2)
Requesting a Level 2 appeal hearing; and
(3)
Receiving a date for hearing the appeal.
(B)
A Level 2 appeal may be filed by or on behalf of the registered owner of the vehicle
that is subject of the Notice of Infraction.
(C)
A person requesting a Level 2 hearing (a "Level 2 appellant") shall provide such information
as the Parking Services Division may require. A Level 2 hearing shall be conducted
by a Hearing Officer provided for by the City. A Level 2 appellant shall be bound
by the decision of the Hearing Officer concerning liability for the infraction(s)
and responsibility for the penalties thereon. It is expected that a Level 2 appellant
will appear in person or by representative at a Level 2 hearing. However, at the Hearing
Officer's discretion, a hearing may be held and the appeal decided without an appearance
by the Level 2 appellant. If any Level 2 appellant scheduling a hearing before the
Hearing Officer fails to appear at such hearing without having first sought and obtained
a continuance of such hearing, the Hearing Officer may (but is not required to) enter
a decision against the appellant for the full amount of fines and penalties scheduled
to be reviewed. In connection with the request for a hearing, the Level 2 appellant
must acknowledge the binding nature of the hearing and the Hearing Officer's authority
in the event the appellant fails to appear at a hearing. The acknowledgment shall
be in substantially the following form:
I ___________, hereby request a binding hearing before the Hearing Officer. My address
is ___________. I request that this hearing involve Notice(s) of Infraction(s) Number
___________. I understand that the Hearing Officer is an attorney and not an elected
or appointed judge.
I understand that I am bound by the decision of the Hearing Officer. I understand
that I am expected to appear in person or by representative at the requested hearing,
but that the hearing may be held and the appeal decided without such appearance. I
understand that if I fail to appear for the scheduled hearing before the Hearing Officer
without first obtaining a continuance of such hearing, the Hearing Officer may (but
is not required to) enter a decision against me for the full amount and penalties
scheduled to be reviewed. I understand and agree that if necessary due to my lack
of timely payment, the City of Las Vegas can and will use this binding decision to
have a formal civil judgment entered against me in the Las Vegas Municipal Court.
I understand that if a civil judgment is obtained, the City may seek and obtain a
writ of execution against me. I understand that if a writ of execution is obtained,
my wages and/or bank accounts may be garnished, liens may be put on my property and
my vehicle(s) may be towed or immobilized. I also understand that my vehicle(s) may
be immobilized without a writ of execution if:
1. I accumulate more than $200.00 in unpaid civil fines, judgments and penalties
for parking violations; and
2. At least two Notices of Infraction have been issued and served with respect to
vehicles registered to me and have not been responded to within the time set forth
in LVMC 11.10.090.
Knowing all of the above, I still wish to request a binding hearing before the Hearing
Officer on the above-described Notice(s) of Infraction(s). I hereby acknowledge the
above and further acknowledge that at my request a hearing has been set for _______,
20___ at the hour of ___m.
___________
Appellant
(D)
Any Level 2 appeal hearing conducted pursuant to this Section shall be presided over
by a Hearing Officer who shall be an attorney licensed to practice law in the State
of Nevada.
(E)
The Hearing Officer may decide in favor of the Level 2 appellant by finding no liability,
may find liability but impose a fine in an amount less than that set forth in this
Title, or may waive late fees and penalties for any one or more of the reasons set
forth in Subsection (C) or Subsection (D) of LVMC 11.10.080.
(F)
The appellant shall pay the total civil fines and penalties forthwith or at such times
and on such conditions as the Hearing Officer shall prescribe if it is found that
the person has either failed to appear or otherwise defend against the issuance of
the infraction, or that the infraction has been committed and no applicable defense
exists. If the appellant fails to pay in accordance with the times and conditions
of the Hearing Officer's decision and any amount due remains unpaid thirty days after
the date due, all amounts outstanding shall be deemed delinquent, including unpaid
portions of the original fine amount and associated penalties. The City shall have
the right to collect such amounts by any means set forth in this Chapter or otherwise
available under law.
(G)
Upon reaching a decision, the Hearing Officer shall, as soon as practicable thereafter,
file a written decision substantially conforming to the following form:
___________, Appellant vs. City of Las Vegas, Nevada, Parking Services Division,
Respondent. Before, ___________, Hearing Officer for the City of Las Vegas, decision
is entered in favor of ___________, (appellant or City Parking Services Division)
for $_______ (enter $0.00 if judgment is for the appellant), on the ___ day of _______,
20_______. I certify that the foregoing is a correct reflection of the decision entered
in the action properly brought for my consideration pursuant to LVMC Chapter 11.10.
___________
Hearing Officer
(H)
The City Attorney may petition the Las Vegas Municipal Court for the entry of a civil
judgment against the appellant in an amount equal to that stated in the written decision
of the Hearing Officer if the City Attorney determines this action to be necessary
to enforce such decision. Service of such petition on the defendant must be made by
certified mail, return receipt requested, restricted delivery, addressed to the registered
owner of the vehicle at his last known address, as indicated by the vehicle registration
which is maintained by the Nevada Department of Motor Vehicles or in any other manner
which is authorized by law. An affidavit or declaration of mailing, a signed, returned
receipt, or other evidence of service shall be filed upon such service of the petition.
Once a petition for civil judgment pursuant to this Subsection (H) has been filed
with the Municipal Court, the assigned judge has jurisdiction to grant or deny the
relief prayed for therein.
(Ord. No. 6437, § 5, 8-5-15)

11.10.110.title: Filing and processing of a Level 1 appeal or Level 2 appeal
11.10.110.text:
In connection with the filing and processing of a Level 1 appeal or Level 2 appeal:
(A)
A person who is an individual may be represented by a member of the person's immediate
family, with the written consent of the individual to be represented, or by an attorney
who is licensed to practice law in Nevada. A business or other entity may be represented
by an officer of the entity or by an attorney who is licensed to practice law in Nevada.
(B)
A properly filed Notice of Infraction shall constitute a claim of liability and a
claim for relief and no other such claim shall be required. Prima facie proof of the
violation alleged shall be established by means of a certified copy of the Notice
of Infraction or by reference to the data stored in a computer or other device as
described in Subsection (C) of LVMC 11.10.030. No formal appearance by the City Attorney's office is required. The hearing and
disposition of all appeals shall be informal, with the purpose of dispensing timely
and appropriate justice.
(C)
The burden of proving any defense shall be upon the person raising such defense.
(Ord. No. 6437, § 5, 8-5-15)

11.10.120.title: Payment schedules
11.10.120.text:
(A)
In connection with a request to arrange a payment schedule pursuant to LVMC 11.10.080(A)(2), or as otherwise made available by the Parking Services Division under this
Chapter, the Parking Services Division is authorized to charge an administrative fee
in the amount of twenty-five dollars for the establishment of such a schedule. The
fee is non-refundable.
(B)
If a person who has arranged a payment schedule pursuant to this Chapter fails to
pay in accordance with the terms and conditions of the schedule and any amount due
remains unpaid fifteen days after the date due, all amounts outstanding shall be deemed
delinquent, including unpaid portions of the original fine amount and associated penalties.
The City shall have the right to collect such amounts by any means set forth in this
Chapter or otherwise available under law.
(Ord. No. 6437, § 5, 8-5-15)

11.10.130.title: Monetary sanctions for prohibited or unlawful acts
11.10.130.text:
(A)
Subject to the provisions of Subsection (B), whenever in this Title an act relating
to the stopping, standing or parking of a vehicle is prohibited or limited, or the
violation of such a prohibition or limitation is made or declared to be unlawful or
an offense or a misdemeanor, the sanction therefor is civil in nature in the monetary
amount which is set forth in the schedule of fines and penalties.
(B)
With respect to any particular violation of the following types, the City may proceed
either by means of a criminal prosecution or by means of the civil infraction process
set forth in this Chapter 11.10:
(1)
A violation of LVMC 11.54.205 or 11.65.110;
(2)
A violation of any other provision of Title 11 pertaining to the stopping, standing or parking of a vehicle where the violation
relates to the misuse of equipment, or involves fraud, deceit or misrepresentation,
or where the language of the provision demonstrates a specific intent for a criminal
rather than civil sanction to be applied.
(Ord. No. 6437, § 6, 8-5-15; Ord. No. 6173, § 2, 12-21-11; Ord. 5274 § 1, 2000: Ord.
3829 § 1 (part), 1994)

11.10.140.title: Schedule of civil fines established
11.10.140.text:
(A)
There is hereby adopted a schedule of fines and penalties for infractions of the parking
laws and regulations which are set forth in this Title, as well as infractions processed
under this Chapter as civil violations pursuant to LVMC 10.78.020 or 13.04.070(A). The schedule is set forth as Subsection (D) of this Section. In the case of any
violation that is not specifically identified in the schedule, the fine shall be twenty-five
dollars, with the penalties to be determined as in the case of a violation specifically
listed with a fine amount of twenty-five dollars.
(B)
The owner and/or operator shall be liable for an additional collection fee where the
collection of the fines, parking permit fees, parking facility usage fees, and penalties
provided for in this Title is referred for collection to a private collection agency.
The amount of such fee may not exceed twenty-five percent of the outstanding indebtedness
or two hundred fifty dollars, whichever is less. The amount of any such collection
fee shall accrue and become due and payable at the time the indebtedness is referred
for collection to the collection agency, and that amount may be added by the collection
agency or the Parking Services Division to the amount sought to be collected. Any
judgment or amended judgment entered under this Chapter may include the amount of
the collection fee authorized by this Subsection (B).
(C)
When a notice of nonpayment of a civil fine imposed under this Chapter has been filed
with the Nevada Department of Motor Vehicles pursuant to NRS 484B.527, the City is
authorized to charge the party liable an administrative fee of fifteen dollars to
cover the costs of the filing, handling and release of the notice of nonpayment. The
administrative fee shall be paid at the time the fine is collected and the release
authorized.

11.10.150.title: Alternative payment of fines—Donation program
11.10.150.text:
(A)
Notwithstanding the provisions of LVMC 11.10.140 or any other provision of this Chapter, the Parking Services Division, from time
to time and upon authorization pursuant to Subsection (B), may operate a program by
which fines for parking infractions may be paid by means of the donation of qualifying
items in lieu of the payment of money. In order to satisfy the amount of the fine
for any particular infraction, the qualifying items donated must be of equal or greater
value than the amount of the corresponding fine.
(B)
A program described in Subsection (A) may be authorized no more than twice per calendar
year and must be approved in advance, as to both time period and duration, by the
City Manager. The Parking Services Division may establish such procedures and requirements
regarding program events as may be desirable or appropriate, including without limitation
what types of qualifying items will apply to a particular program event; a range of
dates within which parking infractions must have been issued in order to be eligible;
and a time period within which donations in lieu of payment must be made. The determination
of the value of donations is completely within the discretion of the Parking Services
Division.
(C)
For purposes of Subsections (A) and (B), "qualifying items" means food items, children's
toys, or personal items for the benefit of specifically-identified groups in need,
including without limitation school supplies.
(Ord. No. 6829, § 1, 2-1-23; Ord. No. 6534, § 1, 6-15-16)

11.10.160.title: Failure to pay a required parking fee—Collection
11.10.160.text:
In the case of a failure to pay a required parking fee as referenced in LVMC 11.52.310 and 11.52.320, the City is entitled to collect the required parking fee in addition to and independent
of any civil fine that may be imposed, and the fee amount shall be added to and be
collectible with the amount of fines and penalties associated with the violation.
(Ord. No. 6629, § 3, 8-15-18)

11.10.170.title: Interference with parking-related services
11.10.170.text:
It is unlawful to physically obstruct, or commit assault or battery upon, a parking
enforcement officer of the City, or an employee or agent of a person or entity providing
parking-related services to the City by contract. Unless a greater penalty is prescribed
by State law, violation of this Section is a misdemeanor.
(Ord. No. 6829, § 2, 2-1-23)

11.10.180.title: Reserved
11.10.180.text:
Editor's note—
Ord. No. 6437, § 8, adopted August 5, 2015, repealed the former § 11.10.180, which
pertained to other parking infractions and derived from Ord. No. 3829, 1994; Ord.
No. 5095; Ord. No. 6149, adopted May 4, 2011; Ord. No. 6173, adopted December 21,
2011 and Ord. No. 6326, adopted June 18, 2014.

11.10.200.title: Removal of vehicle—Circumstances
11.10.200.text:
(A)
The Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department, the Department of Public Safety, and
the Parking Services Division of the Department of Economic and Urban Development
are authorized to remove a vehicle to the nearest garage or other place that has been
designated for vehicle storage by the City, under the circumstances which are hereinafter
enumerated:
(1)
When any vehicle is left unattended upon any highway, bridge, viaduct or causeway,
or in any tube or tunnel, if such vehicle constitutes an obstruction to traffic;
(2)
When a vehicle upon a street or highway is so disabled as to constitute an obstruction
to traffic and the person who is in charge of such vehicle is, by reason of physical
injury or other reason, incapacitated to the extent that he is unable to provide for
its custody or removal, or is not in the immediate vicinity of the disabled vehicle;
(3)
When any vehicle is illegally parked in a parking space or location for twenty-four
hours or more or is parked so illegally as to constitute a definite hazard or obstruction
to the normal movement of traffic;
(4)
When the person who is in charge of a vehicle is unable to provide for its custody
or removal within:
(a)
Twenty-four hours after abandoning such vehicle on any freeway, United States highway
or other primary arterial street, or
(b)
Seventy-two hours after abandoning such vehicle on any other street;
(5)
When the person who is driving or in actual physical control of a vehicle is arrested
for any alleged offense for which the arresting officer is required by law to take
such person before a proper magistrate without unnecessary delay; or
(6)
In accordance with Section 11.10.240.
(B)
As used in this Section 11.10.200 to Section 11.10.280, the term "vehicle" shall include any automobile, motorcycle, truck, boat trailer,
utility trailer, or any other vehicle capable of being driven or towed on any street,
highway, or right-of-way.
(C)
Prior to the release of any vehicle impounded pursuant to this Section, the operator,
registered owner or his designee must pay the costs of such impoundment.
(Ord. No. 6518, § 17, 4-6-16; Ord. No. 6389, § 1 12-17-14; Ord. 5334 § 2, 2001: Ord.
3829 § 1 (part), 1994)

11.10.210.title: Removal of vehicle—Notice—Known owner
11.10.210.text:
Whenever a person removes a vehicle, as authorized in LVMC 11.10.200, and such person knows or is able to ascertain from the registration records in the
vehicle or by other reasonable means the name and address of the owner thereof, such
person must immediately give, or cause to be given, notice in writing and by telephone,
if possible, to the owner of the fact of such removal, the reasons therefor and the
place to which the vehicle has been removed. In the event that the vehicle is stored
in a public garage, a copy of the notice shall be given to the proprietor of the garage.
(Ord. 3829 § 1 (part), 1994)

11.10.220.title: Removal of vehicle—Notice—Unknown owner
11.10.220.text:
Whenever a person removes a vehicle pursuant to LVMC 11.10.200 and does not know and is not able to ascertain the name of the owner, or for any
other reason is unable to give the notice to the owner, as provided in LVMC 11.10.210, and the vehicle is not picked up by the owner or his designee within a period of
three days, such person must immediately send or cause to be sent a written notice
of such removal by mail to the Nevada Department of Motor Vehicles and file a copy
of such notice with the proprietor of the garage or place in which the vehicle is
stored. Such notice must include a complete description of the vehicle, the date,
time and place from which it was removed, the reasons for such removal and the name
of the garage or place in which the vehicle is stored.
(Ord. 3829 § 1 (part), 1994)

11.10.230.title: Writs of execution—Authorized
11.10.230.text:
(A)
The use of writs of execution issued by the Las Vegas Municipal Court is authorized
within the City as an aid in the enforcement of the parking ordinances of the City.
(B)
The City of Las Vegas in whose favor a judgment is given may upon the entry of such
judgment, or at any time before the judgment expires, obtain the issuance of a writ
of execution for its enforcement as prescribed in Chapter 21 of the Nevada Revised
Statutes and Justice Court Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 69. Such issuance may be
conditioned upon the failure of the judgment debtor to pay the judgment and expenses
of enforcement thereof within a specified period of time or any other reasonable and
just condition.
(C)
Upon the City's request, a writ of execution issued pursuant to Subsection B of this
Section shall allow the City to obtain possession of the defendant's vehicle(s) through
towing the vehicle(s), at the expense of the defendant, from any public street, highway,
viaduct, causeway, parking space, tube, tunnel, bridge or alley in compliance with
the procedures prescribed in Sections 11.10.210 and 11.10.220. Upon the City's request, a writ of execution issued pursuant to Subsection B of
this Section shall allow the City to obtain possession of the defendant's vehicle(s)
through the use of an immobilizing device. A fee of fifty dollars per vehicle shall
be recovered from the owner or operator of the vehicle(s) prior to the removal of
the immobilizing device.
(D)
Notwithstanding the provisions of Subsection (C), the City may, without obtaining
a writ of execution, obtain possession of a vehicle by means of an immobilizing device
in accordance with Section 11.10.240.
(Ord. 5334 § 3, 2001: Ord. 3829 § 1 (part), 1994)

11.10.240.title: Automobile immobilizer—Conditions for use
11.10.240.text:
(A)
The City is authorized to attach an immobilizing device to a vehicle that is parked
on any public right-of-way or City-owned or operated lot if the vehicle is included
on an immobilization eligibility list. A vehicle may be included on an immobilization
eligibility list only if:
(1)
The registered owner of the vehicle has accumulated more than two hundred dollars
in unpaid civil fines, judgments and penalties, and at least two Notices of Infraction
have been issued and served with respect to that vehicle and have not been responded
to within the time set forth in Section 11.10.090; and
(2)
At least twenty-one days before including the vehicle on the list, the City provided
notice of impending vehicle immobilization in accordance with Subsection (B) of this
Section.
(B)
Notice of impending vehicle immobilization shall be provided by mailing such notice
to the registered owner of the vehicle at the address last known to the City or on
file with the Nevada Department of Motor Vehicles. The notice shall include the dates
and nature of the infractions which formed the basis for the civil fines, judgments
and penalties; the numbers of the Notices of Infraction; and the amounts owing. The
notice shall advise that the registered owner may challenge the validity of the notice
by requesting a hearing. The hearing shall be held before the Hearing Officer for
the sole purpose of allowing the registered owner to show that:
(1)
The amounts in question have been paid; or
(2)
The vehicle was not properly included on the immobilization eligibility list in accordance
with the provisions of Subsection (A) of this Section.
(C)
A vehicle shall be removed from the immobilization eligibility list if:
(1)
The registered owner pays all fines, judgments, penalties and applicable immobilization
fees;
(2)
The registered owner executes an agreement to pay within a specified period of time
all fines, judgments, penalties and applicable immobilization fees, with a condition
that, for default on the payment obligation, the vehicle shall be subject to reinstatement
on the immobilization list; or
(3)
The Hearing Officer finds that the vehicle was not properly included on the immobilization
eligibility list.
(D)
In connection with the immobilization of a vehicle, a notice shall be attached to
the vehicle in a conspicuous place advising:
(1)
That the vehicle is immobilized and that any attempt to move the vehicle may result
in its damage;
(2)
That the unauthorized removal of or damage to the immobilizing device is a violation
of law;
(3)
How release of the immobilizing device may be obtained; and
(4)
How a hearing may be obtained pursuant to Subsection (H).
(E)
The City may (but is not obligated to) cause to be towed and stored any vehicle which
has been immobilized if, within twenty-four hours after immobilization, no arrangements
have been made for the vehicle's release. An unregistered vehicle that is immobilized
may be towed and stored immediately. Within ten days after an immobilized vehicle
is towed, the City shall send a notice advising that the vehicle has been immobilized
and towed. The notice shall be provided by means of certified mail, return receipt
requested, mailed to the registered owner at the address last known to the City or
on file with the Department of Motor Vehicles. The notice shall state that the registered
owner is entitled to request a hearing pursuant to Subsection (H) of this Section
to determine the validity of the immobilization. If a vehicle is towed pursuant to
this Subsection (E), the City (or a tow operator acting at the City's direction) is
authorized to remove the immobilization device for purposes of transportation and
reapply the device after the vehicle is stored at the location designated for storage
by the City.
(F)
An immobilization fee of seventy-five dollars shall be paid by or on behalf of the
registered owner of the vehicle prior to the removal of an immobilizing device.
(G)
Release of an immobilized vehicle, either by the City or by an authorized tow operator
who has been directed by the City to do so, may be obtained by:
(1)
The payment of all fines, judgments, penalties and applicable immobilization, towing
and storage fees; or
(2)
In connection with the request of a hearing to determine the validity of the immobilization
of the vehicle, the posting of a bond or other sufficient undertaking in an amount
which will satisfy all fines, judgments, penalties and applicable immobilization,
towing and storage fees.
(H)
The registered owner of a vehicle may request a hearing regarding the immobilization
of the owner's vehicle. The request for hearing must be made within ten days after
the date of the notice described in Subsection (D) or Subsection (E) of this Section.
The hearing shall be held before the Hearing Officer and shall be limited to a determination
of whether there was a factual and legal basis for the immobilization. Failure to
request or attend a hearing shall be deemed a waiver of the right to a hearing. If
the Hearing Officer determines that there was a factual and legal basis for the immobilization,
the bond or undertaking shall be forfeited. If the hearing officer determines that
there was an insufficient factual and legal basis for the immobilization, the bond
or undertaking shall be exonerated.
(Ord. No. 6437, § 9, 8-5-15; Ord. No. 6389, § 1 12-17-14; Ord. 5870 § 11, 2006: Ord.
5334 § 5, 2001)

11.10.245.title: Unlocking/releasing of immobilization device
11.10.245.text:
In connection with the use of an immobilization device pursuant to this Chapter, the
City is authorized to employ, either by itself or by means of contract, equipment
and technologies that allow the operator or owner of a vehicle to unlock or otherwise
release the immobilization device by the electronic payment of delinquent fines and
immobilization fees. In connection with the use of such equipment and technologies,
and in addition to and independent of applicable immobilizer fees under this Title,
the City may require the operator or owner of a vehicle to:
(A)
Acknowledge responsibility to return an immobilization device to a designated location
within a specified time period; and
(B)
Authorize a hold to be placed on a debit or credit card account in the amount of seventy-five
dollars, to be either: 1) released when the device is properly returned, or 2) kept
by the City or its vendor if the device is not properly returned within the specified
time period.
(Ord. No. 6703, § 5, 10-2-19)

11.10.250.title: Writ of execution—Procedure upon issuance
11.10.250.text:
Upon the issuance of a writ of execution pursuant to Section 11.10.230, the provisions of Chapter 21 of the Nevada Revised Statutes shall apply, including
the following:
(1)
The writ must be issued in the name of the City of Las Vegas, sealed with the seal
of the Las Vegas Municipal Court, subscribed by a clerk of such court, directed to
the Sheriff of Clark County or the sheriff of the county where the real or personal
property subject to execution is located and otherwise in substantially the same form
as directed by Nevada Revised Statutes 21.025.
(2)
A notice of execution as prescribed in Nevada Revised Statute 21.075 and 21.076 must
be prepared with the City of Las Vegas named as the judgment creditor.
(3)
The notice and a copy of the writ must be provided to the Sheriff who must serve the
notice on the defendant—judgment debtor by regular mail at his last known address,
or, if represented by an attorney, at the attorney's office. The notice must be served
by regular mail the next business day after the writ of execution was served.
(4)
In order to claim exemption of any property, the defendant must, within eight calendar
days after the notice is mailed, serve the Sheriff and the City of Las Vegas, through
the City Attorney and file with a Clerk of the Las Vegas Municipal Court an affidavit
setting out the claim of exemption. The Municipal Court Administrator shall provide
the form for the affidavit.
(5)
When the affidavit is served, the Sheriff shall release the property unless within
five calendar days after written demand by the Sheriff, the City of Las Vegas files
a motion for a hearing to determine whether the money or property is exempt.
(6)
The hearing to determine whether the property or money is exempt must be held within
ten calendar days after the filing of the motion for a hearing, unless the court continues
the hearing for good cause shown. The defendant shall receive at least five calendar
days' notice of the hearing.
(7)
If at any time the defendant satisfies the judgment, including costs for the enforcement
thereof, any property taken pursuant to a writ of execution shall be released to the
defendant as soon as possible thereafter.
(Ord. 3829 § 1 (part), 1994)

11.10.260.title: Failure to timely file claim of exemption
11.10.260.text:
If the defendant—judgment debtor fails to timely file a claim of exemption or fails
to appear at the scheduled hearing to resolve the validity of the claimed exemption,
title and/or lawful possession of the property taken pursuant to the writ of execution
may be transferred in satisfaction of the judgment and expenses of enforcing such
judgment as provided by Chapter 21 of the Nevada Revised Statutes. If such property
is sold, any amount received in excess of the judgment and expenses shall be returned
to the judgment debtor as provided by Chapter 21 of the Nevada Revised Statutes.
(Ord. 3829 § 1 (part), 1994)

11.10.270.title: Towing and automobile immobilizers—Authorized
11.10.270.text:
Vehicles may be towed and immobilizing devices may be placed pursuant to the issuance
of a writ of execution by the Sheriff of Clark County, or his authorized designee,
or as otherwise provided in this Chapter.
(Ord. 5334 § 6, 2001: Ord. 3829 § 1 (part), 1994)

11.10.280.title: Automobile immobilizers—Unlawful acts—Exceptions
11.10.280.text:
(A)
Except as otherwise provided in Subsection (B), it is unlawful for any person to deface,
damage, tamper with, open, break, destroy or remove any immobilizing device; impair
the usefulness thereof; leave such a device attached to the immobilized vehicle and
transport it to another location for purposes of depriving the City of its use; or
attempt to do any of those acts.
(B)
The prohibitions described in Subsection (A) do not apply to the acts of any of the
following when acting within the scope of their duties or employment:
(1)
A City officer, employee, or contractor engaged in the parking enforcement function;
(2)
A peace officer; or
(3)
A person engaged in the provision of emergency services.
(Ord. No. 6829, § 4, 2-1-23; Ord. 5334 § 7, 2001: Ord. 3829 § 1 (part), 1994)

11.10.290.title: Parking enforcement services
11.10.290.text:
(A)
The Parking Services Division is authorized to enter into agreements with the owners
or lessees of parking lots or parking structures by which the Division will provide
parking enforcement services related thereto. The Division shall enforce the parking
prohibitions, rules, regulations and limitations that have been agreed upon and established
by means of any such agreements. The prohibitions, rules, regulations and limitations
to be enforced pursuant to any such agreement may include:
(1)
The parking-related provisions of this Title as if the parking lot or structure were
a City parking facility under this Title;
(2)
The parking prohibitions, rules and regulations that the property owner or lessee
has established for the lot or structure; or
(3)
Any combination thereof.
(B)
Unless otherwise specified in an agreement referred to in Subsection (A), the parking
prohibitions, rules, regulations and limitations established by the agreement shall
be deemed to be the City's parking prohibitions, rules, regulations and limitations
for purposes of the enforcement provisions, fines and other remedies of this Title.
In the case of a parking prohibition, rule, regulation or limitation established by
an agreement referred to in Subsection (A) that does not correspond directly to a
prohibition, rule, regulation or limitation described in this Title, the Division,
for enforcement purposes, is authorized to treat the agreed-upon prohibition, rule,
regulation or limitation as if it were the prohibition, rule, regulation or limitation
of this Title that most closely corresponds.
(C)
In order to enforce any parking prohibition, rule, regulation or limitation referred
to in Subsection (A), notice of the applicable prohibition, rule, regulation or limitation
must be provided to those who will be parking vehicles in the lot or structure, whether
by means of signage or otherwise.
(Ord. No. 6703, § 6, 10-2-19; Ord. No. 6645, § 1, 10-3-18)

11.12.010.title: Course of intersection turns—Regulation authority
11.12.010.text:
The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to place markers, buttons, or signs within
or adjacent to intersections indicating the course to be traveled by vehicles turning
at such intersections, and such course to be traveled as so indicated may conform
to or be other than as prescribed by law or ordinance.
(Ord. 283 § 1 (part), 1943: Ord. 170 § 24(6) (part), 1931: prior code § 10-13-1(A)

11.12.020.title: Course of intersection turns—Conformance to indicators
11.12.020.text:
When authorized markers, buttons, or other indications are placed within an intersection
indicating the course to be traveled by vehicles turning thereat, no driver of a vehicle
shall disobey the direction of such indications.
(Ord. 283 § 1 (part), 1943: Ord. 170 § 24(6) (part), 1931: prior code § 10-13-1(B))

11.12.030.title: Turning restriction authority—Signs
11.12.030.text:
The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to determine those intersections at which
drivers of vehicles shall not make a right turn, left turn or U-turn, and shall place
proper signs at such intersections. The making of such turns may be prohibited between
certain hours of any day and permitted at other hours, in which event the same shall
be plainly indicated on the signs or they may be removed when such turns are permitted.
(Prior code § 10-13-2)

11.12.040.title: Reserved
11.12.040.text:
Editor's note—
Ord. No. 6326, § 13, adopted June 18, 2014, repealed § 11.12.040, which pertained
to daytime left turns and derived from prior code § 10-13-3(D); Ord. No. 170, 1931;
Ord. No. 283, 1943; Ord. No. 1278, 1967 and Ord. 1459 § 2, 1979.

11.12.050.title: Turning around—Generally
11.12.050.text:
The driver of any vehicle shall not turn such vehicle so as to proceed in the opposite
direction upon any street in a business district and shall not upon any other street
so turn a vehicle unless such movement can be made in safety and without interfering
with other traffic.
(Ord. 559 § 3, 1953: prior code § 10-13-5)

11.12.060.title: Turning around—Fire stations
11.12.060.text:
No vehicle in front of the driveway, entrance or approaches to a fire station shall
be turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction. No vehicle shall use the driveway
entrance or approaches to a fire station for the purpose of turning so as to proceed
in the opposite direction.
(Prior code § 10-13-6)

11.12.070.title: Entering a through highway
11.12.070.text:
(A)
The driver of any vehicle shall stop as required by this Code at the entrance to a
through highway and shall yield the right-of-way to other vehicles which have entered
the intersection from the through highway or which are approaching so closely on the
through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard.
(B)
Said driver having so yielded may proceed and the drivers of all other vehicles approaching
the intersection on the through highway shall yield right-of-way to the vehicle about
to enter or cross the through highway.
(Prior code § 10-13-11)

11.12.080.title: Following
11.12.080.text:
(A)
The driver of a motor vehicle shall not follow another vehicle more closely than is
reasonable and prudent, having due regard for the speed of such vehicles and the traffic
upon and the condition of the street.
(B)
The driver of any motor truck or vehicle drawing another vehicle when traveling upon
a roadway whenever conditions permit shall leave sufficient space so that an overtaking
vehicle may enter and occupy such space without danger.
(C)
The provisions of this Section shall not apply to funeral processions.
(Prior code § 10-13-19)

11.12.090.title: Passing animals
11.12.090.text:
Every person having control or charge of any motor vehicle upon any public street
and approaching any vehicle drawn by a horse, or any horse upon which any person is
riding, shall operate, manage, and control such motor vehicle in such manner as to
exercise every reasonable precaution to prevent the frightening of any such horse,
and to ensure the safety and protection of any person riding or driving the same,
and if such horse appears frightened, the person in control of such motor vehicle
shall reduce its speed and if requested by a signal or otherwise by the driver or
rider of such horse, shall not proceed further toward such animal unless such movement
is necessary to avoid accident or injury, or until such animal appears to be under
the control of the driver or rider.
(Ord. 170 § 37, 1931: prior code § 10-13-20)

11.12.100.title: Two-way left-turn lanes
11.12.100.text:
(A)
The City Traffic Engineer may designate a two-way left-turn lane on a street or highway
having two or more lanes for through traffic in each direction. A two-way left-turn
lane is a lane near the center of the street or highway set aside for use by vehicles
making left turns in both directions from or into a street or highway.
(B)
Two-way left-turn lanes shall be designated by distinctive roadway markings consisting
of a solid outside yellow line and an inner parallel dashed yellow line on each side
of the lane. The City Traffic Engineer may determine and prescribe standards and specifications
covering length, width and positioning of the distinctive pavement markings.
(C)
A vehicle shall not be driven in a designated two-way left-turn lane except when preparing
for or making a left turn. A left turn shall not be made from any other lane where
a two-way left-turn lane has been designated.
(Ord. 1459 § 2, 1972; Ord. 1351 § 3, 1968: Ord. 1278 § 13, 1967: prior code § 10-13-21)

11.14.010.title: Purpose
11.14.010.text:
It is the purpose of this Chapter to:
(A)
Serve the City's strong public policy against driving while under the influence of
alcohol, controlled substances, chemicals, organic solvents, compounds or any combination
of these;
(B)
Better detect, discourage, prosecute and punish those who would unreasonably risk
driving while under the influence of alcohol, controlled substances, chemicals, organic
solvents, compounds or any combination of these;
(C)
Minimize the number of victims of those who would jeopardize the safety of themselves,
others and their property by undertaking an unreasonable risk of driving while under
the influence of alcohol, controlled substances, chemicals, organic solvents, compounds
or any combination of these;
(D)
Avoid conflict with the Nevada Revised Statutes and the Constitutions of the United
States of America and the State of Nevada. To this end, nothing herein is to be interpreted
to either authorize, license or require what is forbidden in the Nevada Revised Statutes,
the Constitution of the United States of America or the Constitution of the State
of Nevada, or to forbid what has been expressly licensed, authorized or required therein;
and
(E)
Make violations of this Chapter a misdemeanor, unless greater punishment is otherwise
provided by law.
(Ord. 5864 § 2 (part), 2006)

11.14.020.title: Definitions
11.14.020.text:
Except as defined in this Section or in NRS Chapters 453 and 484, all words, terms
or phrases used in this Chapter are to have their common meaning:
"Actual physical control" with respect to a vehicle means having existing or present
bodily restraint, directing influence, domination, or regulation of the vehicle as
evidenced by available inferences and presumptions and the totality of the circumstances,
including but not limited to:
(1)
Where and in what position the person is found in the vehicle;
(2)
Whether the vehicle's engine is running or not;
(3)
Whether the person is awake or asleep;
(4)
If the person is apprehended at night, whether the vehicle's lights are on;
(5)
The location of the vehicle's keys;
(6)
Whether the person was trying to move the vehicle or has moved the vehicle;
(7)
Whether the property on which the vehicle is located is public or private;
(8)
Whether the person must, of necessity, have driven to the location where apprehended;
(9)
Whether the person is the registered owner of the vehicle; and
(10)
Whether there is any injury to the person which corresponds to physical evidence within
or damage to the vehicle.
"Under the influence or the combined influence" means under a degree of influence
that:
(1)
Diminishes a person's mental or physiological functions so that the risk of an accident
is unreasonably increased; or
(2)
In any other manner makes the person incapable of safely driving, as determined from
the totality of the relevant and admissible presumptions, opinions, facts and circumstances.
(Ord. 5864 § 2 (part), 2006)

11.14.030.title: Penalty—Driving under the influence
11.14.030.text:
(A)
Unless a greater penalty is otherwise provided by law, it is a misdemeanor for any
person to:
(1)
Drive or be in actual physical control of a vehicle upon a highway or premises to
which the public has access while under the influence or the combined influence of
an intoxicating liquor, controlled substance, chemical, poison, organic solvent or
compound; or
(2)
In any other manner violate NRS 484.379.
(B)
Unless a greater penalty is otherwise provided by law, a person who is convicted of
a violation of Subsection (A) of this Section shall be sentenced in accordance with
the applicable provisions of NRS 484.3792(1)(a) and 484.3792(1)(b) (misdemeanor criminal
penalty for first and second offenses). In addition, such person:
(1)
Shall be subject to the applicable penalties provided for in NRS 484.3791 (civil penalty),
484.3797 (first-time offender evaluation and treatment for alcohol or drug abuse),
484.37975 (second offender mandatory suspension of motor vehicle registration) and
484.3798 (fee for chemical analysis);
(2)
Shall be subject to the applicable penalties set forth in NRS 484.3667 (double penalty
if committed in a work zone) and 484.3943 (installation and inspection of device to
prevent starting of vehicle by one who has consumed alcohol); and
(3)
May be ordered by the court to complete an available coroner's program designed to
discourage drivers from driving while under the influence or the combined influence
