of intoxicating liquor, controlled substance, chemical, poison, organic solvent or
compound. Such a program and participation therein is especially encouraged where
the offense involves one or more of the following:
(a)
An accident;
(b)
A blood alcohol content of .18 or more;
(c)
The use of controlled or prohibited substances; or
(d)
An offender who is under the age of twenty-six years old; and
(4)
May be ordered to do or refrain from doing any other act the court deems reasonable,
given the nature of the offense and the criminal history of the defendant.
(C)
The provisions of NRS 484.3793 to 484.3947 (miscellaneous provisions regarding the
evaluation and treatment for alcohol or drug abuse), apply to a violation of Subsection
(A) of this Section.
(D)
The provisions of NRS Chapter 484 relating to implied consent, testing for intoxication
and the definitions of "offense," "prior offense" or "second offense" are further
adopted herein and apply to a suspected violation of Subsection (A) of this Section.
(Ord. 5864 § 2 (part), 2006)

11.14.040.title: Penalty—Drinking while driving
11.14.040.text:
(A)
Unless a greater penalty is otherwise involved (and pursued) for conduct described
in Subsection (A) of LVMC 11.14.030 or NRS 484.379, it is a misdemeanor for any person
to knowingly drink a beverage having a detectible amount of alcohol while driving
or in actual physical control of a motor vehicle upon a highway or on premises to
which the public has access.
(B)
A person convicted of a violation of Subsection (A) of this Section:
(1)
Unless the court identifies reasonable grounds for ordering a lesser sentence, shall
be punished for a misdemeanor with:
(a)
A fine of at least three hundred dollars; and
(b)
An order to complete a drinking driver awareness course; and
(2)
May be ordered to do or refrain from doing any other act the court deems reasonable,
given the nature of the offense and the character of the defendant.
(Ord. 5864 § 2 (part), 2006)

11.14.050.title: Open containers—General
11.14.050.text:
Except as otherwise provided in LVMC 11.14.070, it is unlawful for any person, while in a motor vehicle on a highway or upon a premises
to which the public has access, to knowingly possess any bottle, can or other receptacle
containing any detectable amount of alcoholic beverage which has been opened or the
seal broken, or the contents partially removed.
(Ord. 5864 § 2 (part), 2006)

11.14.060.title: Open containers—Storage
11.14.060.text:
(A)
Except as otherwise provided in Subsection (B) of this Section or in LVMC 11.14.070, it is unlawful for the registered owner of any motor vehicle, or the driver if the
registered owner is not then present in the vehicle, to keep in that vehicle, when
it is upon any highway, any bottle, can or other receptacle containing any detectable
amount of alcoholic beverage which has been opened or the seal broken, or the contents
partially removed.
(B)
The prohibition contained in Subsection (A) of this Section does not apply if the
receptacle is kept in the trunk of the vehicle or, if the vehicle is not equipped
with a trunk, in some other area of the vehicle not normally occupied by the driver
or passengers. For purposes of the preceding sentence, a utility compartment or glove
compartment shall be deemed to be within the area normally occupied by the driver
and passengers.
(Ord. 5864 § 2 (part), 2006)

11.14.070.title: Open containers—Exceptions
11.14.070.text:
The provisions of LVMC 11.14.050 and 11.14.060 do not apply to:
(A)
A motor vehicle operated by a common carrier or used to carry passengers for furtherance
of a commercial enterprise;
(B)
A motor vehicle that is operated as part of a duly licensed limousine service and
that has a partition between the driver's seat and the passenger seats; or
(C)
The living quarters of a motor home, camper or recreational vehicle, as those terms
are defined in NRS Chapter 482.
(Ord. 5864 § 2 (part), 2006)

11.14.080.title: Education—Counseling
11.14.080.text:
By committee, the judges of the Las Vegas Municipal Court shall continue to supervise
and monitor the operation of a program of education and counseling on the use and
abuse of alcohol and controlled substances for the benefit of persons who:
(A)
Are convicted in the Municipal Court of violating this Chapter or any ordinance corresponding
to NRS 484.379; or
(B)
Have agreed or acquiesced to such education or counseling pending an anticipated disposition
of a charge of violating this Chapter or any ordinance corresponding to NRS 484.379.
(Ord. 5864 § 2 (part), 2006)

11.16.010.title: Prima facie limits designated—Applicability
11.16.010.text:
The speed of any vehicle upon a street or highway not in excess of the limits specified
in this Chapter or established as authorized in this Title is lawful. The speed of
any vehicle upon a street or highway in excess of any of the limits specified in this
Section or established as authorized in this Title is prima facie unlawful. The prima
facie limits referred to above are as set out in this Chapter and the same shall be
applicable unless changed as authorized in this Title, and if so changed, then only
when the signs have been erected giving notice thereof, in which event the speed designated
on the sign shall be prima facie limit.
(Ord. 1100 § 1 (part), 1947: Ord. 805 § 1 (part), 1959: Ord. 756 § 1 (part), 1958:
Ord. 750 § 1 (part), 1957: Ord. 706 § 1, 1956: Ord. 559 § 1, 1953: Ord. 508 § 1, 1952:
Ord. 467 § 2, 1951: Ord. 351 § 3, 1948: Ord. 332 § 3, 1947: Ord. 274 § 4, 1942: Ord.
170 § 36, 1931: prior code § 10-25-2 (part))

11.16.020.title: School grounds and vicinity
11.16.020.text:
The prima facie speed limit shall be fifteen miles per hour when in a school zone
during school hours on days on which such school is in session and upon the grounds
or parking lots thereof at all times. Such prima facie limit also shall apply when
in any school zone which is adjacent to the grounds of any school that are not separated
from the street or highway by a fence, gate or any other physical barrier, while such
grounds are in use by children.
(Ord. 3212 § 3, 1986: Ord. 1670 § 1 (part), 1973: Ord. 1100 § 1 (part), 1964: Ord.
805 § 1 (part), 1959: Ord. 756 § 1 (part), 1958: Ord. 750 § 1 (part), 1957: prior
code § 10-25-2(A)(1))

11.16.030.title: Rail crossings at grade
11.16.030.text:
The prima facie speed limit shall be fifteen miles per hour when traversing a grade
crossing of a steam, electric or any other motor railway, if during the last one hundred
feet of the approach to such crossing the driver does not have a clear and unobstructed
view of such crossing and of any traffic on such railway for a distance of four hundred
feet in both directions along such railway. This Section shall not apply in the case
of any railway grade crossing where a human flagman is on duty or clearly visible
electrical or mechanical railway crossing signal device is installed but does not
then indicate the immediate approach of a railway train or car.
(Ord. 1670 § 1 (part), 1973: Ord. 1100 § 1 (part), 1964: Ord. 805 § 1 (part), 1959:
Ord. 756 § 1 (part), 1958: Ord. 750 § 1 (part), 1957: prior code § 10-25-2(A)(2))

11.16.040.title: Intersections
11.16.040.text:
The prima facie speed limit shall be fifteen miles per hour when traversing any intersection
or street or highway if during the last one hundred feet of his approach to such intersection
the driver does not have a clear and unobstructed view of such intersection and of
any traffic upon all of the streets or highways entering such intersection for a distance
of one hundred feet along all such streets or highways, except on a through street
or highway or at a traffic-controlled intersection.
(Ord. 1670 § 1 (part), 1973: Ord. 1100 § 1 (part), 1964: Ord. 805 § 1 (part), 1959:
Ord. 756 § 1 (part), 1958: Ord. 750 § 1 (part), 1957: prior code § 10-25-2(A)(3))

11.16.050.title: City parks and facilities
11.16.050.text:
The prima facie speed limit shall be fifteen miles per hour when driving within the
grounds of a municipally owned or operated park or facility, provided after a traffic
study the City Traffic Engineer determines that such a prima facie speed is necessary.
(Ord. 1670 § 1 (part), 1973: prior code § 10-25-2(A)(4))

11.16.060.title: Unposted streets and highways
11.16.060.text:
The prima facie speed limit is twenty-five miles per hour on all streets and highways
unless a different speed limit is posted as set forth in this Title.
(Ord. 1100 § 1 (part), 1964: Ord. 805 § 1 (part), 1959: Ord. 756 § 1 (part), 1958:
Ord. 750 § 1 (part), 1957: prior code § 10-25-2(B))

11.16.070.title: Posted streets and highways—School crossings
11.16.070.text:
When signs are erected giving notice thereof, the prima facie speed limit upon those
streets or highways or portions thereof described in Schedule 25-I shall be thirty
miles per hour, Schedule 25-II shall be thirty-five miles per hour, Schedule 25-III
shall be forty miles per hour, Schedule 25-IV shall be forty-five miles per hour,
Schedule 25-V shall be fifty miles per hour, Schedule 25-VI shall be fifty-five miles
per hour, Schedule 25-VIII shall be sixty miles per hour and Schedule 25-IX shall
be sixty-five miles per hour. Copies of said Schedules shall be maintained for public
inspection in the office of the City Clerk and the City Traffic Engineer and may be
amended from time to time by resolution of the City Council; provided, however, that
when traffic engineering studies indicate that through intersections of any street
or highway, or any other point along such street or highway, a speed in excess of
twenty-five miles per hour would be unsafe due to the number of children crossing
such street or highway at such intersection or other point on their way to or from
school, the City Traffic Engineer shall designate such intersection as a "school crossing,"
and when signs are erected giving notice thereof, the prima facie speed limit through
such "school crossing" and for a distance of two hundred feet on either side thereof
shall be twenty-five miles per hour while children are going to or leaving school
during school hours on days on which schools are in session.
(Ord. 3990 § 4, 1996: Ord. 3202 § 1, 1985: Ord. 1589 § 14, 1972: Ord. 1534 § 8, 1971;
Ord. 1423 § 5, 1969; Ord. 1384 §§ 4, 5, 1969: Ord. 1339 § 5, 1968; Ord. 1293 § 7,
1967; Ord. 1180 § 1, 1965; Ord. 1100 § 1 (part), 1964; Ord. 1038 § 1 (part), 1963;
Ord. 805 § 1 (part), 1959: Ord. 756 § 1 (part), 1958: Ord. 750 § 1 (part), 1957: prior
code § 10-25-2(C) 1967; Ord. 1180 § 1, 1965; Ord. 1100 § 1 (part), 1964; Ord. 1038
§ 1 (part), 1963; Ord. 805 § 1 (part), 1959: Ord. 756 § 1 (part), 1958: Ord. 750 §
1 (part), 1957: prior code § 10-25-2(C))

11.16.080.title: Variance by traffic signal regulation
11.16.080.text:
The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to regulate the timing of traffic signals
so as to permit the movement of traffic in an orderly and safe manner at speeds slightly
at variance from the speeds otherwise applicable within the district or at intersections
and shall erect appropriate signs giving notice thereof.
(Prior code § 10-25-3)

11.16.090.title: Speed contests
11.16.090.text:
(A)
No person shall engage in any motor vehicle speed contest or exhibition of power or
speed on a highway and no person shall aid or abet in any such motor vehicle speed
contest or exhibition upon any highway.
(B)
No person shall, for the purpose of facilitating or aiding or as an incident to any
motor vehicle speed contest upon a highway, in any manner obstruct or place any barricade
or obstruction or assist or participate in placing any such barricade or obstruction
upon any highway.
(Ord. 1278 § 27, 1967; prior code § 10-25-5)

11.16.100.title: Construction zones
11.16.100.text:
When so required in order to protect the public health, safety and welfare, the City
Traffic Engineer shall have the authority to designate a temporary speed limit or
to redirect the normal flow of traffic, or both, in that portion of a public street
designated by the City Traffic Engineer as a construction zone.
(Ord. 3157 § 2, 1985)

11.16.110.title: Trucks traveling on streets and highways
11.16.110.text:
When signs are erected giving notice thereof, the prima facie speed limit for vehicles
weighing more than eight thousand pounds unladen weight upon those streets or highways
or portions thereof described in Schedule 25-VII shall be twenty-five miles per hour.
Copies of said schedule shall be maintained for public inspection in the office of
the City Clerk and the City Traffic Engineer and may be amended from time to time
by resolution of the City Council; provided, however that no street or highway or
portion proposed for inclusion in Schedule 25-VII shall have been designated as a
truck route and described in Schedule 29-II.
(Ord. 3691 § 1, 1992)

11.18.010.title: Crosswalk and safety zone establishment
11.18.010.text:
The City Traffic Engineer is authorized:
(A)
To designate and maintain, by appropriate devices, marks or lines upon the surface
of the roadway, crosswalks at intersections where in his opinion there is particular
danger to pedestrians crossing the roadway, and at such other places as he may deem
necessary;
(B)
To establish safety zones of such kind and character and at such places as he may
deem necessary for the protection of pedestrians.
(Ord. 170 § 11, 1931: prior code § 10-12-1)

11.18.020.title: School crossings
11.18.020.text:
The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to mark and maintain with yellow paint or
road buttons crosswalks approximately twelve feet in width at intersections in the
vicinity of schools where in the opinion of the City Traffic Engineer crossing the
roadway by schoolchildren is unsafe. The City Traffic Engineer, if necessary, is further
authorized to mark and maintain with a distinguishing color or road buttons upon the
pavement or by signs erected along the curb in a conspicuous manner, the words "School-Xing,"
not less than one hundred feet in advance of each crosswalk established, and it shall
be unlawful for the operator of any vehicle to drive into a crosswalk where there
is displayed a sign with the words "School-Xing," when there is in the crosswalk upon
the side of the roadway on which said vehicle is coming any person attempting to cross
the street.
(Ord. 2203 § 21, 1981: Ord. 1278 § 10, 1967: Ord. 170 § 9, 1931: prior code § 10-12-2)
Cross reference—
For other provisions on speed at school crossings, see Ch. 11.16 of this Code.

11.18.030.title: Traffic lanes
11.18.030.text:
(A)
The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to mark traffic lanes upon the roadway of
any street or highway where a regular alignment of traffic is necessary.
(B)
Where such traffic lanes have been marked, it shall be unlawful for the operator of
any vehicle to fail or refuse to keep such vehicle within the boundaries of any such
lane except when lawfully passing another vehicle or preparatory to making a lawful
turning movement.
(Prior code § 10-12-3)

11.20.010.title: Through streets
11.20.010.text:
Those streets or parts of streets described as planned streets and highways within
the map and schedule adopted pursuant to LVMC 13.12.020, as that map and schedule
may be amended from time to time, are declared to be through streets for the purpose
of this Chapter.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 14, 6-18-14; Ord. 3990 § 5, 1996: Ord. 1589 § 3, 1972: Ord. 1534
§ 1, 1971; Ord. 1278 § 16, 1967; Ord. 1169 § 2, 1965; Ord. 274 § 3, 1942: Ord. 170
§ 17, 1931: prior code § 10-14-1)

11.20.020.title: Stop signs—Erection required where
11.20.020.text:
Whenever any ordinance of this City designates and describes a through street, it
shall be the duty of the City Traffic Engineer to place and maintain a stop sign on
each and every street intersecting such through street or intersecting that portion
thereof described and designated as such by any ordinance of this City unless traffic
at any such intersection is controlled at all times by traffic-control signals; provided,
however, that at the intersection of two such through streets or at the intersection
of a through street and a heavy traffic street not so designated, stop signs shall
be erected at the approaches of either of said streets as may be determined by the
City Traffic Engineer upon the basis of an engineering and traffic study.
(Prior code § 10-14-2)

11.20.030.title: Reserved
11.20.030.text:
Editor's note—
Ord. No. 6326, § 15, adopted June 18, 2014, repealed § 11.20.030, which pertained
to stop signs—content—luminosity and derived from prior code § 10-14-4.

11.20.040.title: Stop signs—Compliance
11.20.040.text:
When stop signs are erected as herein authorized at or near the entrance to any intersection,
every driver of a vehicle approaching such a stop sign shall stop such vehicle before
entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, in the event there
is no crosswalk, shall stop at a clearly marked stop line, but if none, then at a
point at the entrance to the intersecting street or highway.
(Ord. 1459 § 6, 1970: Ord. 1278 § 14, 1967: prior code § 10-14-5)

11.20.050.title: Stop intersections
11.20.050.text:
(A)
The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to determine and designate intersections where
particular hazards exist upon other than through streets and to determine whether
vehicles shall stop at one or more entrances to any such stop intersection, and shall
erect a stop sign at every such place where a stop is required.
(B)
Schedule 14-II, a copy of which is to be maintained for public inspection in the offices
of the City Clerk and the City Traffic Engineer, shall list those stop intersections
designated pursuant to Subsection (A) of this Section and such other stop intersections
as may be added to said Schedule by written finding of the City Traffic Engineer.
(Ord. 3990 § 5, 1996: Ord. 1589 § 4, 1972: Ord. 1534 § 2, 1971; Ord. 1459 § 5, 1970:
Ord. 1423 § 1, 1969; Ord. 1384 § 1, 1969; Ord. 1339 § 1, 1968; Ord. 1293 § 2, 1967;
Ord. 1278 § 17, 1967: prior code § 10-14-3)

11.20.060.title: Crossing sidewalks—Entering roadways
11.20.060.text:
The driver of a vehicle within a business or residence district emerging or entering
an alley, driveway or building shall stop such vehicle immediately prior to driving
onto a sidewalk or onto the sidewalk area extending across any alleyway or driveway,
yielding the right-of-way to any pedestrian as may be necessary to avoid collision,
and upon entering the roadway shall yield the right-of-way to all vehicles approaching
on said roadway.
(Ord. 1278 § 15, 1967: Ord. 170 § 15, 1931: prior code § 10-14-7)

11.20.070.title: Obstructing intersection or crosswalk
11.20.070.text:
No driver shall enter an intersection or a marked crosswalk unless there is sufficient
space on the other side of the intersection or crosswalk to accommodate the vehicle
he is operating without obstructing the passage of other vehicles or pedestrians,
notwithstanding any traffic-control signal indication to proceed.
(Prior code § 10-14-8)

11.22.010.title: Full time and attention
11.22.010.text:
A person shall, when operating a vehicle, give his full time and attention to the
operation of the vehicle.
(Ord. 1308 § 1, 1968: prior code § 10-15-22)

11.22.020.title: Carelessness or imprudence
11.22.020.text:
It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate a vehicle of any kind or character
in a careless or imprudent manner on any highway in the City.
(Ord. 2034 § 1, 1979: prior code § 10-15-24)

11.22.030.title: Shutdown before leaving
11.22.030.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person to leave unattended upon any street or other public
place any automobile or other motor vehicle while any part of its machinery is running
or in motion.
(Ord. 170 § 48, 1931: prior code § 10-19-4)

11.22.040.title: Sidewalk area violation
11.22.040.text:
The driver of a vehicle shall not drive within any sidewalk area except at a permanent
or temporary driveway or permit such vehicle to stand thereon.
(Ord. 170 § 22, 1931: prior code § 10-15-7)

11.22.050.title: Controlled-access roadways
11.22.050.text:
No person shall drive a vehicle onto or from any controlled-access roadway except
at such entrances and exits as are established by public authority.
(Prior code § 10-15-11)

11.22.055.title: Engine compression brakes
11.22.055.text:
It is unlawful for any person to use engine compression brakes or any similar braking
system while operating a vehicle, other than an emergency vehicle, within the City,
unless the vehicle is equipped with an operational muffler and exhaust system which
complies with Federal and state noise emission standards.
(Ord. 5017 § 1, 1997: Ord. 5002 § 1, 1997)

11.22.060.title: Quiet zones
11.22.060.text:
The City Council may, by resolution, declare and designate any street or alley within
two hundred feet of a hospital, church, courthouse, or sick chamber a zone of quiet,
and upon and in this zone, when so declared and designated, there shall be no ringing
of bells, sounding of gongs or whistles, unnecessary noises or itinerant music.
(Ord. 170 § 32, 1931: prior code § 10-15-15)

11.22.070.title: Safety zone violation
11.22.070.text:
No vehicle shall at any time be driven through or within a safety zone.
(Ord. 170 § 7, 1931: prior code § 10-15-19)

11.22.080.title: Front-seat passenger limit
11.22.080.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person owning, driving or permitting the driving of any
automobile or other motor-propelled vehicle with more than three persons occupying
the front seat of a vehicle.
(Prior code § 10-15-14)

11.22.090.title: Door opening
11.22.090.text:
No person shall open the door of a motor vehicle on the side available to moving traffic
unless and until it is reasonably safe to do so, nor shall any person leave a door
open upon the side of a vehicle available to moving traffic for a period of time longer
than necessary to load or unload passengers.
(Prior code § 10-15-17)

11.22.100.title: New pavement or closed street
11.22.100.text:
No person shall ride or drive any horse or vehicle over or across any pavement newly
laid or repaired across or around which there has been placed a barrier, or at or
near which there is a person or a sign warning persons against riding or driving over
such pavement, or a sign stating that the highway is closed. The provisions of this
Section shall not apply to the employees actually engaged in the paving or repair
of such pavement.
(Ord. 170 § 73, 1931: prior code § 10-15-16)

11.22.110.title: Railroad obstruction of streets
11.22.110.text:
It shall be unlawful for the directing officer or the operator of any railroad train
to direct the operation of or to operate the same in such a manner as to prevent the
use of any street for the purposes of travel for a period of time longer than five
minutes, except that this provision shall not apply to trains or cars in motion other
than those engaged in switching.
(Ord. 170 § 93, 1931: prior code § 10-15-20)

11.22.120.title: Nonmotorized-traffic street closures
11.22.120.text:
(A)
The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to determine and designate those heavily traveled
streets upon which shall be prohibited the use of the roadway by motor-driven cycles,
bicycles, horse-drawn vehicles or other nonmotorized traffic and shall erect appropriate
signs giving notice thereof.
(B)
When signs are erected giving notice thereof, no person shall disobey the restriction
stated on such signs.
(Prior code § 10-19-3)

11.22.130.title: Wheeled toys on streets and sidewalks
11.22.130.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person to ride or use a coaster, roller skates, scooter,
skateboard, toy vehicle or similar device:
(A)
On any roadway except while crossing a street at a crosswalk, and, when any such device
is so crossing, it shall be granted all of the rights and shall be subject to all
of the duties applicable to pedestrians;
(B)
On the sidewalks of Fremont Street between Main Street and Seventh Street which, because
of the high volume of pedestrian traffic normally present, shall be posted with signs
indicating that the use of these devices on the sidewalk is prohibited;
(C)
On any other public property when signs have been erected at the entrances to, or
displayed prominently on, the property prohibiting the use of coasters, roller skates,
scooters, skateboards, toy vehicles or similar devices on such property; or
(D)
In any other place in the City in such a manner as to be dangerous to persons or property.
(Ord. 3412 § 4, 1989: Ord. 2038 § 2, 1979: Ord. 170 § 75, 1931: prior code § 10-7-5)

11.22.135.title: Wheeled toys on posted private property
11.22.135.text:
Any person who rides or uses a coaster, roller skates, scooter, skateboard, toy vehicle
or similar device on any private property to which the public is invited after signs
have been erected at the entrances to, or displayed prominently on, the property prohibiting
the use of coasters, roller skates, scooters, skateboards, toy vehicles or similar
devices shall be deemed to have committed a trespass.
(Ord. 3412 § 3, 1989)

11.22.137.title: Wheeled toys—Definitions
11.22.137.text:
As used in this Chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, the following terms
shall have the meanings that are ascribed to them as follows:
(A)
"Coaster" means a nonmotorized wheeled vehicle which, after being propelled by either
human or mechanical force of any kind, becomes by momentum or gravity a free-moving
vehicle without the need of further application of propulsive power; and includes
a child's wagon.
(B)
"Roller skate" means tandem sets of wheels mounted on a metal frame that can be fitted
to the sole of a shoe, or a shoe mounted on tandem sets of wheels; and used for skating
over flat surfaces.
(C)
"Scooter" means a foot-propelled vehicle consisting of a platform of metal, plastic,
wood or other type of composition or combinations thereof, mounted on or between one
set or tandem sets of wheels, with an upright steering handle attached to the front
of the platform or the front wheel or wheels.
(D)
"Skateboard" means a foot-propelled vehicle consisting of a platform of metal, plastic,
wood or other type of composition or combinations thereof, mounted on tandem sets
of wheels.
(Ord. 3412 § 2, 1989)

11.22.140.title: Aggregates and other loose loads
11.22.140.text:
(A)
It is unlawful for any person to operate, on any public road, street or highway within
the City, any vehicle:
(1)
Unless such vehicle is constructed, covered or loaded in such a manner as to prevent
its contents or load, other than clear water or other substance that may be sprinkled
on the roadway for the purpose of cleaning the same, from dropping, sifting, leaking,
blowing, spilling or otherwise escaping therefrom;
(2)
That is used to transport any aggregate material, whether the vehicle is loaded or
empty at the time, unless:
(a)
Such material is carried in the cargo area of the vehicle, with the tailgate thereof
in the closed position, and does not extend above the topmost edge of the cargo area,
(b)
The cargo area is equipped with a tailgate, is completely and securely covered and
does not contain any holes, cracks or openings through which such material may escape,
regardless of the degree to which the vehicle is loaded, and
(c)
The vehicle is equipped with shed boards;
(3)
That is loaded with garbage, rubbish or dirt or anything that is being transported
to either an approved or unapproved dumping area unless the load is completely covered
in a manner that will prevent the load, or any part thereof, from spilling or falling
from the vehicle; provided, however, that this paragraph does not prohibit a garbage
vehicle from being without a cover while it is in the process of acquiring its load.
(B)
For the purpose of this Section, the terms:
(1)
"Aggregate material" means rock fragments, pebbles, sand, gravel, cobbles, crushed
base, asphalt and other similar materials;
(2)
"Garbage," "rubbish" and "dirt" shall have the meanings that are ascribed to them
in LVMC 9.08.010;
(3)
"Shed boards" means a device that is designed to prevent aggregate material from being
deposited on the body of the vehicle during the loading process.
(Ord. 3310 §§ 2, 3, 1987)

11.22.150.title: Operation of vehicle within one hundred feet of an ice cream truck
11.22.150.text:
Within one hundred feet of an ice cream truck that has engaged the safety equipment
described in Subsection (C) of Section 6.47.100, it is unlawful to operate a vehicle as follows:
(A)
At a speed greater than is prudent when children are present in the area; or
(B)
In excess of fifteen miles per hour, in any event.
(Ord. 5040 § 15, 1997)

11.22.160.title: Test driving on residential streets—Prohibited
11.22.160.text:
(A)
Except as otherwise provided in this Section, it is unlawful for:
(1)
A customer or potential customer of a motor vehicle dealership to test-drive a vehicle
on a residential street;
(2)
An employee of a motor vehicle dealership to allow a customer or potential customer
of the dealership to test-drive a vehicle on a residential street; or
(3)
A principal or employee of an auto repair facility to test-drive a customer's vehicle
on a residential street.
(B)
The prohibitions contained in Subsection (A) of this Section do not apply to the test-driving
of a vehicle on a residential street if the test-driving of vehicles on that particular
street by customers or potential customers of a motor vehicle dealership, or by principals
or employees of an auto repair facility, has been approved by the Department of Community
Development in connection with the Department's approval of a test-driving plan submitted
by that dealership or auto repair facility.
(C)
For purposes of this Section:
(1)
"Residential street" means a street within a residential area that has a right-of-way
width of less than eighty feet.
(2)
"Test-drive a vehicle," with respect to a customer, potential customer, or employee
of a motor vehicle dealership, means to test-drive a vehicle that is being offered
for sale or lease by that dealership.
(3)
"Test-drive a vehicle," with respect to a principal or employee of an auto repair
facility, means to test-drive a customer vehicle.
(4)
"Test-drive a vehicle on a residential street" does not include the necessary use
of a residential street to gain access to, or return to, a street that is not a residential
street, provided that travel on the residential street for that limited purpose does
not exceed a speed of fifteen miles per hour.
(D)
A dealership whose employees allow customers or potential customers of the dealership
to test-drive vehicles on a residential street in violation of this Section, or in
violation of an approved test-driving plan, is subject to disciplinary action against
the dealership's business license, as well as action to revoke any associated Special
Use Permit or Site Development Plan.
(E)
An auto repair facility whose principals or employees test-drive vehicles on a residential
street in violation of this Section, or in violation of an approved test-driving plan,
is subject to disciplinary action against the facility's business license, as well
as action to revoke any associated Special Use Permit or Site Development Plan.
(Ord. No. 6816, § 111, 8-17-22; Ord. No. 6316, § 1, 5-7-14; Ord. 5665 § 1, 2004)

11.24.010.title: Unlawful activities on public thoroughfares, City-owned parking lots or parking garages
11.24.010.text:
(A)
It is unlawful to do any of the following upon any highway, street or other public
thoroughfare within the City:
(1)
Abandon a vehicle;
(2)
Park a vehicle:
(a)
Concerning which there is no valid current registration from the Nevada Department
of Motor Vehicles or another state or nation; or
(b)
Which does not display thereon a valid current license plate bearing a current and
valid registration sticker (if required), temporary placard, or moving permit issued
for that vehicle by the Nevada Department of Motor Vehicles or by another state or
nation;
(3)
Allow a vehicle to remain positioned:
(a)
On the same highway, street or other public right-of-way adjacent to the same parcel
or property line for more than seventy-two consecutive hours;
(b)
On the same highway, street or other public right-of-way adjacent to the same parcel
or property line for more than seventy-two hours of any consecutive ninety-six-hour
period;
(c)
On adjoining highways, streets or other public rights-of-way adjacent to the same
parcel or property line for more than seventy-two hours of any consecutive ninety-six-hour
period;
(4)
Park a vehicle and cause it to be suspended on jacks or any other lifting device,
except as and to the extent reasonably necessary to change a tire or effect an immediate
repair; or
(5)
Park a vehicle and engage in mechanical repairs thereon, except as and to the extent
reasonably necessary to effect an immediate emergency repair.
(B)
It is unlawful to do any of the following upon or within any City parking facility
within the City:
(1)
Abandon a vehicle;
(2)
Park a vehicle:
(a)
Concerning which there is no valid current registration from the Nevada Department
of Motor Vehicles or another state or nation; or
(b)
Which does not display thereon a valid current license plate bearing a current and
valid registration sticker (if required), temporary placard, or moving permit issued
for that vehicle by the Nevada Department of Motor Vehicles or by another state or
nation;
(3)
Park a vehicle and cause it to be suspended on jacks or any other lifting device,
except as and to the extent reasonably necessary to change a tire or effect an immediate
repair; or
(4)
Park a vehicle and engage in mechanical repairs thereon, except as and to the extent
reasonably necessary to effect an immediate emergency repair.
(Ord. No. 6703, § 7, 10-2-19; Ord. No. 6326, § 16, 6-18-14; Ord. No. 6149, § 3, 5-4-11;
Ord. 5095 § 15, 1998: Ord. 3484 § 10, 1990: Ord. 854 § 1(a), 1960: prior code § 10-15-21(A))

11.24.020.title: Public or private property
11.24.020.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person to:
(A)
Abandon a vehicle upon public or private property within the City without the consent
of the owner or person in control or management of the public or private property;
or
(B)
Leave a vehicle in a parking space in the parking lot of a multifamily residential
development for more than seven consecutive days if the vehicle:
(1)
Is in an obviously mechanically inoperable condition; and
(2)
Is visible from public property, including a street or alley.
(Ord. 5802 § 1, 2005: Ord. 5634 § 2, 2003: Ord. 2203 § 23 (part), 1981: Ord. 854 §
1(b), 1960: prior code § 10-15-21(B)(part))

11.24.030.title: Notice—Removal deadline
11.24.030.text:
Any officer of the Metropolitan Police Department, the Department of Public Safety,
or the unit of the Department of Economic and Urban Development assigned to parking
enforcement who has reasonable grounds to believe that a vehicle has been abandoned
or has been parked in violation of LVMC 11.24.010 may affix a Notice of Infraction to the vehicle. An authorized employee of the code
enforcement authority who has reasonable grounds to believe that a vehicle has been
abandoned or parked on private property in violation of LVMC 11.24.020 may affix a Notice of Infraction to the vehicle. The officer or employee may also
affix a warning notice advising that the vehicle is subject to tow because it is in
violation, and may mark one or more tires of the vehicle to indicate the current date.
Subject to the provisions of NRS Chapters 484B and 487, any such officer or employee
is authorized to immediately remove or have such vehicle removed from any street,
highway, public thoroughfare, public or private property, for the purpose of storage
or disposition, to any garage within the City as designated by the officer or employee
if the vehicle:
(A)
Has not been removed within seventy-two hours after the warning notice is affixed.
(B)
Has been parked for more than twenty-four hours while in violation of a parking prohibition,
restriction or time limitation.
(C)
Is parked at a location or in a manner so as to constitute a traffic hazard or an
obstruction to the normal movement of traffic or pedestrians.
(D)
Is parked within a fire lane, whether on public or private property, which has been
designated and posted as such pursuant to the City's Fire Code.
(E)
Is parked within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant located on either public or private
property, whether or not:
(1)
A sign has been posted to indicate "No Parking"; or
(2)
The adjacent curb or road surface has been painted red.
(F)
Has obviously been abandoned upon a street, highway, public thoroughfare or on public
property.
(G)
Has been abandoned or parked in violation of LVMC 11.24.020, and has not been removed within seventy-two hours after a warning notice has been
affixed.
(H)
Is parked upon a street, highway, public thoroughfare or public property and is so
disabled or in such a state of disrepair that its normal operation is impossible or
impractical.
(I)
Is parked upon a street, highway, public thoroughfare or public property and:
(1)
Concerning which there is no valid current registration from the Nevada Department
of Motor Vehicles or another state or nation; or
(2)
Does not display thereon a valid current license plate, temporary placard, or moving
permit issued for that vehicle by the Nevada Department of Motor Vehicles or by another
state or nation;
(J)
Is parked on private property to which the public has access and has been damaged
or is in such a state of disrepair as to constitute an imminent hazard to the public.
(Ord. No. 6518, § 18, 4-6-16; Ord. No. 6326, § 17, 6-18-14; Ord. No. 6184, § 8, 3-21-12;
Ord. No. 6149, § 4, 5-4-11; Ord. 5802 § 2, 2005: Ord. 5634 § 3, 2003: Ord. 5095 §
16, 1998: Ord. 3484 § 11, 1990: Ord. 2203 § 23 (part), 1981: Ord. 854 § 2, 1960: prior
code § 10-15-21(B)(part))

11.24.040.title: Intent to avoid time limitations
11.24.040.text:
For purposes of the twenty-four-hour and seventy-two-hour limitations contained in
LVMC 11.24.010 and 11.24.030, vehicles which are moved short distances with the intent of avoiding
the time limitations will be considered in violation and are subject to citation and
tow.
(Ord. 5095 § 18, 1998)

11.24.050.title: Towing at owner's expense
11.24.050.text:
The towing of any vehicle in accordance with the provisions of LVMC 11.24.030 shall be at the expense of the owner of the vehicle.
(Ord. 5095 § 19, 1998)

11.26.010.title: Permission to use land
11.26.010.text:
No person shall drive a motor vehicle on lands belonging to or occupied by another
without having in his immediate possession and, upon request of a peace officer displaying,
written permission from the owner of such lands, his agent, or the person in lawful
possession thereof, but this Section shall not apply to a person having lawful business
with the owner.
(Ord. 1587 § 1 (part), 1972: prior code § 10-15-23(A))

11.26.020.title: Exempt locations
11.26.020.text:
This Chapter shall not apply on public or private lands expressly set apart for the
use of motor vehicles by or with permission of the owner of such lands pursuant to
any zoning permit or other permit or licensing procedure authorized by law. This Chapter
shall not apply upon any public highway, street, road or alley.
(Ord. 1587 § 1 (part), 1972: prior code § 10-15-23(B))

11.26.030.title: Exempt vehicles
11.26.030.text:
This Chapter shall not apply to the use of farm vehicles for agricultural purposes,
vehicles being used for grading or construction purposes, vehicles being used for
governmental purposes, or golf carts being used on golf courses.
(Ord. 1587 § 1 (part), 1972: prior code § 10-15-23(C))

11.26.040.title: Government property
11.26.040.text:
Nothing in this Chapter shall be deemed to interfere with the right of any government
agency to regulate, prohibit or permit the use of motor vehicles on property owned
by it or under its control and under its jurisdiction, nor to permit or authorize
any trespass or nuisance.
(Ord. 1587 § 1 (part), 1972: prior code § 10-15-23(D))

11.27.010.title: Motorized vehicles prohibited—Exceptions
11.27.010.text:
(A)
Except as otherwise provided in Subsection (B), it is unlawful to operate a motorized
vehicle upon or within a right-of-way that:
(1)
Has been designated on an official trails plan as an equestrian trail, multi-use trail,
or other trail not intended for use by motorized vehicles;
(2)
Has been dedicated to the City for use as such a trail; and
(3)
Has been posted with appropriate signs to indicate that motorized vehicles are prohibited.
(B)
The provisions of Subsection (A) do not apply to:
(1)
An emergency vehicle;
(2)
Any vehicle that is being used in connection with maintenance of the right-of-way;
or
(3)
Any motorized wheelchair or other device that is designed for and used by a mobility-impaired
person.
(Ord. 5745 § 2, 2004)

11.28.010.title: Unsafe-vehicle operation—Unsafe loads
11.28.010.text:
It is unlawful to operate any vehicle or combination of vehicles which is in an unsafe
condition, which is not equipped as required by this Title, or which is not safely
loaded.
(Prior code § 10-20-41)

11.28.020.title: High beam intensity
11.28.020.text:
There shall be an uppermost distribution of light, or composite beam, so aimed and
of such intensity as to reveal persons and vehicles at a distance of at least three
hundred feet ahead for all conditions of loading. The maximum intensity of this uppermost
distribution of light or composite beam one degree of arc or more above the horizontal
level of the lamps when the vehicle is not loaded shall not exceed eight thousand
apparent candlepower, and at no other point of the distribution of light or composite
beam shall there be an intensity of more than seventy-five thousand apparent candlepower.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 103: prior code § 10-20-18)

11.28.030.title: Drip or leakage prevention
11.28.030.text:
Every motor vehicle or any machinery or apparatus using electricity, gasoline or any
product of petroleum for its motor power shall have attached thereto a suitable device
or devices for the purpose of preventing deposits from leaking or dripping being made
upon the pavements or public streets.
(Ord. 170 § 49, 1931: prior code § 10-20-21)

11.28.040.title: Draining oils on streets
11.28.040.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person operating any automobile or any machinery or apparatus
using electricity, or gasoline or other product of petroleum for its motor power,
to drain such petroleum products from the crank or gear case, or from any other part
of the machinery, upon any street.
(Ord. 170 § 50, 1931: prior code § 10-20-22)

11.28.050.title: Horn requirements
11.28.050.text:
Any person driving a motor vehicle within the City shall, when reasonably necessary
to ensure safe operation, give audible warning with his horn, but shall not otherwise
use such horn within the City limits. Every automobile when operated upon a roadway
within the City shall be equipped with a horn in good working order and capable of
emitting sound audible under normal conditions from a distance of not less than two
hundred feet, but no horn or other warning device shall emit an unnecessary loud or
harsh sound or a whistle.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 115 (part): prior code § 10-20-23 (part))
Note—
Prior history: Ord. 170 § 38.

11.28.060.title: Sirens—Theft alarms
11.28.060.text:
No vehicle shall be equipped with nor shall any person use upon a vehicle any siren,
whistle, or bell, except as otherwise permitted in this Section. It is permissible,
but not required, that any commercial vehicle be equipped with a theft alarm signal
device which is so arranged that it cannot be used by the driver as an ordinary warning
signal. Any authorized emergency vehicle may be equipped with a siren, whistle or
bell capable of emitting sound audible under normal conditions from a distance of
not less than five hundred feet, but such siren shall not be used except when such
vehicle is operated in response to an emergency call or in the immediate pursuit of
an actual or suspected violator of the law, in which said latter events the driver
of such vehicle shall sound such sirens when necessary to warn pedestrians and other
drivers of the approach thereof.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 115 (part): prior code § 10-20-23 (part))
Note—
Prior history: Ord. 170 § 39.

11.28.070.title: Windshield required when
11.28.070.text:
Every passenger vehicle other than a motorcycle, and every motor truck or truck tractor,
and every fire truck, fire engine or other fire apparatus, whether publicly or privately
owned, shall be equipped with an adequate windshield.
(Prior code § 10-20-31(A))

11.28.080.title: Safety glass required
11.28.080.text:
(A)
No person shall sell or operate any motor vehicle, except a motorcycle, manufactured
after January 1, 1936, unless it is equipped with safety glass of a type approved
by the Metropolitan Police Department, wherever glass or glazing materials are used
in partitions, doors, windows, windshields, rear windows or wind deflectors.
(B)
"Safety glass" is any type of glass or glazing material so manufactured, fabricated,
treated, or combined with other materials as to reduce, in comparison with ordinary
sheet glass or plate glass, the likelihood of injury to persons by objects from external
sources or by glass or glazing material when the same is cracked or broken.
(C)
The Metropolitan Police Department shall establish specifications or requirements
for approved safety glass which shall not be lower in standard than those specifications
or requirements for safety glass established by the American Standards Association
for glazing in motor vehicles as of September 22, 1951, and shall maintain a list
of approved types of safety glass.
(Prior code § 10-20-32(A—C))

11.28.090.title: Defective windshield or rear window
11.28.090.text:
It is unlawful to operate any motor vehicle upon a highway when the windshield or
rear window is in such a defective condition as to impair the driver's vision either
to the front or rear. In the event any windshield or rear window fails to comply with
this Chapter, the officer making the inspection shall direct the driver to make the
windshield and rear window conform to the requirements of this Chapter within forty-eight
hours. The officer may also arrest the driver and give him notice to appear and further
require the driver or the owner of the vehicle to produce in court satisfactory evidence
that the windshield or rear window has been made to conform to the requirements of
this Chapter.
(Prior code § 10-20-31(B))

11.28.100.title: Broken glass—Replacement glass
11.28.100.text:
All broken glass in windows or elsewhere on a vehicle subject to the provisions of
this Title shall be removed. Replacement glass shall be of the safety type as defined
in Section 11.28.080.
(Prior code § 10-20-32(D))

11.28.110.title: Nontransparent window materials
11.28.110.text:
No person shall drive any motor vehicle with any sign, poster, card, sticker, or other
nontransparent material upon the front windshield, side wings, side or rear windows
of the vehicle, except that signs, posters, cards, stickers, or other materials may
be placed on the windshield within a six-inch square in the lower corner farthest
removed from the driver's position or upon the side windows of the vehicle to the
rear of the driver and so placed that the materials will not obstruct the driver's
clear view of traffic conditions.
(Ord. 2203 § 29, 1981: prior code § 10-20-25(A))

11.28.120.title: Windshield obstruction
11.28.120.text:
No person shall drive any motor vehicle upon a highway with any object so placed in
or upon the vehicle as to obstruct the driver's clear view through the windshield,
except required or permitted equipment of the vehicle.
(Prior code § 10-20-25(B))

11.28.130.title: Clear view and unimpaired operation
11.28.130.text:
No person shall drive any motor vehicle upon a highway with any object or person so
placed in the vehicle, or so placed on or about the driver of the vehicle as to obstruct
the driver's clear view of the traffic conditions or to interfere with the driver's
operation of the vehicle.
(Prior code § 10-20-25(C))

11.28.140.title: Obstruction exemption for common carriers
11.28.140.text:
Sections 11.28.110, 11.28.120 and 11.28.130 do not apply to direction, destination, or termini signs upon a passenger common
carrier motor vehicle.
(Prior code § 10-20-25(D))

11.28.150.title: Tints, reflective or other window obstructions
11.28.150.text:
(A)
No person shall drive any motor vehicle with any object or material placed upon the
windshield, side or rear windows or with any object placed in or upon the vehicle
so as to obstruct or reduce the driver's clear vision through the windshield or side
windows, or to obstruct or restrict the view of any person into or through such motor
vehicle. No person shall color or tint windows or windshields beyond the manufacturer's
specifications.
(B)
This Section shall not apply to:
(1)
Rear view mirrors or adjustable nontransparent sun visors which are mounted forward
of the side windows and are not attached to the glass;
(2)
Side windows which are to the rear of the driver.
(Ord. 1365 § 1, 1969: prior code § 10-20-43)

11.28.160.title: Spray or splash control
11.28.160.text:
No person shall operate any motor vehicle, trailer, or semitrailer unless equipped
with fenders, covers, or devices, including flaps or splash aprons, or unless the
body of the vehicle or attachments thereto afford adequate protection to effectively
minimize the spray or splash of water or mud to the rear of the vehicle. This Section
does not apply to those vehicles exempt from registration, nor to any other vehicles
having an unladen weight of under one thousand five hundred pounds.
(Prior code § 10-20-26)

11.28.170.title: Radiator or hood ornaments
11.28.170.text:
On and after January 1, 1939, no person shall sell any new motor vehicle, nor shall
any person operate any motor vehicle sold as a new motor vehicle in this State after
January 1, 1939, which is equipped with a radiator cap or radiator ornament upon the
top thereof which extends or protrudes to the front of the face of the radiator grill
of the motor vehicle, nor shall any person operate a motor vehicle equipped with a
radiator or hood ornament which interferes with the clear view of the driver of the
motor vehicle.
(Prior code § 10-20-27)

11.28.180.title: Fuel tank closure
11.28.180.text:
No motor vehicle shall be driven or moved upon any highway if the filling spout for
the fuel tank is closed or partly closed with a plug of wood, rags, or other combustible
material, and/or open completely so that the gas fumes are escaping from the filling
spout of the fuel tank.
(Prior code § 10-20-28)

11.28.190.title: Safety chain for towing
11.28.190.text:
Every towed vehicle shall be coupled to the towing vehicle by means of a safety chain,
chains, cables, or equivalent devices in addition to the regular trailer hitch or
coupling. This requirement does not apply to a semitrailer having a connecting device
composed of a fifth wheel and kingpin assembly, nor to a pole or pipe dolly. No more
slack shall be left in safety chains, cables, or equivalent devices than is necessary
to permit proper turning and the safety chains, cables or equivalent device shall
be so connected to the towed and towing vehicle and/or to a drawbar to prevent the
dropping of the towed vehicle or the loss of the towed vehicle and shall be of sufficient
strength to control the towed vehicle in the event of failure of the regular trailer
hitch or coupling.
(Prior code § 10-20-29)

11.28.200.title: Trailer signal requirements
11.28.200.text:
Whenever any motor vehicle is towing a trailer coach, either the motor vehicle or
trailer coach shall be equipped with a mechanical or electrical signal lamp or device.
(Prior code § 10-20-30)

11.28.210.title: Reserved
11.28.210.text:
Editor's note—
Ord. No. 6326, § 18, adopted June 18, 2014, repealed § 11.28.210, which pertained
to noisy vehicles and derived from prior code § 10-20-42 and Ord. No. 170, 1931.

11.28.220.title: Muffling required
11.28.220.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person to ride, drive or propel or cause or permit to
be ridden, driven or propelled any motor vehicle in, upon, or along any street or
to operate or cause or permit to be operated the motor in any such vehicle in any
street or other public place if such motor vehicle or the motor in such vehicle is
not provided with a good and sufficient muffler properly attached thereto or if the
exhaust from the motor of such vehicle is ejected otherwise than through such muffler,
or if such exhaust is ejected toward the surface of the street or ground.
(Ord. 170 § 46, 1931: prior code § 10-20-42(part))

11.28.230.title: Reserved
11.28.230.text:
Editor's note—
Ord. No. 6326, § 18, adopted June 18, 2014, repealed § 11.28.230, which pertained
to exhaust system—configuration—tubing type and derived from prior code § 10-20-36.

11.28.240.title: Exhaust system—Height of side discharge
11.28.240.text:
The exhaust gases from a motor vehicle shall not be directed to the side of the vehicle
between two feet and eleven feet above the ground.
(Prior code § 10-20-37)

11.28.250.title: Exhaust system—Gastightness—Cab tightness
11.28.250.text:
The cab of any motor vehicle shall be reasonably tight against the penetration of
gases and fumes from the engine and exhaust system. The exhaust system, including
the manifold, muffler, and exhaust pipes shall be so constructed as to be capable
of being maintained and shall be maintained in a reasonably gastight condition.
(Prior code § 10-20-39)

11.28.260.title: Exhaust system—Modification
11.28.260.text:
No person shall modify the exhaust system of a motor vehicle in a manner which will
amplify or increase the noise emitted by the motor of such vehicle above that emitted
by the muffler originally installed on the vehicle, and the original muffler shall
comply with all of the requirements of this Code.
(Prior code § 10-20-38)

11.28.270.title: Roadway clearance modification
11.28.270.text:
It is unlawful to operate any passenger motor vehicle which has been modified from
the original design so that any portion of such vehicle other than the wheels has
less clearance from the surface of a level roadway than the clearance between the
roadway and the lowermost portion of any rim of any wheel in contact with such roadway.
(Prior code § 10-20-40)

11.30.010.title: Rights and restrictions
11.30.010.text:
Pedestrians shall be granted those rights and be subject to the restrictions stated
in this Chapter.
(Prior code § 10-16-1)

11.30.020.title: Right-of-way—Darting before vehicles
11.30.020.text:
When traffic-control signals are not in place or not in operation the driver of a
vehicle shall yield the right-of-way, slowing down or stopping if need be to so yield,
to a pedestrian crossing the roadway upon which the vehicle is traveling, or when
the pedestrian is approaching so closely from the opposite one-half of the roadway
as to be in danger, but no pedestrian shall suddenly leave a curb or other place of
safety and walk or run into the path of a vehicle which is so close that it is impossible
for the driver to yield. A pedestrians' right-of-way in a crosswalk is modified under
the condition and as stated in Section 11.30.060.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 91(a): prior code § 10-16-2(A))

11.30.030.title: Passing vehicle stopped at crosswalk
11.30.030.text:
Whenever any vehicle is stopped at a marked crosswalk or at any unmarked crosswalk
at an intersection to permit a pedestrian to cross the roadway, the driver of any
other vehicle approaching from the rear shall not overtake and pass such stopped vehicle.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 91(b): prior code § 10-16-2(B))

11.30.040.title: Right half of crosswalks
11.30.040.text:
Pedestrians shall move, whenever practicable, upon the right one-half of crosswalks.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 92: prior code § 10-16-3)

11.30.050.title: Route of crossing roadway
11.30.050.text:
No pedestrian shall cross a roadway at any place other than by a route at right angles
to the curb or by the shortest route to the opposite curb except in a crosswalk.
(Ord. 170 § 10, 1931: prior code § 10-16-4)

11.30.060.title: Crossing outside crosswalk
11.30.060.text:
(A)
Every pedestrian crossing a roadway at any point other than within a marked crosswalk
or within an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection shall yield the right-of-way to
all vehicles upon the roadway.
(B)
Any pedestrian crossing a roadway at a point where a pedestrian tunnel or overhead
pedestrian crossing has been provided shall yield the right-of-way to all vehicles
upon the roadway.
(C)
The foregoing rules in this Section shall have no application under the conditions
stated in Section 11.30.070 when pedestrians are prohibited from crossing at certain designated places.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 94: prior code § 10-16-5)

11.30.070.title: Crosswalk use required when
11.30.070.text:
(A)
Between adjacent intersections at which traffic-control signals are in operation,
pedestrians shall not cross at any place except in a crosswalk.
(B)
No pedestrian shall cross a roadway other than in a marked crosswalk or within an
unmarked crosswalk in any business district.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 19, 6-18-14; 1949 code Ch. 36 § 95: prior code § 10-16-6)

11.30.080.title: Railroad crossing-control conformance
11.30.080.text:
No pedestrian shall pass through, around, over, or under any crossing gate or barrier
at a railroad grade crossing or bridge while such gate or barrier is closed or is
being opened or closed.
(Prior code § 10-16-7)

11.30.090.title: Sidewalk use required
11.30.090.text:
Where sidewalks are provided it shall be unlawful for any pedestrian to walk along
and upon an adjacent roadway.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 96(a): prior code § 10-16-8(A))

11.30.100.title: Walking along roadway
11.30.100.text:
Where sidewalks are not provided any pedestrian walking along and upon a street shall,
when practicable, walk only on the left side of the roadway or its shoulder facing
traffic which may approach from the opposite direction.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 96(b): prior code § 10-16-8(B))

11.30.110.title: Solicitation from roadway
11.30.110.text:
No person shall stand in a roadway for the purpose of soliciting a ride, employment,
or business from the occupant of any vehicle.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 96(c): prior code § 10-16-9(A))

11.30.120.title: Soliciting protection of parked vehicle
11.30.120.text:
No person shall stand on or in proximity to a street or highway for the purpose of
soliciting the watching or guarding of any vehicle while parked or about to be parked
on a street or highway.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 96(b): prior code § 10-16-9(B))

11.30.130.title: Due care of drivers
11.30.130.text:
Notwithstanding the foregoing provisions of this Chapter, every driver of a vehicle
shall exercise due care to avoid colliding with any pedestrian upon any roadway and
shall give warning by sounding the horn when necessary and shall exercise proper precaution
upon observing any child or any confused or incapacitated person upon a roadway.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 97: prior code § 10-16-10)

11.30.140.title: Blind persons
11.30.140.text:
(A)
No person, except those wholly or partially blind, shall carry or use on any street,
highway or in any other public place a cane or walking stick which is white in color
or white tipped with red.
(B)
Any pedestrian who is not wholly or partially blind, or any driver of any vehicle
who approaches or comes in contact with a person wholly or partially blind, carrying
a cane or walking stick white in color, or white tipped in red, or being assisted
by a person with wisdom, shall immediately come to a full stop and take such precautions
before proceeding as may be necessary to avoid an accident or injury to the person
wholly or partially blind.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 98: prior code § 10-16-11)

11.32.010.title: Duty to place and maintain
11.32.010.text:
The City Traffic Engineer shall place and maintain traffic-control signs, signals,
and devices when and as required under the traffic ordinances of the City to make
effective the provisions of said ordinances, and may place and maintain such additional
traffic-control devices as he may deem necessary to regulate traffic under the traffic
ordinances of this City or under State law or to guide and warn traffic.
(Ord. 1278 § 8, 1967: prior code § 10-10-1)

11.32.020.title: Standards—Uniformity—Official status
11.32.020.text:
All traffic-control signs, signals and devices shall conform to the manual and specifications
approved by the State Department of Transportation or resolution adopted by the City
Council. All signs and signals required hereunder for a particular purpose shall,
so far as practicable, be uniform as to type and location throughout the City. All
traffic-control devices so erected and not inconsistent with the provisions of State
law or this Code shall be official traffic-control devices.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 27 (part): prior code § 10-10-2)

11.32.030.title: Signs required for enforcement
11.32.030.text:
No provision of this Title for which signs are required shall be enforced against
an alleged violator if at the time and place of the alleged violation an official
sign is not in proper position and sufficiently legible to be seen by an ordinarily
observant person. Whenever a particular section does not state that signs are required,
such section shall be effective even though no signs are erected or in place.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 30: prior code § 10-10-4)

11.32.040.title: Lane direction control
11.32.040.text:
When lane-directional-control signals are placed on the individual lanes of a street
or highway, vehicular traffic may travel in any lane over which a green signal is
shown, but shall not enter or travel in any lane over which a red signal is shown.
(Ord. 1278 § 9, 1967: prior code § 10-10-10)

11.32.050.title: Interference unlawful
11.32.050.text:
No person shall, without lawful authority, attempt to or in fact alter, deface, injure,
knock down or remove any official traffic-control device, parking meter or any railroad
sign or signal or any inscription, shield or insignia thereon, or any other part thereof.
(Ord. 3989 § 3, 1996: Ord. 1157 § 1 (part), 1964: prior code § 10-31-1)

11.32.060.title: Removal by contractors
11.32.060.text:
It shall be unlawful for a contractor working in the street right-of-way of the City
to remove an official traffic-control device unless he has, at least two hours prior
to the removal of said device, notified the Director of Public Works or his designee
of his intention to remove said device and, in addition thereto, unless he has, immediately
prior to his removal of said device, installed a temporary device approved by the
Director of Public Works or his designee in a place approved by the Director of Public
Works or his designee to ensure traffic control.
(Ord. 3989 § 4, 1996: Ord. 1157 § 1 (part), 1964: prior code § 10-31-2(A))

11.32.070.title: Replacement by contractors—Required at completion
11.32.070.text:
It shall be unlawful for a contractor who has moved an official traffic-control device
to fail to install a traffic-control device approved by the Director of Public Works
or his designee in a location approved by the Director of Public Works or his designee
simultaneously with the completion of that portion of work in the street right-of-way
which made necessary the removal of the official traffic-control device.
(Ord. 3989 § 5, 1996: Ord. 1157 § 1 (part), 1964: prior code § 10-31-2(B))

11.32.080.title: Replacement by contractors—Deadline—Flagmen
11.32.080.text:
It shall be unlawful for a contractor working in the public right-of-way who has been
notified by the Director of Public Works or his designee to remove an official traffic-control
device from the construction area and install said device where directed by the Director
of Public Works or his designee to fail to do so within twenty-four hours after said
notification. The contractor shall furnish a traffic-control device approved by the
Director of Public Works or his designee, or shall comply with another traffic control
plan approved by the Director or his designee, to control traffic while the device
is being moved and until it is operative.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 20, 6-18-14; Ord. 3989 § 6, 1996: Ord. 1157 § 1 (part), 1964: prior
code § 10-31-2(C))

11.32.090.title: Damage by contractors
11.32.090.text:
(A)
The contractor shall notify the Director of Public Works or his designee immediately
after damage to an official traffic-control device.
(B)
The contractor shall provide for the directing of traffic by a method approved by
the City Traffic Engineer until the damaged device is replaced by a device approved
by the Director of Public Works or his designee.
(C)
The contractor shall, within twenty-four hours after damage to an official traffic-control
device, install a traffic-control device approved by the Director of Public Works
or his designee in a place approved by the Director of Public Works or his designee
to ensure traffic control.
(D)
It shall be unlawful for a contractor who has been notified by the Director of Public
Works or his designee that an official traffic-control device has been damaged during
the construction and who has further been notified by the Director of Public Works
or his designee to install a traffic-control device approved by the Director of Public
Works or his designee in a place approved by the Director of Public Works or his designee
to fail to do so within twenty-four hours after notification. The contractor shall
provide for the directing of traffic by a method approved by the City Traffic Engineer
or provide a traffic-control device approved by the Director of Public Works or his
designee to control traffic until the new traffic-control device is operative.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 21, 6-18-14; Ord. 3989 § 7, 1996: Ord. 1157 § 1 (part), 1964: prior
code § 10-31-3)

11.32.100.title: Impairment of view
11.32.100.text:
It shall be unlawful for the contractor to permit the construction, his workmen or
equipment to impair the view of any official traffic-control device unless he has,
at least two hours prior to the impairment of the view of said device, notified the
Director of Public Works or his designee that the construction, workmen or equipment
will impair the view of said device, and, in addition thereto, unless he has immediately
prior to the impairment of the view of said device, installed a temporary device approved
by the Director of Public Works or his designee in a place approved by the Director
of Public Works or his designee to ensure traffic control.
(Ord. 3989 § 8, 1996: Ord. 1157 § 1 (part), 1964: prior code § 10-31-4(A))

11.32.110.title: Failure to correct impairment
11.32.110.text:
It shall be unlawful for a contractor who has been notified that the construction,
workmen, or equipment impairs the view of any official traffic-control device and
who has further been notified by the Director of Public Works or his designee to install
a traffic-control device approved by the Director of Public Works or his designee
to fail to do so within twenty-four hours after notification. The contractor shall
provide for the directing of traffic by a method approved by the City Traffic Engineer
or provide a traffic-control device approved by the Director of Public Works or his
designee to control traffic until the new traffic-control device is operative.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 22, 6-18-14; Ord. 3989 § 9, 1996: Ord. 1157 § 1 (part), 1964: prior
code § 10-31-4(B))

11.33.010.title: Approval and installation
11.33.010.text:
(A)
The approval and installation of speed humps on residential streets within the City
shall be in accordance with:
(1)
This Section;
(2)
Any criteria for the approval and installation of such devices that have been adopted
by the City Council; and
(3)
Applicable provisions of the City's Fire Code.
(B)
The City Council shall have the discretion to waive any of the criteria described
in Paragraph (2) of Subsection (A) for good cause.
(C)
For purposes of this Section and the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices adopted
pursuant to NAC 408.411, speed humps are deemed to be roadway design features rather
than traffic-control devices.
(Ord. 5741 § 2, 2004)

11.34.010.title: Soliciting tow service at scene
11.34.010.text:
No person shall, at the location of any vehicular accident, collision or other catastrophe
or calamity, solicit or offer the sale of any tow service. The prohibition contained
in this Section shall apply from time of the happening of any of the aforesaid occurrences
until a reasonable time thereafter, and at all times while law enforcement officers,
public health personnel, emergency personnel and other persons discharging duties
imposed by law are actively engaged in the performance of duty at the location of
said occurrences.
(Prior code § 10-9-11)

11.34.020.title: Impoundment of hit-and-run suspects
11.34.020.text:
When any regularly employed and salaried Officer of the Metropolitan Police Department
has reasonable cause to believe that a motor vehicle has been involved in a hit-and-run
accident, and the vehicle is found on the public streets, under circumstances where
the operator or owner cannot be located after reasonable effort is made, the Officer
may impound the vehicle for the purpose of inspection completion of any necessary
accident report. Unless sooner released, the vehicle shall be released upon the expiration
of twenty-four hours after impound has occurred, upon demand of the owner.
(Ord. 1350 § 4, 1968: prior code § 10-9-12)

11.36.010.title: Gaseous-discharge lamps for traffic control
11.36.010.text:
Emergency vehicles of the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department and the Department
of Fire and Rescue, when they are operated under the conditions provided in NRS 484B.700,
and Traffic Engineering test vehicles may display a flashing white light from gaseous-discharge
lamps which are designed and used for the purpose of controlling official traffic-control
signals.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 23, 6-18-14; Ord. 4028 § 1, 1996: Ord. 2203 § 19, 1981: prior code
§ 10-8-1)

11.38.010.title: Seat use mandatory
11.38.010.text:
A person operating a motorcycle shall not ride other than upon the permanent and regular
seat attached thereto or carry any other person, nor shall any other person ride upon
such motorcycle, other than upon a firmly attached seat to the rear or side of the
operator.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 13: prior code § 10-15-9(A))

11.38.020.title: Passengers
11.38.020.text:
No driver of a two-wheeled or three-wheeled motor vehicle shall carry any other person
on, upon or within such vehicle on any street or highway in the City, except as hereinafter
provided; provided, however, that if any two-wheeled or three-wheeled motor vehicle
shall have either a double seating device with double footrests or a sidecar attachment
providing a separate seat space within such sidecar attachment for each person riding
therein so that such person is seated entirely within the body of said sidecar, then
it shall be permissible for an operator who has attained the age of sixteen or older
to carry a passenger. A demonstration ride by a licensed dealer or his employee is
excepted from the provisions hereof.
(Ord. 1291 § 1 (part), 1967: prior code § 10-1A-1 (part))

11.38.030.title: Sidewalk riding
11.38.030.text:
No motorcycle or motor scooter shall be ridden upon any sidewalk of the City.
(Ord. 1291 § 1 (part), 1967: prior code § 10-1A-1 (part))

11.38.040.title: Holding to moving vehicles
11.38.040.text:
No rider of a motorcycle or motor scooter shall hold to any moving vehicle for the
purpose of being propelled.
(Ord. 1291 § 1 (part), 1967: prior code § 10-1A-1 (part))

11.38.050.title: Passing between lanes
11.38.050.text:
No driver of a motorcycle or motor scooter shall pass other vehicles in between lanes
of traffic traveling in the same direction, authorized emergency vehicles excepted.
(Ord. 1291 § 1 (part), 1967: prior code § 10-1A-1 (part))

11.38.060.title: Windshield
11.38.060.text:
On motorcycles the glazing material shall be of either approved safety glass or clear
plastic which need not be of an approved type.
(Prior code § 10-15-9(B))

11.38.070.title: Reserved
11.38.070.text:
Editor's note—
Ord. No. 6326, § 24, adopted June 18, 2014, repealed § 11.38.070, which pertained
to handlebar height and derived from prior code § 10-1A-1; Ord. No. 1291, 1967.

11.38.080.title: Applicability of equipment requirements
11.38.080.text:
The equipment provided for in Sections 11.38.090 through 11.38.130 shall be required on all motorcycles and all motor scooters except on actual trail
rides conducted outside of public roads and highways.
This section shall not apply to operators or passengers of three-wheeled vehicles
which have an enclosed passenger compartment.
(Ord. 2203 § 3 (part), 1981: Ord. 1291 § 1 (part), 1967: prior code § 10-1A-3 (part)(F))

11.38.090.title: Brakes—Stop lamps
11.38.090.text:
All motorcycles and motor scooters covered under this Section, as provided in Section
11.38.080, shall be equipped with brakes adequate to control the movement of same, to stop
and hold such vehicles, including two separate means of applying the brakes; one means
shall be effective to apply the brakes to the front wheel and one means shall be effective
to apply the brakes to the rear wheels. All such vehicles shall be equipped with a
stop lamp on the rear of the vehicle, which shall display a red or amber light, or
any shade of color between red and amber, visible from a distance of not less than
three hundred feet to the rear in normal sunlight, and which shall be actuated upon
application of the rear service brakes.
(Ord. 2203 § 3 (part), 1981: Ord. 1291 § 1 (part), 1967: prior code § 10-1A-3(A))

11.38.100.title: Speedometer
11.38.100.text:
All vehicles covered under this Section, as provided in Section 11.38.080, shall be equipped with a properly operating speedometer capable of registering at
least the maximum legal speed limit for that vehicle.
(Ord. 2203 § 3 (part), 1981: Ord. 1291 § 1 (part), 1967: prior code § 10-1A-3(B))

11.38.110.title: Fenders
11.38.110.text:
All vehicles covered under this Section, as provided in Section 11.38.080, shall be equipped with a fender over each wheel. All fenders shall be of the type
provided by the manufacturer, but can be made of other material.
(Ord. 2203 § 3 (part), 1981: Ord. 1291 § 1 (part), 1967: prior code § 10-1A-3(C))

11.38.120.title: Lights
11.38.120.text:
(A)
All vehicles covered under this Section, as provided in Section 11.38.080, shall carry at least one lighted headlamp capable of showing a white light visible
at least three hundred feet in the direction in which the same are proceeding, and
one tail lamp mounted on the rear which, when lighted, shall emit a red light plainly
visible from at least five hundred feet to the rear.
(B)
The lights required by this Section shall be burning whenever such vehicles are in
motion during the period from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise
and at any other time when, due to insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions,
persons and vehicles on the streets are not clearly discernible at a distance of at
least five hundred feet ahead.
(Ord. 2203 § 3 (part), 1981: Ord. 1291 § 1 (part), 1967: prior code § 10-1A-3(D))

11.38.130.title: Shoes
11.38.130.text:
No person shall operate or ride upon any vehicle covered under this Section, as provided
in Section 11.38.080, unless such person is wearing protective foot covering. Sandals, thongs and open-toed
shoes are not considered protective foot covering.
(Ord. 2203 § 3 (part), 1981: Ord. 1291 § 1 (part), 1967: prior code § 10-1A-3(E))

11.39.010.title: Legislative determination
11.39.010.text:
The City Council declares as a matter of legislative determination that:
(A)
The growth of Las Vegas and the continuing expansion of hotels, casinos and other
businesses in downtown Las Vegas are drawing increasing numbers of pedestrians and
vehicles to the downtown area.
(B)
Because of the influx of pedestrians and motor vehicles, the streets are becoming
more congested. In this context, the introduction of slower-moving vehicles such as
animal-drawn vehicles, pedicabs, and pedalbuses into downtown traffic poses unacceptable
hazards to those persons using the streets downtown.
(C)
In hearings conducted regarding the use of such vehicles, the predecessor to the Public
Utilities Commission of Nevada acknowledged the authority of the City to regulate
the use of its streets for the public safety and welfare.
(D)
The regulations contained in this Chapter are necessary for the public safety and
welfare.
(Ord. No. 6555, § 3, 11-2-16; Ord. No. 6326, § 25, 6-18-14; Ord. 3317 §§ 1 (part),
2, 1987)

11.39.020.title: Definitions
11.39.020.text:
Unless the context otherwise requires, the terms and words used in this chapter shall
have the meaning ascribed to them in Chapter 11.02 of this Title and in this Section:
(A)
"Bicycle" means a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride, having
two tandem wheels, either of which is over fourteen inches in diameter, or every such
device generally recognized as a bicycle, though equipped with two front or two rear
wheels, except a moped.
(B)
"Pedicab" means a three-wheeled bicycle that is:
(1)
Moved solely by the muscle power of the operator or with the assistance of an electric
motor; and
(2)
Capable of transporting up to four passengers plus the operator.
(C)
"Pedalbus" means a four-wheeled bicycle that is:
(1)
Capable of transporting five or more passengers;
(2)
Steered by an operator who is not a passenger; and
(3)
Powered by more than one person, whether operator or passenger, and with the optional
assistance of an electric motor.
(Ord. No. 6803, § 5, 1-19-22; Ord. No. 6555, § 4, 11-2-16; Ord. 3317 §§ 1 (part),
3—6, 1987)

11.39.030.title: Restricted area—Designated
11.39.030.text:
It is unlawful for any person, unless exempted by Section 11.39.040 or by specific action of the City Council, to operate, drive or propel an animal-drawn
vehicle, pedicab or pedalbus on public streets beyond the boundaries of the area designated
as the Central Traffic District.
(Ord. No. 6555, § 5, 11-2-16; Ord. 5972 § 12, 2008: Ord. 3317 §§ 1 (part), 7, 1987)

11.39.040.title: Restricted area—Exemptions
11.39.040.text:
The following persons are exempt from the restriction of Section 11.39.030:
(A)
Persons riding bicycles and not carrying passengers for hire; and
(B)
Persons operating, driving or propelling animal-drawn vehicles in any parade for which
a permit has been issued pursuant to this Title.
(Ord. No. 6555, § 3, 11-2-16; Ord. 3317 §§ 1 (part), 8, 1987)

11.39.050.title: Routes
11.39.050.text:
Routes for the operation of animal-drawn vehicles may be established on public streets
subject to the provisions of Section 11.39.030 of this Chapter and the following restrictions:
(A)
A vehicle subject to this Chapter shall be operated only upon the routes approved
by the City Council upon the recommendation of the Traffic and Parking Commission
and pursuant to time schedules approved by the Traffic and Parking Commission.
(B)
The City Traffic Engineer may reject any proposed route or time schedule that would
present a hazard to the public health, safety or welfare, or interfere with the safe
and efficient operation of vehicular traffic on any public street.
(C)
The Traffic and Parking Commission shall review annually all routes approved pursuant
to this Section in light of changed conditions on those routes that affect the public
