health, safety or welfare, or the safe and efficient operation of vehicular traffic
on the affected public streets.
(1)
If the operating conditions on a given route have not changed so as to adversely affect
the public health, safety or welfare, or the safe and efficient operation of vehicular
traffic on the affected public streets, the Commission shall recommend that the City
Council approve the licensee's use of those routes for the following year.
(2)
If the operating conditions on a given route have changed to as to adversely affect
the public health, safety or welfare, or the safe and efficient operation of vehicular
traffic on the affected public streets on a continuing basis, the Commission shall
recommend that the City Council prohibit the licensee's use of that portion of the
route so affected.
(D)
Any route or time schedule approved pursuant to this Chapter shall be subject to the
right of the City to prohibit or suspend the use of the City streets by the licensee
when such operation would pose an immediate hazard to the safety requirements of the
public or interfere with special events approved by the City.
(E)
Modifications to the approved route and time schedule may be issued by the Traffic
Engineer to the licensee for special purposes for a period not to exceed ten days.
Permanent modifications to the approved route and time schedule must be approved by
the Traffic and Parking Commission. Said modifications shall be subject to approval
by any other regulatory agency having jurisdiction over the licensee, such as the
Public Service Commission.
(Ord. No. 6555, § 7, 11-2-16; Ord. 3317 §§ 1 (part), 9, 1987)

11.39.055.title: Pedicabs and pedalbuses
11.39.055.text:
A person may operate a pedicab or pedalbus on any public street within the Central
Traffic District, except as otherwise follows:
(A)
Pedicabs and pedalbuses shall only operate upon those streets, and during the days
and times as indicated by the appropriate restrictions map produced by the Department
of Public Works. The restrictions indicated by such maps shall conform initially with
the Pedicab Restrictions Map and Pedalbus Restrictions Map provided as attachments
to Ordinance No. 6555. Such maps, and the restrictions indicated may be amended by
resolution of the City Council, after receiving a recommendation from the Traffic
and Parking Commission to take such actions, in conformance with Subsection B of this
Section.
(B)
Upon the request of the Traffic Engineer, the Traffic and Parking Commission shall
review the boundaries of the Central Traffic District, the prohibited streets, the
restricted streets, or hours of restriction in light of changed conditions on those
routes that affect the public health, safety or welfare, or the safe and efficient
operation of vehicular traffic on the affected public streets. If the operating conditions
within the Central Traffic District have changed as to adversely affect the public
health, safety or welfare, or the safe and efficient operation of vehicular traffic
on a continuing basis, the Commission shall recommend to the City Council modifications
to the Central Traffic District boundaries, the prohibited streets, the restricted
streets or hours of restriction.
(C)
The City may prohibit or suspend the use of the public streets by an operator of a
pedicab or pedalbus when such operation would pose a hazard to the public or interfere
with special events approved by the City. Except for emergency declarations, the Traffic
Engineer shall endeavor to provide seventy-two hours' notice of a prohibition or suspension
to such operators, and such prohibition or modification shall not exceed sixty days
without another notice of prohibition or suspension from the Traffic Engineer.
(Ord. No. 6555, § 8, 11-2-16)

11.39.060.title: Operation restrictions
11.39.060.text:
Pedicabs, pedalbuses and animal-drawn vehicles may be operated within the Central
Traffic District, subject to the following restrictions:
(A)
Animal-Drawn Vehicles.
(1)
The vehicles shall pick up, and discharge passengers only at designated stands approved
by the Traffic and Parking Commission.
(2)
The vehicles shall park only in designated stands approved by the Traffic and Parking
Commission.
(3)
Except when making left turns, the vehicles shall be operated only in the traffic
lane nearest the curb on any public street and the driver shall obey all applicable
State and local traffic laws, ordinances and regulations.
(B)
Pedicabs.
(1)
Loading and Unloading Passengers. A pedicab shall only remain standing upon a public
street provided that such pedicab is located within a legal, metered parking space
and only for the time required to load or unload passengers not to exceed three minutes,
or if parked in conformance with this Section as provided herein. Notwithstanding
any provision of the Code to the contrary, if the operator of a pedicab is actively
loading or unloading passengers as provided above within a legal, metered parking
space, activation of the parking meter for such space pursuant to LVMC Chapter 11.54 not required. Pedicabs shall not stand in any designated loading zone at any time
for any reason.
(2)
Parking.
(a)
If a pedicab is standing in a legal, metered parking space, but not actively loading
or unloading passengers, the operator of that pedicab shall immediately activate the
meter for such space as required by LVMC Chapter 11.54, unless that specific pedicab is the subject of a space rental agreement with the
Parking Services Division for that specified parking space.
(b)
A pedicab shall not park in a designated loading zone at any time for any reason.
(c)
Notwithstanding Subparagraph (a), above, a pedicab is prohibited from parking or standing
for any amount of time in specially-designated spaces by the City, such as designated
spaces for animal-drawn carriages, taxicabs, busses, and handicapped individuals,
except and unless the pedicab operator has executed a space rental agreement designating
a specific parking space or spaces for specified pedicabs with the Parking Services
Division.
(C)
Pedalbuses. Pedalbuses shall not park or remain standing upon any public street for
any reason, unless the pedalbus is wholly-contained within an activated, metered parking
space or spaces, or is parking or standing in a parking space that is the subject
of a space rental agreement with the Parking Services Division for that specified
pedalbus.
(D)
Pedicabs and Pedalbuses. Pedicabs and pedalbuses that are moved with the assistance
of an electric motor on any public street within the Central Traffic District shall
not operate at a speed exceeding the speed limit posted on that street for motor vehicle
traffic.
(Ord. No. 6803, § 6, 1-19-22; Ord. No. 6555, § 9, 11-2-16; Ord. 3317 §§ 1 (part),
10, 1987)

11.39.070.title: Council authority over Commission actions
11.39.070.text:
There is reserved to the City Council the power to reverse, modify or confirm any
action of the Traffic and Parking Commission under this Chapter if any member of the
City Council makes a request to review the decision to the Secretary of the Traffic
and Parking Commission within fourteen days of the date of the decision of the Traffic
and Parking Commission. If any member of the City Council makes such a request, the
matter shall be placed on the agenda for the next meeting of the City Council and
the decision of the Traffic and Parking Commission shall be stayed until the City
Council has acted on the matter.
(Ord. 3317 §§ 1 (part), 11, 1987)

11.39.080.title: Requirements
11.39.080.text:
Before operating any pedicab or pedalbus, whether or not equipped with motorized assistance,
the operator must:
(A)
Comply with applicable licensing requirements under LVMC Chapter 6.63; and
(B)
Obtain the approval of all State agencies, if any, which may have jurisdiction over
the operation of pedicabs or pedalbuses on public streets, including but not necessarily
limited to, the Nevada Transportation Authority.
(Ord. No. 6803, § 7, 1-19-22)

11.40.010.title: Defined
11.40.010.text:
"Bicycle" includes every device propelled by human power upon which any person or
persons may ride, having two tandem wheels, either of which is over fourteen inches
in diameter, and also any device generally recognized as a bicycle although equipped
with two front and/or two rear wheels.
(Ord. No. 6555, § 10, 11-2-16; Ord. 2203 § 1, 1981: Ord. 1293 § 1, 1967: prior code
§ 10-1-1)

11.40.020.title: Conformance required
11.40.020.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person to do any act forbidden, or fail to perform any
act required, in this Chapter.
(1949 code Ch. 6 § 2(a): prior code § 10-1-2(part))

11.40.030.title: Parent or guardian responsibility
11.40.030.text:
The parent of any child and the guardian of any ward shall not authorize or knowingly
permit any such child or ward to violate any of the provisions of this Chapter.
(1949 code Ch. 6 § 2(b): prior code § 10-1-2 (part))

11.40.040.title: Applicability to streets and public paths
11.40.040.text:
These regulations applicable to bicycles, electric bicycles, and electric scooters
shall apply whenever a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter is operated
upon any street, or upon any public path set aside for the exclusive use of bicycles,
electric bicycles, or electric scooters, subject to those exceptions stated herein.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 3, 8-6-25; 1949 code Ch. 6 § 2(c): prior code § 10-1-2 (part))

11.40.050.title: Report of sale or purchase
11.40.050.text:
Every person engaged in the business of buying or selling new or secondhand bicycles
shall make a report to the Sheriff of every bicycle purchased or sold by such dealer,
giving the name and address of the person from whom purchased or to whom sold, a description
of such bicycle by name or make, the frame number thereof and the number of license
plate, if any, found thereon.
(1949 code Ch. 6 § 11: prior code § 10-1-10)

11.40.060.title: Traffic-law applicability
11.40.060.text:
Every person riding a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter upon a roadway
shall be granted all of the rights and shall be subject to all the duties applicable
to the driver of a vehicle by the laws of this State declaring rules of the road applicable
to vehicles or by the traffic laws of the City applicable to the driver of a vehicle,
except as to special regulations in this Chapter and except to those provisions of
laws which by their nature can have no application.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 4, 8-6-25; 1949 code Ch. 6 § 12: prior code § 10-1-11)

11.40.070.title: Traffic-control devices
11.40.070.text:
Any person operating a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter shall obey the
instructions of official traffic-control signals, signs and other control devices
applicable to vehicles, unless otherwise directed by a Police Officer.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 5, 8-6-25; 1949 code Ch. 6 § 13(a): prior code § 10-1-12(part))

11.40.080.title: Restricted turns
11.40.080.text:
Whenever authorized signs are erected indicating that no right turn, left turn or
U-turn is permitted, it shall be unlawful for any person operating a bicycle, electric
bicycle, or electric scooter to disobey the direction of any such sign, except where
such person dismounts from the bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter to make
any such turn, in which event such person shall then obey the regulations applicable
to pedestrians.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 6, 8-6-25; 1949 code Ch. 6 § 13(b): prior code § 10-1-12(part))

11.40.090.title: Seat use—Number riding
11.40.090.text:
A person propelling a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter shall not ride
other than astride a permanent and regular seat attached thereto. No bicycle, electric
bicycle, or electric scooter shall be used to carry more persons at one time than
the number for which it is designed and equipped.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 7, 8-6-25; 1949 code Ch. 6 § 14: prior code § 10-1-13)

11.40.100.title: Keeping to right—Passing vehicles
11.40.100.text:
Every person operating a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter upon a roadway
shall ride as near to the right-hand side of the roadway as practicable, exercising
due care when passing a standing vehicle or one proceeding in the same direction.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 8, 8-6-25; 1949 code Ch. 6 § 15(a): prior code § 10-1-14(part))

11.40.110.title: Riding abreast
11.40.110.text:
Persons riding bicycles, electric bicycles, or electric scooters upon a roadway shall
not ride more than two abreast except on paths or parts of roadways set aside for
the exclusive use of bicycles, electric bicycles, and electric scooters.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 9, 8-6-25; 1949 code Ch. 6 § 15(b): prior code § 10-1-14(part))

11.40.120.title: Use of available path
11.40.120.text:
Whenever a usable path for bicycles, electric bicycles, or electric scooters has been
provided adjacent to a roadway, riders of bicycles, electric bicycles, and electric
scooters shall use such path and shall not use the roadway.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 10, 8-6-25; 1949 code Ch. 6 § 15(c): prior code § 10-1-14(part))

11.40.130.title: Speed
11.40.130.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a bicycle at a speed greater than is
reasonable and prudent under the conditions then existing.
(1949 code Ch. 6 § 16: prior code § 10-1-15)

11.40.140.title: Crossing sidewalk or sidewalk area
11.40.140.text:
The operator of a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter within a business
or residence district entering into or emerging from an alley, driveway or building
shall stop such vehicle immediately prior to driving onto a sidewalk or onto the sidewalk
area extending across any alleyway, driveway or building, yielding the right-of-way
to any pedestrian as may be necessary to avoid collision.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 11, 8-6-25; 1949 code Ch. 6 § 17: prior code § 10-1-16)

11.40.150.title: Attaching to vehicles
11.40.150.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person riding upon any bicycle, electric bicycle, or
electric scooter to attach the same or himself to any vehicle upon a roadway.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 12, 8-6-25; 1949 code Ch. 6 § 18: prior code § 10-1-17)

11.40.160.title: Carrying articles in hands
11.40.160.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person operating a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric
scooter to carry any package, bundle or article which prevents the rider from keeping
at least one hand upon the handlebars.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 13, 8-6-25; 1949 code Ch. 6 § 19: prior code § 10-1-18)

11.40.170.title: Parking
11.40.170.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person to park a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric
scooter upon a street other than upon the roadway against the curb or upon the sidewalk
in a rack to support the bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter or against
a building or at the curb, in such a manner as to afford the least obstruction to
pedestrian traffic.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 14, 8-6-25; 1949 code Ch. 6 § 20: prior code § 10-1-19)

11.40.180.title: Sidewalk riding
11.40.180.text:
(A)
It shall be unlawful for any person to ride a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric
scooter upon the sidewalks on Fremont Street between Main Street and Seventh Street.
This area shall be posted with signs indicating that the riding of bicycles, electric
bicycles, or electric scooters on the sidewalk is prohibited.
(B)
The Director of Public Works is authorized to erect signs on any other sidewalk or
any roadway in the City prohibiting the riding of bicycles, electric bicycles, or
electric scooters thereon by any person when the Director after consultation with
the City Traffic Engineer and the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department determines
that the use of bicycles, electric bicycles, or electric scooters on the sidewalk
or roadway in question will impede or interfere with the flow of pedestrian or vehicular
traffic, and when such signs are in place it shall be unlawful for any person to disobey
the same.
(C)
Whenever any person is riding a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter upon
a sidewalk, such person shall yield the right-of-way to any pedestrian and shall give
audible signal before overtaking and passing such pedestrian.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 15, 8-6-25; Ord. No. 6326, § 26, 6-18-14; Ord. 2038 § 1, 1979: prior
code § 10-1-20)

11.40.185.title: Electric bicycles and electric scooters
11.40.185.text:
(A)
Unless otherwise designated or posted, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
may be operated on a public roadway or sidewalk, or a lane, path, or route designated
for bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter use.
(B)
It shall be unlawful for any person to perform stunts or wheelies, ride on handlebars,
operate at unsafe speeds, or engage in any other reckless behavior while operating
an electric bicycle or electric scooter on a public roadway or sidewalk, or a lane,
path or route designated for bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter use.
(C)
Helmets are recommended for any person operating an electric bicycle or electric scooter.
Minors must wear a helmet at all times when operating an electric bicycle or electric
scooter on a public roadway or sidewalk, or a lane, path or route designated for bicycle,
electric bicycle, or electric scooter use.
(D)
A violation of LVMC 11.40.185 is a civil infraction. A first violation shall result in a fine of one hundred and
fifty dollars. A second violation shall result in a fine of three hundred dollars.
Subsequent violations shall result in a fine of five hundred dollars. Parents or guardians
shall be held financially responsible for violations of LVMC 11.40.185 committed by a minor under their supervision.
(E)
Law enforcement officers are authorized to enforce the provisions of this Section.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 16, 8-6-25)

11.40.190.title: Lamps and reflectors
11.40.190.text:
Every bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter, when in use at night-time, shall
be equipped with a lamp on the front which shall emit a white light visible from a
distance of at least five hundred feet to the front and with a red reflector on the
rear of a type which shall be visible from all distances from fifty feet to three
hundred feet to the rear when directly in front of lawful upper beams of headlamps
on a motor vehicle. In addition to the red reflector, a lamp emitting a red light
visible from a distance of five hundred feet to the rear shall be used.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 17, 8-6-25; Ord. 1515 § 1, 1971: prior code § 10-1-21 (part))

11.40.200.title: Audible signaling device
11.40.200.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person to use a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric
scooter unless it is equipped with a bell or other device capable of giving a signal
audible for a distance of at least one hundred feet except that a bicycle, electric
bicycle, or electric scooter shall not be equipped with, nor shall any persons use
upon a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter, any siren or whistle.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 18, 8-6-25; Ord. 1515 § 1 (part), 1971: prior code § 10-1-21 (part))

11.40.210.title: Brake
11.40.210.text:
Every bicycle, electric bicycle, and electric scooter shall be equipped with a brake
which will enable the operator to make the braked wheel skid on dry, level, clean
pavement.
(Ord. No. 6921, § 19, 8-6-25; Ord. 1515 § 1 (part), 1971: prior code § 10-1-21 (part))

11.40.220.title: Violation—Juvenile warming citation
11.40.220.text:
In addition to any other penalties provided in this Code, a juvenile warning citation
may be issued to any juvenile for any violation of the provisions of this Chapter.
(Ord. 1497 § 2 (part), 1971: prior code § 10-1-22(part))

11.40.230.title: Violation—Bicycle safety school
11.40.230.text:
(A)
If a juvenile receives three juvenile warning citations within a six month period,
the Sheriff shall cause a notice to be given to said juvenile requiring him to attend
bicycle safety school at a time and place to be set forth in said notice.
(B)
The fee to attend said bicycle safety school shall be five dollars, which said fee
must be paid by the juvenile or his parent at the time the juvenile attends the school.
(Ord. 1497 § 2 (part), 1971: prior code § 10-1-22(part))

11.41.010.title: Operation of golf carts—Where permitted
11.41.010.text:
Those streets, parts of streets, or areas described in Schedule 28-I, a copy of which
is to be maintained for public inspection in the office of the City Clerk and the
City Traffic Engineer, and such other streets, parts of streets, or areas as may be
added to said Schedule by resolution of the City Council, are declared to be public
street segments where the operation of golf carts is permitted in accordance with
the provisions of the Nevada Revised Statutes.
(Ord. 3607 § 2, 1991)

11.41.020.title: Operation of golf carts—Unlawful—Exceptions
11.41.020.text:
Except in locations designated by Schedule 28-I, and except where crossing a public
street at a marked and signed crossing authorized by the City Traffic Engineer, it
shall be unlawful to operate a golf cart on any City street or right-of-way.
(Ord. 3607 § 3, 1991)

11.42.010.title: Sign posting
11.42.010.text:
Whenever any regulation of this City designates any one-way street or alley the City
Traffic Engineer shall place and maintain signs giving notice thereof, and no such
regulation shall be effective unless such signs are in place. Signs indicating the
direction of lawful traffic movement shall be placed at every intersection where movement
of traffic in the opposite direction is prohibited.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 21: prior code § 10-26-1)

11.42.020.title: Designation in schedules on file
11.42.020.text:
Upon these streets and parts of streets and in those alleys described in Schedules
26-I and 26-II, respectively, copies of which shall be maintained for public inspection
in the offices of the City Clerk and the City Traffic Engineer and may be amended
from time to time by resolution of the City Council, vehicular traffic shall move
only in the indicated direction at every intersection where movement in the opposite
direction is prohibited.
(Ord. 1589 § 14, 1972: Ord. 1534 § 9, 1971; Ord. 1384 §§ 6, 7, 1969; Ord. 1339 § 6,
1968; Ord. 1278 § 29, 1967; Ord. 800 § 2 (part), 1959: Ord. 750 § 4(A), 1957: prior
code § 10-26-2)

11.42.030.title: Reversible lanes—Temporary designation
11.42.030.text:
The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to determine and designate streets, or specific
lanes thereon upon which vehicular traffic shall proceed in one direction during one
period and the opposite direction during another period of the day, and may also erect
signs temporarily designating lanes to be used by traffic moving in any particular
direction, regardless of the centerline of the roadway. It shall be unlawful for any
person to operate any vehicle in violation of such markings, signs, barriers, or other
devices so placed in accordance with this Section.
(Ord. 800 § 2 (part), 1959: Ord. 750 § 4(B), 1957: prior code § 10-26-3)

11.43.010.title: Operation of vehicles within a roundabout
11.43.010.text:
The following regulations pertain to the operation of vehicles within a roundabout:
(A)
All vehicular travel shall be in a counterclockwise direction.
(B)
The operator of a vehicle entering a roundabout shall yield the right-of-way to vehicles
already in the roundabout and wait for a gap in traffic before entering.
(C)
The operator of a vehicle who intends to exit a roundabout:
(1)
Shall use the left lane to turn left or complete a U-turn;
(2)
Shall use the right lane to turn right; and
(3)
May use either lane to go straight through the roundabout.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 27, 6-4-14)

11.44.010.title: Designation authority—Signposting
11.44.010.text:
The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to determine the location of passenger and
freight curb-loading zones and shall place and maintain appropriate signs indicating
the same and stating the hours during which the provisions of this Section are applicable.
(Ord. 1589 § 11 (part), 1972: prior code § 10-18-1)

11.44.020.title: Passenger
11.44.020.text:
Upon those streets or highways or parts of streets or highways described in Schedule
18-I, a copy of which is to be maintained for public inspection in the offices of
the City Clerk and the City Traffic Engineer, which may be amended from time to time
by written finding of the City Traffic Engineer, no person shall stop, stand or park
a vehicle for any purpose or period of time other than for the expeditious loading
or unloading of passengers in any place marked as a passenger curb-loading zone during
hours when the regulations applicable to such curb loading zone are effective. The
time period limitations under this Section are as follows:
(A)
Not to exceed three minutes, at locations designated as limited to three minutes and
posted with signage accordingly.
(B)
No specific time period but limited to expeditious loading and unloading, at locations
designated as an "immediate loading and unloading" zone and posted with signage accordingly.
(Ord. No. 6703, § 8, 10-2-19; Ord. 3990 § 7, 1996: Ord. 1589 § 11 (part), 1972: Ord.
1534 § 7, 1971; Ord. 1278 § 26, 1967; Ord. 1169 § 6, 1965: Ord. 750 § 7, 1957: prior
code § 10-18-2)

11.44.030.title: Hotel
11.44.030.text:
Upon those streets or highways or parts of streets or highways described in Schedule
18-II, a copy of which is to be maintained for public inspection in the offices of
the City Clerk and the City Traffic Engineer, which may be amended from time to time
by written finding of the City Traffic Engineer, no person shall stop, stand or park
a vehicle for any purpose or period of time other than for the expeditious loading
or unloading of passengers or goods in any place marked as a hotel loading zone, during
hours when the regulations applicable to such hotel loading zone are effective, and
then only for a period not to exceed ten minutes.
(Ord. 3990 § 8, 1996: Ord. 1589 § 11 (part), 1972: Ord. 1278 § 25, 1967: prior code
§ 10-18-3)

11.44.040.title: Time-limited—Fifteen minutes
11.44.040.text:
Upon those streets or highways or parts of streets or highways described in Schedule
18-III, a copy of which shall be maintained for public inspection in the offices of
the City Clerk and the City Traffic Engineer, which may be amended from time to time
by written finding of the City Traffic Engineer, no person shall stop, stand or park
a vehicle for any purpose or period of time other than for the expeditious loading
or unloading of passengers or goods in any place marked as a time-limited loading
zone, during hours when the regulations applicable to such loading zone are effective,
and then only for a period not to exceed fifteen minutes.
(Ord. 3990 § 9, 1996: Ord. 1589 § 11 (part), 1972: prior code § 10-18-4)

11.44.060.title: Commercial—Designated
11.44.060.text:
Upon those streets or highways or parts of streets or highways described in Schedule
18-V, a copy of which shall be maintained for public inspection in the offices of
the City Clerk and the City Traffic Engineer, which may be amended from time to time
by written finding of the City Traffic Engineer, no person shall stop, stand or park
a vehicle for any purpose or length of time other than for the expeditious and continuous
loading and delivery or pickup and loading of heavy or voluminous freight, cargo or
other goods in any place marked as a commercial loading zone during hours when the
provisions applicable to such zones are in effect. In no case shall the stop for loading
and unloading of materials exceed thirty minutes, day or night. The use of a commercial
loading zone under this Section is limited to:
(A)
Commercial vehicles whose commercial nature is evident from the type of vehicle; or
(B)
Vehicles which have commercially-printed markings on the exterior of the vehicle clearly
identifying the commercial use of the vehicle.
(Ord. 5870 § 12, 2006: Ord. 3990 § 10, 1996: Ord. 3829 § 2, 1994: Ord. 1589 § 11 (part),
1972: prior code § 10-18-6)

11.44.070.title: Commercial—Length
11.44.070.text:
Commercial loading zones shall be limited in distance so that the stopping, standing
or parking of vehicles within the zone shall not create an especially hazardous condition
or cause an unusual delay to traffic.
(Ord. 1589 § 11 (part), 1972: prior code § 10-18-10)

11.44.080.title: Tour bus
11.44.080.text:
Upon those streets, highways, thoroughfares, or parts thereof, described in Schedule
18-VI, a copy of which is to be maintained for public inspection in the office of
the City Clerk and the office of the City Traffic Engineer, and which may be amended
from time to time by written finding of the City Traffic Engineer, it shall be unlawful
to stop, stand or park a vehicle for any purpose or length of time other than for
the expeditious loading and unloading of passengers from a licensed tour bus, shuttle
bus or limo in any place marked as a Tour Bus, Shuttle Bus or Limo Loading Zone during
hours where the provisions applicable to such zones are in effect. In no case shall
the stop for the loading or unloading of passengers exceed thirty minutes.
(Ord. 5095 § 20, 1998: Ord. 3990 § 11, 1996: Ord. 3011 § 1, 1982: prior code § 10-8-11)

11.46.010.title: School zones designated
11.46.010.text:
Those portions of streets that are described in Schedule 27-I, copies of which shall
be maintained for public inspection in the offices of the City Clerk and the City
Traffic Engineer and may be amended from time to time by written finding of the City
Traffic Engineer that are contiguous to school sites, are hereby designated as "school
zones."
(Ord. 3990 § 12, 1996: Ord. 3212 § 4, 1986)

11.46.020.title: Crossing guards or safety patrol
11.46.020.text:
The Metropolitan Police Department is authorized to appoint crossing guards or a school
safety patrol to direct traffic at school crossings by means of lawful orders, signs,
or semaphores, and such persons shall wear a distinctive garb or insignia indicating
such appointment. No minor other than a member of the school safety patrol shall direct
or attempt to direct traffic unless authorized to do so by a Police Officer.
(Ord. 2203 § 37, 1981: Ord. 927 § 1 (part), 1961: prior code § 10-28-1)

11.46.030.title: Stopping at signal or flag
11.46.030.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person driving or operating, propelling or causing to
be propelled, any vehicle, to fail to stop not less than fifty feet from the nearest
side of a school pedestrian lane where any signal device, flagman or other person
is stationed, giving warning that children are about to cross or are crossing the
street; and it is further declared unlawful to proceed until such signal has stopped,
raised, or been removed, or the flagman or person stationed at such pedestrian lane
has given a signal to go, or has left the locality.
(Ord. 927 § 1 (part), 1961: prior code § 10-28-2)
Cross reference—
For other provisions within this Code on school zones, see Chapter 11.16 and Section 11.52.130.

11.48.010.title: Unladen weight defined
11.48.010.text:
As used in this Chapter, "unladen weight" means the weight of any vehicle without
load, but fully equipped with such accessories and appliances belonging to and used
by such vehicle in the transportation of persons or property.
(Ord. 1278 § 31 (part), 1967: Ord. 1021 § 16(1), 1963: prior code § 10-29-16(A))

11.48.020.title: Governments and utilities
11.48.020.text:
The provisions of this Chapter shall not apply to any specially designed equipment
operated by any duly franchised public utility or governmental agency when such equipment
is required in providing an essential public service.
(Ord. 1278 § 31 (part), 1967: Ord. 1021 § 16(4), 1963: prior code § 10-29-16(D))

11.48.030.title: Weight limit—Route use required
11.48.030.text:
Notwithstanding any of the other provisions of this Chapter, no vehicle in excess
of eight thousand pounds unladen weight shall be operated or moved upon any public
street, highway or alley within the City, except upon truck routes, as set forth in
Schedule 29-II. The City Council may impose specific restrictions upon the use of
any of the enumerated truck routes, where such restrictions are deemed warranted in
order to promote the health, safety and welfare of the public. Any such restrictions
shall be included in Schedule 29-II. Copies of Schedule 29-II shall be maintained
for public inspection in the offices of the City Clerk and the City Traffic Engineer
and may be amended from time to time by resolution of the City Council. Such vehicles
may also travel upon temporary truck routes hereafter designated by the Department
of Public Works pursuant to Section 11.48.070. Travel by any vehicle in excess of eight thousand pounds unladen weight on a non-truck
route may occur only if merchandise, freight or other supplies are to be picked up
by or delivered from such vehicle, or such vehicle is required in the performance
or service, repair, construction or similar essential use; provided, however, that
in any such event the vehicle shall use the shortest possible route from a designated
truck route to the point of pickup, delivery or essential use and shall return therefrom
to the nearest designated truck route; provided further, that the additional restrictions
set out in Sections 11.48.040, 11.48.050 and 11.48.060 shall apply.
(Ord. 3888 § 1, 1995: Ord. 1589 § 17 (part), 1972: Ord. 1384 § 8, 1969; Ord. 1339
§ 7, 1968; Ord. 1278 §§ 31 (part), 32, 33, 1967: Ord. 1021 § 16(2) (part): prior code
§ 10-29-16(B) (part))

11.48.040.title: Pickups and deliveries off routes
11.48.040.text:
No vehicle in excess of eight thousand pounds unladen weight shall be operated or
moved upon any street unless the use of such route is required in the pick-up or delivery
of merchandise, freight or other supplies or in some essential use at some point not
served by a truck route but served by such direct route street.
(Ord. 1589 § 17 (part), 1972: Ord. 1278 § 31 (part), 1967: Ord. 1021 § 16 (2)(a),
1963: prior code § 10-29-16(B)(1))

11.48.050.title: Nighttime trucking permits
11.48.050.text:
No vehicle in excess of eight thousand pounds unladen weight shall be operated or
moved upon any street (other than a truck route), in any residence district between
the hours of seven p.m. and six a.m.; provided, however, that the Department of Public
Works may, at its discretion, upon application in writing, issue a special permit
in writing authorizing the applicant to operate or move such vehicle between the hours
of seven p.m. and six a.m. In issuing such permit, the Department may impose such
conditions thereon, such as routes to be followed, time of operation or movement,
or other matters, as it deems necessary or desirable.
(Ord. 5017 § 2, 1997: Ord. 5011 § 1, 1997: Ord. 1589 § 17 (part), 1972: Ord. 1278
§ 31 (part), 1967: Ord. 1021 § 16(2)(b), 1963: prior code § 10-29-16(B)(2))

11.48.060.title: Streets between
11.48.060.text:
Streets, other than truck routes, shall not be used as through routes from one truck
route to another unless pick-up, delivery or essential use is required enroute.
(Ord. 1589 § 17 (part), 1972: Ord. 1278 § 31 (part), 1967: Ord. 1021 § 16(2)(c), 1963:
prior code § 10-29-16(B)(3))

11.48.070.title: Temporary designation
11.48.070.text:
The Department of Public Works shall have authority to designate additional, temporary
truck routes for the purpose of directing and controlling traffic along necessary
detours or between designated truck routes and construction projects or other areas
where commercial vehicles are required to be employed over extended periods of time.
Such temporary routes, when so designated, shall be posted with appropriate signs
as temporary truck routes, and the use of such routes shall be subject to the same
conditions as set forth in this Chapter for permanent truck routes.
(Ord. 1278 § 31 (part), 1967: Ord. 1021 § 16(3), 1963: prior code § 10-29- 16(C))

11.48.080.title: Posting—Street classifications
11.48.080.text:
The truck routes provided for in this Chapter shall be posted with adequate signs
indicating that such routes are truck routes and shall, in general, be the streets
classified major, primary or secondary thoroughfares as designated on the official
Master Plan of Streets and Highways of the City.
(Ord. 1278 § 31 (part), 1967: Ord. 1021 § 16(5), 1963: prior code § 10-29-16(E))

11.48.090.title: Reserved
11.48.090.text:
Editor's note—
Ord. No. 6240, § 2, adopted March 20, 2013, repealed § 11.48.090, which pertained
to heavy trucks in residence districts and derived from prior code § 10-29-17; Ord.
No. 1021, 1963 and Ord. No. 5319, 2001.

11.48.100.title: Over-length vehicle operation—Permit required when
11.48.100.text:
No person shall operate any vehicle, or any combination of vehicles coupled together,
which exceed seventy feet in length upon any street, highway or alley within the City
except as follows:
(A)
Such over-length vehicles are allowed on those routes described in Schedule 29-1,
and as may be amended from time to time by resolution of the Board. Said Schedule
29-1 shall be kept in the office of the City Clerk for public inspection, and copies
thereof may be obtained from the City Clerk or from the Traffic Engineer for the City.
(B)
Such over-length vehicles are allowed on those routes or streets, other than those
described in Schedule 29-1, for which the Department of Public Works has issued a
permit. Upon receipt of a written application and the payment of a fifty dollar application
fee, the Department of Public Works may issue a temporary permit authorizing the operation
of such over-length vehicle on the routes or streets stated therein; provided, that
the Department of Public Works determines that such operation will not unduly threaten
the safety and convenience of persons or property. Such permit may contain limitations
as to the origin, destination, time or specific routes of travel, and such other limitations
as the Director of Public Works considers necessary to protect the interest of the
public. If an application is denied, the applicant may appeal the denial to the Board
by filing a written notice of appeal with the City Clerk within fifteen days following
notice of denial. The notice of denial becomes effective upon its deposit in the U.S.
mails addressed to the applicant at the address as shown on the application.
(Ord. No. 6816, § 112, 8-17-22; Ord. 3054 § 1, 1983)

11.50.010.title: State manual—Adopted—Conformance
11.50.010.text:
The "Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices," in the version adopted by the Nevada
Department of Transportation pursuant to NRS 484B.430 and NAC 408.411 (hereinafter
referred to as the "MUTCD"), shall govern the operations of all contractors, subcontractors
and other persons who are engaged in work subject to the MUTCD within the corporate
limits of the City.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 28, 6-18-14; Ord. 5570 § 1, 2003: Ord. 2107 § 2, 1980: prior code
§ 10-30-1)

11.50.030.title: Violation—Notice
11.50.030.text:
Violation of any regulation contained in the MUTCD or elsewhere shall be corrected
within two hours by the violator, after receipt of written notice from the City Traffic
Engineer or his duly authorized representative that a violation exists.
(Ord. 5570 § 3, 2003: Ord. 1563 § 1 (part), 1972: Ord. 1253 § 1 (part), 1966: Ord.
1037 § 5, 1963: prior code § 10-30-4)

11.50.040.title: Violation—City correction—Stop-work order
11.50.040.text:
(A)
The City is authorized to charge fees related to the placement of traffic barricades
in accordance with the fee schedule established pursuant to LVMC 13.40.050. The fees may include, without limitation, fees relating to the approval and renewal
of traffic barricade plans, and the fees described in this Section.
(B)
In the case of a violation referred to in LVMC 11.50.030, failure on the part of the violator to correct any such deficiencies within the
two-hour period described in that Section shall be sufficient authorization for the
City to correct the existing deficiencies. The City Traffic Engineer or designee is
authorized to charge the violator a noncompliance correction fee in accordance with
the fee schedule established pursuant to LVMC 13.40.050. The City Traffic Engineer, in his discretion, may order a cessation of work on the
operation with respect to which such deficiencies exist until the same shall have
been corrected.
(C)
Where barricades or other traffic-control devices are left within the travel lanes
or sidewalk areas of a right-of-way for longer than the period authorized by a permit,
the City is authorized to charge a noncompliance correction fee and lane/sidewalk
rental fees, including fees charged on a per-unit of equipment basis, in accordance
with the fee schedule established pursuant to LVMC 13.40.050.
(Ord. No. 6879, § 11, 9-4-24; Ord. 5570 § 4, 2003: Ord. 1563 § 1 (part), 1972: Ord.
1253 § 1 (part), 1966: Ord. 1037 § 6, 1963: prior code § 10-30-5)

11.50.050.title: Nonconforming devices
11.50.050.text:
(A)
No person shall place, maintain, or display upon or in view of any construction site,
any temporary traffic-control device which, in the opinion of the City Traffic Engineer
or his designee is deemed as substandard, damaged, worn out, faded, or otherwise nonconforming.
(B)
Any temporary traffic-control device which is in violation of this Section shall be
red-tagged, and shall be corrected within four hours by the violator after receipt
of notice of said red tag.
(C)
Failure on the part of the violator to correct any such deficiencies within said four-hour
period shall constitute a misdemeanor.
(Ord. 5570 § 5, 2003: Ord. 1563 § 1 (part), 1972: Ord. 1278 § 34, 1967: prior code
§ 10-30-7)

11.50.060.title: Interference with barricades, signs or lights
11.50.060.text:
(A)
No person shall, without lawful authority, attempt to or in fact alter, deface, injure,
knock down, damage or remove any barricades or signs or warning lights that have been
placed upon or in the area of temporary traffic control or detour or construction
zone.
(B)
Any person who violates this Section is guilty of a misdemeanor.
(Ord. 1563 § 1 (part), 1972: prior code § 10-30-8)

11.50.070.title: Violation—Penalty
11.50.070.text:
Every person, company, contractor or subcontractor violating any of the provisions
of this Chapter, either personally or by his or its agent or employee shall, upon
conviction thereof, be punished by the penalty provided for misdemeanors.
(Ord. 1563 § 1 (part), 1972: Ord. 1253 § 1 (part), 1966: prior code § 10-30-6)

11.52.010.title: Necessary or directed stops excepted
11.52.010.text:
The provisions of this Chapter prohibiting the standing or parking of a vehicle shall
apply at all times or at those times herein specified or as indicated on official
signs except when it is necessary to stop a vehicle to avoid conflict with other traffic
or in compliance with the direction of a Police Officer or official traffic-control
device.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 83: prior code § 10-17-22)
Cross reference—
For provisions on loading zones, see Ch. 11.44 of this Code. For provisions on taxi stands and bus stops, see Ch. 11.60. For provisions on metered parking, see Ch. 11.54.

11.52.020.title: Other regulations apply
11.52.020.text:
The provisions of this Chapter imposing a time limit on parking shall not relieve
any person from the duty to observe other and more restrictive provisions prohibiting
or limiting the stopping, standing or parking of vehicles in specified places or at
specified times.
(1949 code Ch. 36 § 84: prior code § 10-17-23)

11.52.030.title: Curb marking color code
11.52.030.text:
The parking of vehicles is prohibited or restricted in certain zones as set forth
in this Section. The location of such zones shall be established by posting appropriate
signage or other durable markings, by painting curbs or the edges of road surfaces
in accordance with the colors listed below, or by a combination thereof:
(A)
Red indicates no stopping, standing or parking, whether or not the vehicle is attended
and whether or not the engine or motor is running, subject to the following:
(1)
Except as provided in this Subsection, a curb or road surface edge which is painted
red indicates no parking, whether or not accompanied by signage to that effect.
(2)
When the location is accompanied by signage which indicates that parking is limited
to tour buses, shuttle buses and limos, those vehicles may park for a period up to
thirty minutes for the loading or unloading of passengers.
(3)
When the location is accompanied by signage which indicates that parking is limited
to RTC buses, those vehicles may park for a period up to thirty minutes for the loading
or unloading of passengers.
(4)
Armored cars and emergency vehicles may park at such locations for the period necessary
to conduct their business, whether or not there is accompanying signage so indicating.
(5)
At locations where a drop box for U.S. mail is adjacent to a curb or road surface
painted red, a person may stop for the period of time necessary to expeditiously deposit
mail in such a drop box.
(B)
Yellow indicates a zone for:
(1)
Commercial vehicles to stop, stand or park for the purpose of loading or unloading
freight in accordance with the conditions and times posted on an accompanying sign;
and
(2)
Taxicabs to stop, stand, park for the purpose of loading, unloading or waiting for
passengers in accordance with the conditions and times posted on an accompanying sign.
(C)
White indicates time-limited and other limited parking, as described in LVMC 11.44.020, 11.44.030, 11.44.040 and 11.52.270, and in accordance with the conditions and times posted on an accompanying sign.
(D)
Gray indicates that previous parking restrictions have been removed and that stopping,
standing or parking is permitted.
(E)
Blue indicates parking for handicapped persons (driver or passenger) for a period
not to exceed four hours, whether or not the time limit is posted, but only regarding:
(1)
A handicap space which is properly posted pursuant to LVMC 11.52.135; and
(2)
A vehicle which displays a valid handicapped permit or license plate.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 29, 6-18-14; Ord. 5095 § 22, 1998: Ord. 3829 § 3, 1994: Ord. 1865
§ 2, 1977; Ord. 1293 § 4, 1967: Ord. 750 § 6, 1957: prior code § 10-17-21)

11.52.040.title: Parallel norm—Distance from curb
11.52.040.text:
Except as otherwise provided in this Chapter:
(A)
No person shall stand or park a vehicle in a roadway other than parallel with the
edge of the roadway headed in the direction of lawful traffic movement.
(B)
No person shall stand or park a vehicle in a roadway with the wheels of the vehicle
farther than eighteen inches from the curb or edge of the roadway.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 30, 6-18-14; Ord. 3000 § 2, 1982: Ord. 1278 § 18, 1967: Ord. 170
§ 24(3), 1931: prior code § 10-17-1)

11.52.050.title: Obstruction of traffic
11.52.050.text:
No person shall park any vehicle upon a street or alley, in such a manner or under
such conditions as to leave available less than ten feet of the width of the roadway
or alley for free movement of vehicular traffic.
(Ord. 3089 § 3, 1983: prior code § 10-17-10)

11.52.060.title: Projection into street
11.52.060.text:
In no case shall any part of any vehicle, part of the load of such vehicle or trailer
attached to such vehicle, project into the street more than fifteen feet measured
on a line at right angles to the curb.
(Ord. 170 § 26 (part), 1931: prior code § 10-17-19)

11.52.070.title: Angle parking—Determination authority
11.52.070.text:
The City Traffic Engineer shall determine upon what streets angle parking shall be
permitted, and shall provide signage or other markings to indicate where such parking
is permitted. Where angle parking is permitted, no person shall stand or park a vehicle
unless the front of the vehicle is pointed toward the direction of lawful traffic
movement.
(Ord. No. 6829, § 4, 2-1-23; Ord. No. 6326, § 31, 6-18-14; Ord. 170 § 28, 1931: prior
code § 10-17-2)

11.52.090.title: Loading permits
11.52.090.text:
The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to issue special permits to permit the backing
of a vehicle to the curb or building in alleys for the purposes of loading or unloading
merchandise or materials subject to the terms and conditions of such permit. Such
permits may be issued either to the owner or lessee of real property or to the owner
of the vehicle and shall grant to such person the privilege as therein stated and
authorized herein. The City Traffic Engineer shall immediately provide notice to the
Parking Services Division of the Department of Economic and Urban Development of the
issuance of a permit under this Section.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 32, 6-18-14; Ord. No. 6184, § 9, 3-21-12; Ord. 3989 § 10, 1996:
Ord. 3829 § 4, 1994: Ord. 1278 § 19, 1967: Ord. 981 § 3, 1962: prior code § 10-17-4)

11.52.110.title: Locking, setting brake, turning wheels
11.52.110.text:
No person driving or in charge of a motor vehicle shall permit it to stand unattended
within the City without first stopping the engine, locking the ignition, removing
the key and effectively setting the brake thereon and, when standing upon any grade,
turning the front wheels to the curb or side of the highway.
(Ord. 2203 § 25, 1981: prior code § 10-17-6)

11.52.120.title: Locking in persons
11.52.120.text:
No person shall leave standing a locked vehicle in which there is any person who cannot
escape readily therefrom.
(Prior code § 10-17-20)

11.52.130.title: Posted places
11.52.130.text:
(A)
No person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle except when necessary to avoid conflict
with other traffic in compliance with law or the directions of a police officer or
a traffic control device, in any of the following places:
(1)
Except as otherwise described in Paragraph (3) below, at any place where official
signs or the painting of curbs or road surfaces, or any combination thereof prohibit
or restrict stopping, standing or parking for a period longer or purpose other than
is permitted by such signs or painting;
(2)
At any place or in any space adjacent to a curb which has been designated and posted
as a fire lane pursuant to the City's Fire Code, whether the vehicle is attended or
unattended and whether the location is on public or private property;
(3)
At any location on a highway, street or public thoroughfare where official signs have
been posted to prohibit or restrict stopping, standing or parking based upon a determination
that such activity is dangerous or would unduly interfere with the free movement of
traffic, including adjacent to any curb or road surface which is painted red and is
posted with signage indicating "NO STOPPING, STANDING OR PARKING"; "EMERGENCY VEHICLES
ONLY"; or "ARMORED CARS ONLY";
(4)
Within the following distances of any fire hydrant, whether or not the location is
posted with a sign, whether or not the adjacent curb or roadway surface is painted
red, and whether the location is on public or private property:
(a)
At a location where parallel parking is permitted, fifteen feet;
(b)
At a location where angle parking is permitted or no parking is permitted, twenty
feet;
(5)
In front of any sidewalk elevator or chute or within a space of five feet on each
side of such sidewalk elevator or chute;
(6)
On or blocking a sidewalk;
(7)
In front of or within five feet of a public or private driveway; provided, however,
that this provision does not apply to the parking of a vehicle in or near a private
driveway by a person who owns or is in control of that driveway, or who is a family
member or invitee of the person so owning or controlling the driveway;
(8)
Within fifty feet of the nearest rail of a railroad track;
(9)
Within twenty feet of a driveway entrance to any fire station and, on the side of
a public street or thoroughfare opposite the entrance to any fire station, within
seventy-five feet of such station;
(10)
On the street side of any vehicle which is stopped, standing or parked at the edge
or curb of a highway (i.e., to "double park");
(11)
Within fifteen feet of an intersection;
(12)
Within twenty feet of any marked crosswalk;
(13)
Within thirty feet of any official traffic control signal or device located at the
side of any roadway, highway, street or other public thoroughfare:
(14)
On any traffic lane designated and posted as a bike lane;
(15)
In such a manner as to create an undue obstruction to or interference with traffic,
a hazardous condition for pedestrians, or a visual obstruction for motorists; or
(16)
Upon any bridge or other elevated structure or within any tunnel or underpass.
(B)
The provisions of Paragraphs (1) and (7) of Subsection (A) of this Section do not
apply to a United States Postal Service vehicle while it is being operated on official
business.
(Ord. No. 6437, § 10, 8-5-15; Ord. No. 6326, § 33, 6-18-14; Ord. 5095 § 23, 1998:
Ord. 3829 § 5, 1994: Ord. 3498 § 2, 1990: Ord. 3346 § 1, 1988: Ord. 3089 § 4, 1983:
Ord. 2203 § 25, 1981; Ord. 1925 § 1, 1978; Ord. 1293 § 3, 1967: Ord. 170 § 24, 1931:
prior code § 10-17-7)

11.52.135.title: Handicapped parking
11.52.135.text:
(A)
Any parking space designated for the handicapped must be indicated by a sign:
(1)
Bearing the international symbol of access with or without the words "Parking," "Handicapped
Parking," "Handicapped Parking Only," "or "Reserved for the Handicapped," or any other
word or combination of words indicating that the space is designated for the handicapped;
(2)
Stating "Minimum fine of two hundred fifty dollars for use by others" or equivalent
words; and
(3)
The bottom of which must not be less than four feet above the ground.
(B)
In addition to the requirements of Subsection (A), a parking space designated for
the handicapped which:
(1)
Is designed for the exclusive use of a vehicle with a side-loading wheelchair lift;
and
(2)
Is located in a parking lot with sixty or more parking spaces,
→ must be indicated by a sign using a combination of words to state that the space
is for the exclusive use of a vehicle with a side-loading wheelchair lift.
(C)
If a parking space is designed for the use of a vehicle with a side-loading wheelchair
lift, the space which is immediately adjacent and intended for use in the loading
and unloading of a wheelchair into or out of such a vehicle must be indicated by a
sign:
(1)
Stating "No Parking" or similar words which indicate that parking in such a space
is prohibited;
(2)
Stating "Minimum fine of two hundred fifty dollars for violation" or similar words
indicating that the minimum fine for parking in such a space is two hundred fifty
dollars; and
(3)
The bottom of which must not be less than four feet above the ground.
(D)
A person shall not park a vehicle in a space designated for the handicapped by a sign
that meets the requirements of Subsection (A), whether on public or privately owned
property, unless he is eligible to do so and the vehicle displays:
(1)
A special license plate or plates issued pursuant to NRS 482.384;
(2)
A special or temporary parking placard issued pursuant to NRS 482.384;
(3)
A special or temporary parking sticker issued pursuant to NRS 482.384;
(4)
A special license plate or plates, a special or temporary parking sticker, or a special
or temporary parking placard displaying the international symbol of access issued
by another state or foreign country; or
(5)
A special license plate or plates for a disabled veteran issued pursuant to NRS 482.377.
(E)
Except as otherwise provided in this Subsection (E), a person shall not park a vehicle
in a space that is reserved for the exclusive use of a vehicle with a side-loading
wheelchair lift and is designated for the handicapped by a sign that meets the requirements
of Subsection (B), whether on public or privately owned property, unless:
(1)
He is eligible to do so;
(2)
The vehicle displays the special license plates or placard set forth in Subsection
(D); and
(3)
The vehicle is equipped with a side-loading wheelchair lift.
→ A person who meets the requirements of Paragraphs (1) and (2) of this Subsection
(E) may park a vehicle that is not equipped with a side-loading wheelchair lift in
such a parking space if the space is in a parking lot with fewer than sixty parking
spaces.
(F)
A person shall not park in a space which:
(1)
Is immediately adjacent to a space designed for use by a vehicle with a side-loading
wheelchair lift; and
(2)
Is designated as a space in which parking is prohibited by a sign that meets the requirements
of Subsection (C),
→ whether on public or privately owned property.
(G)
A person shall not use a plate, sticker or placard described in Subsection (D) to
park in a space designated for the handicapped unless he is a person with a permanent
disability, disability of moderate duration or temporary disability, a disabled veteran,
or the driver of a vehicle in which any such person is a passenger.
(H)
A person with a permanent disability, disability of moderate duration or temporary
disability to whom a:
(1)
Special license plate, or a special or temporary parking sticker, has been issued
pursuant to NRS 482.384 shall not allow any other person to park the vehicle or motorcycle
displaying the special license plate or special or temporary parking sticker in a
space designated for the handicapped unless the person with the permanent disability,
disability of moderate duration or temporary disability is a passenger in the vehicle
or on the motorcycle, or is being picked up or dropped off by the driver of the vehicle
or motorcycle, at the time that the vehicle or motorcycle is parked in the space designated
for the handicapped.
(2)
Special or temporary parking placard has been issued pursuant to NRS 482.384 shall
not allow any other person to park the vehicle which displays the special or temporary
parking placard in a space designated for the handicapped unless the person with the
permanent disability, disability of moderate duration or temporary disability is a
passenger in the vehicle, or is being picked up or dropped off by the driver of the
vehicle, at the time that it is parked in the space designated for the handicapped.
(Ord. 5785 § 4, 2005)

11.52.136.title: Parking in an access aisle—Prohibited
11.52.136.text:
No person shall park a vehicle in an access aisle.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 34, 6-4-14)

11.52.140.title: Prohibited places
11.52.140.text:
The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to determine and to designate by "No Parking"
or other appropriate signs or markings:
(A)
Places not exceeding one hundred feet in length in which the stopping, standing or
parking of vehicles would create an especially hazardous condition or would cause
unusual delay in traffic;
(B)
Places on streets with an actual pavement width of less than thirty-two feet in which
on-street parking would leave insufficient clear travel area for two-directional traffic.
(Ord. 5095 § 24, 1998: Ord. 3583 § 1, 1991: Ord. 3000 § 4, 1982; 1949 Code Ch. 36
§ 75: prior code § 10-17-18)

11.52.150.title: Occupancy permit
11.52.150.text:
The Parking Division of the Department of Economic and Urban Development may issue
to a person, company, contractor or agency, upon application therefor, a parking space
occupancy permit authorizing the occupancy of one or more non-metered parking spaces
on City streets for extended periods of time in order to provide supplies, materials,
or services, on a temporary basis, in the immediate area of the parking spaces. Issuance
of such an occupancy permit shall be in the discretion of the Parking Division. In
connection with the issuance of an occupancy permit, the City is authorized to charge
an occupancy permit fee, which shall be paid by the applicant before any permit is
issued or space reserved for the applicant. The amount of the occupancy permit fee
shall be determined by the Parking Division and shall be in an amount that represents
the costs of processing the application and occupancy permit.
(Ord. No. 6829, § 5, 2-1-23)

11.52.180.title: Alleys—Parking prohibited when
11.52.180.text:
(A)
When signs are posted giving notice thereof, no person shall stop, stand or park a
vehicle in an alley described in Schedule 17-I, a copy of which is to be maintained
for public inspection in the office of the City Clerk and the City Traffic Engineer,
and such other alleys as may be added to the schedule by written finding of the City
Traffic Engineer, except for the following vehicles, while actually engaged in loading
or unloading heavy or voluminous freight, cargo or other goods:
(1)
Commercial vehicles whose commercial nature is evident from the type of vehicle; or
(2)
Vehicles which have commercially-printed markings on the exterior of the vehicle clearly
identifying the commercial use of the vehicle.
(B)
When signs are posted giving notice thereof, no person shall park a vehicle at any
time in alleys or portions thereof described in Schedule 17-II, a copy of which is
to be maintained for public inspection in the office of the City Clerk and the City
Traffic Engineer, and such other alleys as may be added to the schedule by written
finding of the City Traffic Engineer.
(C)
A vehicle otherwise lawfully parked in an alley shall not park for a greater period
than thirty minutes within any one-hour period.
(Ord. 5870 § 13, 2006: Ord. 3990 § 13, 1996: Ord. 3829 § 6, 1994: Ord. 3000 § 3, 1982:
Ord. 1589 § 6, 1972: Ord. 1534 § 4, 1971; Ord. 1459 § 8, 1970; Ord. 1169 § 3, 1965:
Ord. 999 § 2, 1962: Ord. 747 § 1, 1957: Ord. 274 §§ 5, 6, 1942: Ord. 170 § 26a, 1931:
prior code § 10-17-12)

11.52.240.title: Streets of prohibited parking—Schedule 17-III
11.52.240.text:
Except as provided in LVMC 11.52.030, when signs are erected or the adjacent curbing or edge of road is painted red giving
notice thereof, no person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle at any time upon any
streets or parts of streets described in Schedule 17-III, a copy of which is to be
maintained for public inspection in the offices of the City Clerk and the City Traffic
Engineer, and such other additions, deletions, corrections or amendments that may
be made to said Schedule by written finding of the City Traffic Engineer.
(Ord. 5095 § 25, 1998: Ord. 3990 § 14, 1996: Ord. 3829 § 7, 1994: Ord. 1604 § 1, 1973:
Ord. 1589 § 7 1973: Ord. 1534 § 5 1971; Ord. 1459 § 9, 1970: Ord. 1423 § 2, 1969;
Ord. 1384 § 2, 1969; Ord. 1339 § 2, 1968; Ord. 1293 § 5, 1967; Ord. 1278 § 22, 1967:
Ord. 1169 § 4, 1965: prior code § 10-17-24)

11.52.245.title: Streets of prohibited parking—Schedule 17-IIIa
11.52.245.text:
Except as provided in LVMC 11.52.030, when signs are erected or the adjacent curbing or edge of road is painted giving
notice thereof, no person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle at any time upon any
of the streets or parts of streets described in Schedule 17-IIIa, except for those
vehicles which are specifically permitted to park at those locations in accordance
with the posted signage and the terms of Schedule 17-IIIa. Said Schedule is to be
maintained for public inspection in the office of the City Clerk and the City Traffic
Engineer, including such other additions, deletions, corrections or amendments that
may be made to said Schedule by written finding of the City Traffic Engineer.
(Ord. 5095 § 26, 1998: Ord. 3990 § 15, 1996: Ord. 3829 § 8, 1994)

11.52.250.title: Hours of prohibited parking
11.52.250.text:
Except as provided in LVMC 11.52.030, when signs are erected or the adjacent curbing or edge of road is painted giving
notice thereof, no person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle upon any of the streets
or parts of streets or within the district described in Schedule 17-IV during the
hours specified on the posted signage and in Schedule 17-IV on any day except Sundays
and public holidays. A copy of Schedule 17-IV is to be maintained for public inspection
in the offices of the City Clerk and City Traffic Engineer. Said Schedule may be amended,
corrected, added to, or deleted from by written finding of the City Traffic Engineer.
(Ord. 5095 § 27, 1998: Ord. 3990 § 16, 1996: Ord. 1589 § 8, 1973: prior code § 10-17-25)

11.52.260.title: Hours of general prohibition
11.52.260.text:
Except as provided in LVMC 11.52.030, when signs are erected or the adjacent curbing or edge of road is painted red giving
notice thereof, no person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle upon any of the streets
or parts of streets or within the district described in Schedule 17-V during the hours
specified on the posted signage and in Schedule 17-V, a copy of which is to be maintained
for public inspection in the offices of the City Clerk and the City Traffic Engineer.
Said Schedule may be amended, corrected, added to, or deleted from by written finding
of the City Traffic Engineer.
(Ord. 5095 § 28, 1998: Ord. 3990 § 17, 1996: Ord. 1589 § 9, 1973: Ord. 1459 § 10,
1970: Ord. 1423 § 3, 1969; Ord. 1339 § 3, 1968; Ord. 1169 § 5,* 1965: prior code §
10-17-26)
Editor's note—
Editor's Note: Ord. 1169 has two sections numbered 5.

11.52.270.title: Time-limited parking
11.52.270.text:
When signs are erected on each block or the adjacent curbing or edge of road is painted
giving notice thereof, no person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle upon any of the
streets described in Schedule 17-VI, or within any district or time limited parking
zone described therein, for a period longer than the parking limit as posted and as
specified in Schedule 17-VI. The prohibition contained in this Section applies during
the hours the time-limited parking is in effect as posted and as specified in Schedule
17-VI, except that a person may park a vehicle at such location for a period not to
exceed four hours if the person lawfully displays on the vehicle a special or temporary
handicap parking permit or plate. The prohibition contained in this Section does not
apply on any day which is excepted and posted, as specified in Schedule 17-VI. A copy
of Schedule 17-VI shall be maintained for public inspection in the offices of the
City Clerk and the City Traffic Engineer. Said Schedule may be amended, corrected,
added to, or deleted from by written finding of the City Traffic Engineer.
(Ord. 5095 § 29, 1998: Ord. 3990 § 18, 1996: Ord. 1589 § 10, 1973: Ord. 1534 § 6,
1971; Ord. 1459 § 11, 1970: Ord. 1423 § 4, 1969; Ord. 1384 § 3, 1969; Ord. 1339 §
4, 1968; Ord. 1293 § 6, 1967; Ord. 1278 § 23, 1967; Ord. 1169 § 5,* 1965: Ord. 170
§ 26 (part), 1931: prior code § 10-17-27)
Editor's note—
Ord. 1169 has two sections numbered 5.

11.52.280.title: Signposting required
11.52.280.text:
Whenever by any provision of LVMC 11.52.030 to 11.52.270, inclusive, any parking time limit is imposed or parking is prohibited on designated
streets, the City Traffic Engineer shall cause to be placed the appropriate signs,
meters, markings or curb or surface painting giving notice thereof, and no such provision
shall be effective unless said signs, meters, markings or curb or surface painting
are in place at the time of any alleged offense.
(Ord. 5095 § 30, 1998: Ord. 3829 § 9, 1994: 1949 code Ch. 36 § 79: prior code § 10-17-28)

11.52.290.title: Authority to designate handicapped parking
11.52.290.text:
The City Council or the City Traffic Engineer may from time to time designate zones
or spaces on any public street or other public place or in any publicly owned parking
lot to be limited to parking for the handicapped for a period not to exceed four hours.
(Ord. 3498 § 3, 1990: Ord. 3346 § 3, 1988)

11.52.300.title: Nighttime and nonmotor vehicles
11.52.300.text:
Except for a motor vehicle, no person shall park any vehicle on any street for a period
of time longer than thirty minutes between the hours of one a.m. and six a.m. of any
day.
(Ord. 1278 § 20, 1967: prior code § 10-17-32)

11.52.305.title: Commercial vehicles, recreational vehicles and trailers
11.52.305.text:
(A)
Except as otherwise provided in this Section or as permitted by posted sign, it is
unlawful for a person to stand, park or store, upon any street adjacent to a residence
district, public school or public park, a commercial vehicle, recreational vehicle,
trailer, or any combination of vehicle and trailer having an overall length of twenty-four
feet or more or an unladen weight in excess of eight thousand pounds. For purposes
of the preceding sentence, a "residence district" means the territory contiguous to
a street, not comprising a business district, in which the parcels abutting such street
for a distance of three hundred feet or more are mainly occupied by dwellings or by
dwellings and buildings in use for residence.
(B)
The provisions of Subsection (A) do not apply to a commercial vehicle that is:
(1)
Parked in front of property from which or to which goods or passengers are being picked
up or delivered, but only for that period of time during which goods or passengers
are being expeditiously loaded or unloaded; or
(2)
Being used in conjunction with the performance of service, repair, construction or
similar essential use within the immediate neighborhood.
(C)
A person may park a recreational vehicle upon a residential street in front of property
from which or to which passengers and travel items will be loaded or unloaded, but
only:
(1)
For a period not to exceed forty-eight consecutive hours; and
(2)
In accordance with a permit issued by the Parking Services Division of the Department
of Economic and Urban Development in accordance with Subsection (D).
For purposes of this Subsection (C) and Subsection (D), "recreational vehicle" means
any vehicle or trailer, or vehicle-trailer combination, that is designed, maintained
and used as a travel trailer, camper, motor home, tent trailer, or camping trailer.
(D)
A permit issued for recreational vehicle parking described in Subsection (C):
(1)
Shall specify the location and vehicle to which it pertains, the date and time permitted
parking may begin, and the date and time the permit expires;
(2)
Must be displayed in or on the vehicle in a conspicuous location that is clearly visible
from the street;
(3)
Is valid only for the vehicle, location and times specified;
(4)
Is not valid with reference to the same recreational vehicle more than six times within
any three-month period;
(5)
Is not valid for any period that commences less than seventy-two hours after a previous
permit for the same recreational vehicle has expired; and
(6)
May be revoked for abuse, misuse, ineligibility or other good cause.
(E)
It is unlawful for a person to stand, park or store a mobile billboard upon any street
at a location within five hundred feet of a dwelling, including any apartment unit
or residential condominium. For purposes of this Subsection (E), "mobile billboard"
means one or more sign structures that are mounted on a vehicle or trailer and are
used for general advertising or advertising for hire. The term does not include signs
that are displayed or installed on:
(1)
A bus, taxicab or similar vehicle that is used primarily for the purpose of transporting
multiple passengers; or
(2)
A vehicle operated in the normal course of the vehicle owner's business, if the signs
contain advertising or identifying information directly related to the business and
are not used to display advertising unrelated to that business.
(Ord. No. 6574, § 1, 4-19-17; Ord. No. 6240, § 1, 3-20-13; Ord. No. 6062, § 1, 10-21-09;
Ord. 5870 § 14, 2006: Ord. 5434 § 8, 2002: Ord. 5319 § 3, 2001: Ord. 5095 § 32, 1998)

11.52.310.title: City lots—Regulation authority
11.52.310.text:
The City Manager is authorized to limit parking within City parking facilities to
certain specified persons, for designated purposes, and for certain specific lengths
of time, and to erect signs giving notice of such limitations. In any such facility,
those limitations may include, among other things, the requirement to pay a fee for
parking that is collected upon entrance or exit.
(Ord. No. 6703, § 9, 10-2-19; Ord. No. 6629, § 1, 8-15-18; Ord. 1839 § 1 (part), 1976:
Ord. 1692 § 1, 1974: Ord. 1664 § 1 (part), 1973: Ord. 1331 § 2 (part), 1968: prior
code § 10-17-33(A))

11.52.315.title: City lots—Markings
11.52.315.text:
The City Manager or designee is authorized to cause individual parking spaces within
City parking facilities to be marked, either by means of painted lines or other durable
markings. Where such parking spaces have been so marked, it is unlawful to park any
vehicle:
(A)
In such a way that the vehicle is not entirely within the limits of a single space
so designated; or
(B)
In an area not marked as a parking space.
(Ord. No. 6703, § 10, 10-2-19; Ord. No. 6149, § 5, 5-4-11)

11.52.320.title: City lots—Conformance to signs
11.52.320.text:
When signs are erected giving notice thereof, it shall be unlawful for any person
to park a vehicle within a City parking facility in violation of such limitations.
Violations of this Section include:
(A)
Parking a vehicle at a location within the City parking facility or in a manner that
is contrary to or prohibited by the posted limitations; and
(B)
The failure to pay a required parking fee in accordance with LVMC 11.52.310.
(Ord. No. 6703, § 11, 10-2-19; Ord. No. 6629, § 2, 8-15-18; Ord. 1839 § 1 (part),
1976: Ord. 1664 § 1 (part), 1973: Ord. 1331 § 2 (part), 1968: prior code § 10-17-33(B))

11.52.325.title: City lots—Misdemeanors or civil violations
11.52.325.text:
Whether or not signs are erected within or adjacent to a City parking facility giving
notice thereof, it is unlawful, and punishable as a misdemeanor or by means of civil
fine, for any person:
(A)
To deface, damage, tamper with, willfully break, destroy, impair the usefulness of,
evade without tendering due payment, or open without lawful authority an entry or
exit gate or other access-control mechanism pertaining to the parking facility. A
fee equal to the amount of the cost of the repair or replacement of the damaged equipment
will be assessed to the individual or entity responsible for such damage, in addition
to applicable parking fees, parking-related fines, and criminal penalties.
(B)
Where authorized entry to a City parking facility is by means of a gate or other access-
control mechanism, or by receiving a stub or ticket for such entry (or both), to park
a vehicle within the parking facility without having entered the facility in an authorized
manner. Parking in violation of this Subsection (B) is deemed and declared to be a
theft of City services.
(C)
For purposes of avoiding payment of the applicable parking or permit fee; to drive
a vehicle through the entry or exit of a controlled-access parking facility by trailing
immediately behind another vehicle before the gate or other access-control mechanism
has an opportunity to drop or close.
(D)
For purposes of avoiding payment of the applicable parking or permit fee, to drive
a vehicle into or out of the parking facility by any other unauthorized means, such
as by breaking though a gate or other access-control mechanism, or bv entering or
exiting without stopping to receive a stub or ticket for entry or without paying for
exit. In the case of damage caused by breaking through a gate or other access-control
mechanism, a fee equal to the amount of the cost of the repair or replacement of the
damaged equipment will be assessed to the individual or entity responsible for such
damage, in addition to applicable parking fees, parking-related fines, and criminal
penalties.
(Ord. No. 6829, § 6, 2-1-23)

11.52.330.title: City lots—Penalties for violations
11.52.330.text:
(A)
The City Council finds that the parking of a vehicle in violation of LVMC 11.52.320 or 11.52.325 is a public nuisance per se and a disruption of the effective use of City parking
facilities by those persons authorized to use them. The City Manager or his duly authorized
representative shall have the authority to immobilize any vehicle or have any vehicle
removed by towing and impounding from a City parking facility if such vehicle is found
to be in violation of LVMC 11.52.320 or 11.52.325. All expenses incurred in the immobilization or towing and impounding of such vehicle
found to be in violation shall be the responsibility of and charged to the registered
owner of said vehicle and shall be paid prior to removal of the immobilizer or prior
to release of the vehicle from impoundment. The fee for releasing any car immobilized
or impounded under this Section is fifty dollars.
(B)
Citations issued for the violation of LVMC 11.52.320 and 11.52.325 shall be disposed of under normal procedures and need not be paid as a condition
for the release of the vehicle from custody.
(Ord. No. 6829, § 7, 2-1-23; Ord. No. 6703, § 12, 10-2-19; Ord. 5870 § 15, 2006: Ord.
1839 § 1 (part), 1976: Ord. 1826 § 1, 1976: Ord. 1664 § 1 (part), 1973: prior code
§ 10-17-33(C))

11.52.335.title: Parks
11.52.335.text:
(A)
When hours of closure have been established for a park and signs have been posted
therein specifying the hours of closure, no person shall park a motor vehicle in the
park, on a parking lot therein, or in any publicly maintained parking lot immediately
adjacent thereto during the hours of closure.
(B)
No person shall park a motor vehicle on any surface area of a park except those portions
which are either paved or, if unpaved, are specifically designated for the parking
of vehicles.
(C)
The prohibitions contained in Subsections (A) and (B) of this Section do not apply
to the parking of a vehicle in connection with a duly authorized park improvement
or maintenance activity, or to parking which is specifically authorized by the City's
Department of Parks, Recreation and Cultural Affairs, or the Department of Public
Safety.
(Ord. No. 6816, § 113, 8-17-22; Ord. No. 6518, § 19, 4-6-16; Ord. No. 6326, § 35,
6-18-14; Ord. 5095 § 33, 1998)

11.52.340.title: Municipal vehicles
11.52.340.text:
The City Council may designate parking spaces upon City streets or in City parking
facilities for the parking of City vehicles. It is unlawful to park a vehicle other
than a City vehicle in any such space that has been duly posted or marked.
(Ord. No. 6703, § 13, 10-2-19; Ord. No. 6326, § 36, 6-18-14; Ord. 170 § 26 (part),
1931: prior code § 10-17-9)

11.52.350.title: Solicitation prohibitions
11.52.350.text:
No person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle in a street for the purpose of engaging
or soliciting the employment of a pedestrian.
(Ord. 4092 § 1, 1997)

11.53.010.title: Purpose
11.53.010.text:
The purpose of this Chapter is to set forth the criteria to be used by the City for
the installation, removal, and regulation of selected areas for valet parking in public
rights-of-way. This Chapter is enacted in response to the need to provide additional
parking space, and facilitate additional parking options, for patrons, guests and
residents of commercial and noncommercial locations in parking-impacted areas within
the boundaries of the Downtown Las Vegas Overlay District, as described in LVMC 19.10.110.
(Ord. No. 6608, § 19, 12-6-17; Ord. 5805 § 2, 2005)

11.53.020.title: Definitions
11.53.020.text:
For purposes of this Chapter, the following terms have the meanings ascribed to them:
"Valet parking" means a service by which patrons, guests or residents of commercial
or noncommercial establishments or locations leave their vehicles at the street curbline
and attendants park and retrieve the vehicles, whether or not for consideration.
"Valet parking zone" means an area within the public right-of-way that has been set
aside by the City for valet parking in accordance with this Chapter.
"Valet parking permit" means a permit issued in accordance with this Chapter for the
approved use of valet parking in a valet parking zone.
(Ord. 5805 § 3, 2005)

11.53.030.title: Valet parking designation
11.53.030.text:
The City Traffic Engineer is responsible for the designation of valet parking zones.
In deciding whether or not to designate an area as a valet parking zone, the City
Traffic Engineer shall consider:
(A)
The safety and convenience of the public;
(B)
