The actual number of passengers to be served by the valet parking zone;
(C)
The proximity of any existing valet parking zones;
(D)
Existing demands for curb use such as the number and location of existing transit
and taxi loading zones, and existing commercial loading zones in the general area
of the requested zone;
(E)
The availability of on- and off-street parking for the area; and
(F)
Any potential impact on the environment.
(Ord. 5805 § 4, 2005)

11.53.040.title: Permit authorization
11.53.040.text:
(A)
The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to issue valet parking permits pursuant to
this Chapter. Application for a valet parking permit shall be made in writing on a
form approved by the City Traffic Engineer and shall be accompanied by a filing fee.
The filing fee shall be as set forth in the fee schedule adopted pursuant to LVMC
13.40.050. The City may also assess usage fees and parking meter-related fees in amounts set
forth in the fee schedule.
(B)
The application for a valet parking permit shall include:
(1)
The business name and address of the person, corporation, partnership or other business
entity seeking the permit;
(2)
The identifying number of the applicant's business license, if one is required;
(3)
A description and map of the location proposed to be used as a valet parking zone
and the location of the use or uses the valet parking zone is intended to serve;
(4)
A description and map sufficient to show how the valet parking zone(s) will be operated;
(5)
A description and map of the parking lot or lots where vehicles will be stored, and
how vehicles will be moved between the valet parking zone and the vehicle storage
sites; and
(6)
Any other information that the City Traffic Engineer deems necessary in order to approve
a valet parking permit.
(Ord. 5805 § 5, 2005)

11.53.050.title: Permit renewal
11.53.050.text:
Each valet parking permit issued by the City Traffic Engineer shall be valid for not
more than one year from date of issuance. An application for renewal of the permit
shall be processed in general accordance with LVMC 11.53.040. Renewal of a permit is subject to an inspection of the valet parking zone and its
operation. The City may charge a permit renewal fee and related fees as set forth
in the fee schedule adopted pursuant to LVMC 13.40.050.
(Ord. 5805 § 6, 2005)

11.53.060.title: Permit approval
11.53.060.text:
A valet parking permit authorizes the permittee to provide valet parking in a valet
parking zone that is designated for use in connection with that permit. The approval
of a permit shall be limited by the locations and operational details that were submitted
as part of the application process. Approval of a permit may be made subject to conditions
designed to minimize the impact of the valet parking on the surrounding areas. A permit
is also subject to the following:
(A)
The permittee shall be responsible for ensuring that a valet parking zone is operated
in such a manner as to provide ample opportunity for passenger drop-off or pick-up
by motorists who do not wish to utilize valet parking services.
(B)
The permittee may operate the valet parking service or contract with an operator to
do so. The permittee must be:
(1)
The owner or a principal of the business or other concern that is to be served by
the valet parking service; or
(2)
An employee or contractor of that business or other concern.
(C)
The permittee or operator shall provide and maintain portable pedestal signs as may
be required by the City Traffic Engineer. Except as otherwise permitted by the City
Traffic Engineer, pedestal signs shall be twenty-four inches wide and not more than
four feet high. The signs shall have three-inch black letters on a white background
and shall indicate that the marked area is designated for valet parking and passenger
loading and unloading only. The signs may indicate that vehicles parked in violation
of the restrictions are subject to citation or other enforcement activity. Sign pedestals
must be located within twenty-four inches of the face of the curb and be placed in
such a manner as not to create an impediment to pedestrians.
(D)
The permittee or operator shall not allow the valet parking zone or any other public
right-of-way to be used for the storage of valet-parked cars.
(E)
The permittee or operator must obtain the written approval of the City Traffic Engineer
before changing the location or operation of a valet parking zone, including the location
of parking lots upon which vehicles are stored.
(F)
The applicant must provide the City Traffic Engineer with copies of all agreements
relating to the operation of the valet parking zone, including without limitation
agreements between a permittee and an operator, agreements between a permittee and
the businesses and concerns to be served by the valet parking service, and agreements
between the permittee or operator and the owner or operator of the parking lots to
be used for the storage of vehicles.
(G)
The use of parking lots for the storage of vehicles must be in compliance with Title 19 and all zoning requirements established thereunder.
(H)
The operator must demonstrate compliance with any business licensing requirements
applicable to the valet parking operation.
(I)
The permittee must indemnify the City by means of an indemnification agreement satisfactory
to the City Attorney.
(J)
The permittee or operator must maintain a policy of liability insurance in an amount
satisfactory to the City in order to protect the City from any claims which may arise
from the valet parking operation.
(K)
During the operation of a valet parking service, the permittee or operator must display
the applicable valet parking permit in a conspicuous place at the valet parking zone,
and must make it available for inspection on the demand of any peace officer or enforcement
official of the City.
(Ord. 5805 § 7, 2005)

11.53.070.title: Valet parking zone—Public uses
11.53.070.text:
(A)
Except as otherwise provided in Subsection (B), an area designated as a valet parking
zone pursuant to this Chapter may also be used for public parking or for the loading
and unloading of persons or property, as may be indicated on appropriate signage.
(B)
During periods of time in which a valet parking zone is being used for valet parking,
a vehicle may not be parked within the zone for longer than is necessary for passenger
loading or unloading, or for a parking attendant to enter the vehicle to drive it
to its parking destination or to return it to the valet parking zone for pickup by
the valet customer. When such limitations are in effect, the zone must be posted with
approved signage indicating the limitations on the use of the valet parking zone.
(Ord. 5805 § 8, 2005)

11.53.080.title: Parking regulations
11.53.080.text:
Nothing in this Chapter authorizes the parking of vehicles by the permittee or operator
in a manner contrary to applicable State law or City traffic and parking regulations.
(Ord. 5805 § 9, 2005)

11.53.090.title: Permittee—Responsibility
11.53.090.text:
(A)
The permittee (and the operator, if someone other than the permittee operates the
valet parking service) are jointly and severally responsible for the proper operation
of the valet parking service and valet parking zone.
(B)
The failure to comply with any requirement of this Chapter or any condition imposed
upon a valet parking permit shall be sufficient cause for revocation of the permit
by the City Traffic Engineer. A permit may be revoked if the City Traffic Engineer,
after a hearing on the matter, finds the existence of grounds which would have constituted
just cause for refusal to issue the permit, or finds that the permittee or operator
has failed to comply with any requirement of this Chapter or condition imposed upon
the permit. Written notice of the revocation hearing, setting forth the time and place
of hearing and a brief statement of the reason(s) for the proposed revocation, shall
be served on or mailed to the permittee at the business address listed in the permit
application not less than ten days before the hearing.
(C)
A valet parking permit may be temporarily suspended without a hearing if the City
Traffic Engineer determines that the continued operation of the valet parking service
is a hazard to public safety or is in violation of this Chapter. The suspension shall
remain in effect until a hearing is held and a decision made, but in no event for
more than sixty days.
(Ord. 5805 § 10, 2005)

11.53.100.title: Responsibility delegation
11.53.100.text:
The City Traffic Engineer may delegate any responsibility assigned to him under this
Chapter to one or more employees of the City.
(Ord. 5805 § 11, 2005)

11.53.110.title: Parking violation—Public uses
11.53.110.text:
No person shall park a vehicle in violation of Subsection (B) of LVMC 11.53.070.
(Ord. 5805 § 12, 2005)

11.53.120.title: Violations
11.53.120.text:
It is unlawful, and a criminal violation, for any person to:
(A)
Operate, engage in, conduct, manage, or cause to be operated on any public right-of-way
a valet parking service without a valid valet parking permit issued by the City;
(B)
Provide false information in an application for a valet parking permit; or
(C)
Permit the use or display of a valet parking permit for any purpose other than that
for which the permit is issued.
(Ord. 5805 § 13, 2005)

11.54.010.title: Definitions
11.54.010.text:
For the purposes of this Chapter the terms "operator," "park," "parking," "parking
meter," "parking meter space," "parking meter zone," "street" and "vehicle" have the
meaning subscribed in Subsection C of Section 11.10.010 of this Title.
(Ord. 3829 § 10, 1994: Ord. 354 § 1, 1948: prior code § 10-3-1)

11.54.020.title: Zone designated
11.54.020.text:
Those streets or portions of streets or areas described in Schedule 3-I, a copy of
which is to be maintained for public inspection in the offices of the City Clerk and
City Traffic Engineer, and such other streets, portions of streets or other areas
as may be added to said Schedule by written finding of the City Traffic Engineer shall
constitute a parking meter zone.
(Ord. No. 6184, § 10, 3-21-12; Ord. 3990 § 19, 1996: Ord. 1589 § 1 (part), 1972: Ord.
1278 § 1 (part), 1967: Ord. 1169 § 1 (part), 1965: Ord. 710 § 1, 1956: Ord. 354 §
2, 1948: prior code § 10-3-2)

11.54.030.title: Meter placement approval
11.54.030.text:
The placement or removal of parking meters on those streets, portions of streets and
other areas identified in LVMC 11.54.020 shall be done by written finding of the City Traffic Engineer approving such placement
or removal.
(Ord. No. 6184, § 11, 3-21-12; Ord. 3989 § 11, 1996: Ord. 1589 § 1 (part), 1972: Ord.
1278 § 1 (part), 1967: Ord. 1169 § 1 (part), 1965: Ord. 710 § 2, 1956: prior code
§ 10-3-2 (part))

11.54.040.title: Space designation
11.54.040.text:
The City Traffic Engineer is directed and authorized to mark off individual parking
spaces in the parking zones which may be established. Except for metered parking spaces
on the street, parking spaces are to be designated by lines painted or durably marked
on the curbing or surfaces within such parking zone. In any parking zone so marked
off, it shall be a violation of this Chapter to park any vehicle in such a way that
the vehicle shall not be entirely within the limits of a single space so designated
or in an area not marked off for parking.
(Ord. 3989 § 12, 1996: Ord. 3829 § 11, 1994: Ord. 2203 § 5, 1981: Ord. 981 § 2 (part),
1962: Ord. 354 § 3, 1948: prior code § 10-3-3)

11.54.050.title: Meter installation and specifications
11.54.050.text:
In parking meter zones, the City Traffic Engineer shall cause parking meters to be
installed at the appropriate locations so as to control the metered parking spaces
established under this Chapter. The Parking Services Division of the Department of
Economic and Urban Development shall be responsible for the enforcement, installation,
operation, maintenance and use of parking meters. Each device shall enable legal parking
for the period of time established under this Chapter, upon activation of the meter
in accordance with Section 11.54.060. Upon the expiration of the period for which parking in a particular space:
(A)
Is permitted pursuant to this Chapter; and
(B)
Has been duly enabled under this Chapter by means of payment,
→ the right of the vehicle to occupy such space shall cease and the operator, owner,
possessor or manager thereof shall be subject to the penalties provided in this Title.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 37, 6-18-14; Ord. No. 6184, § 12, 3-21-12; Ord. 5870 § 16, 2006:
Ord. 3829 § 12, 1994: Ord. 2203 § 6, 1981: Ord. 981 § 2 (part), 1962: prior code §
10-3-4)

11.54.060.title: Activation of meter—Lawful occupancy
11.54.060.text:
(A)
Except in a period of emergency determined by an officer of the Department of Fire
and Rescue or the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department, or in compliance with
the directions of a police officer or traffic-control sign or signal, when any vehicle
shall be parked in any parking space controlled by a parking meter, the operator of
such vehicle shall, upon entering the parking meter space, immediately activate the
meter in accordance with this Section. Failure to activate a meter in accordance with
this Section is a violation of this Chapter.
(B)
For purposes of this Section, activation of the meter consists of paying the amount
required to set in operation the timing function of the meter or activating the meter
by the alternate means described in Subsection (C) of this Section. Activation by
payment may be accomplished by one of the following means:
(1)
Deposit of the required amount in United States coin;
(2)
An approved debit or credit payment; or
(3)
Activation of the meter by electronic means established and approved by the City.
(C)
As an alternative to meter activation by means of payment described in Subsection
(B), a meter in a particular meter zone may be activated by the display of a valid
permit that has been authorized, designated and issued by the City for use in that
meter zone. The City may charge a fee for such a permit under the authority described
in LVMC 11.54.100(A).
(D)
In connection with authorizing payment by electronic means as described in Paragraph
(3) of Subsection (B), the City is authorized to charge a convenience fee.
(E)
Upon activation of the parking meter in accordance with this Section, the parking
space may be lawfully occupied by such vehicle during the period of time which has
been prescribed for the part of the street in which said parking space is located
and for the period during which the parking meter is activated.
(Ord. No. 6402, § 1, 2-18-15; Ord. No. 6326, § 38, 6-18-14; Ord. 5870 § 17, 2006:
Ord. 5233 § 1, 2000: Ord. 2203 § 7 (part), 1981: Ord. 1278 § 2 (part), 1967: Ord.
354 § 5 (part), 1948: prior code § 10-3-5 (part))

11.54.070.title: Overtime parking
11.54.070.text:
If a vehicle shall remain parked in any parking space contemplated in LVMC 11.54.060 beyond the time period that has been paid for regarding that space, the vehicle shall
be deemed in violation of this Chapter. This provision regarding overtime parking
shall not apply to any vehicle lawfully displaying a special or temporary parking
sticker, placard, permit or plate, and parked in a space for a period of four hours
or less as provided in NRS 484B.463.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 39, 6-18-14; Ord. 5870, § 18, 2006: Ord. 3829 § 13, 1994: Ord. 2203
§ 7 (part), 1981: Ord. 1278 § 2 (part), 1967: Ord. 354 § 5 (part), 1948: prior code
§ 10-3-5 (part))

11.54.080.title: Unattached trailers
11.54.080.text:
It shall be a violation of this Chapter to park any trailer, trailer coach or other
unattached vehicle which is capable of being towed by a motor vehicle in any parking
meter space except:
(A)
An unattached vehicle used as a temporary traffic control device to display messages
directing traffic during emergencies or construction; or
(B)
By means of a special permit issued by the City Traffic Engineer.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 41, 6-18-14; Ord. 5095 § 34, 1998: Ord. 3989 § 13, 1996: Ord. 2203
§ 7 (part), 1981: Ord. 1278 § 2(part), 1967: prior code § 10-3-5 (part))

11.54.090.title: Hours of operation
11.54.090.text:
(A)
Subject to the provisions of Subsection (B), the hours of operation for any parking
meter shall be those which are established by the City Traffic Engineer.
(B)
Any metered parking space may be occupied without activating the meter on the following
days: January 1; the third Monday in January; the third Monday in February; the last
Monday in May; June 19; July 4th; the first Monday in September; the last Friday in
October; November 11; the fourth Thursday in November; the Friday following the fourth
Thursday in November; December 25; and any general holiday declared by the President
of the United States, the Governor of the State or the Mayor.
(Ord. No. 6829, § 8, 2-1-23; Ord. No. 6326, § 42, 6-18-14; Ord. 5870 § 20, 2006)

11.54.100.title: Rates—Spaces on street
11.54.100.text:
Parking or standing a vehicle in a parking meter space on the streets and parts of
streets that are designated in Schedule 3-I, as the same is established pursuant to
LVMC 11.54.020, or in any City parking facility is permissible in accordance with the rates and
time limits which have been:
(A)
Established by the Parking Services Division of the Department of Economic and Urban
Development, and approved by the City Manager; and
(B)
Indicated upon the parking meter or by means of a duly-posted sign.
(Ord. No. 6703, § 14, 10-2-19; Ord. No. 6402, § 2, 2-18-15; Ord. 5181 § 2, 1999: Ord.
3989 § 15, 1996: Ord. 3353 § 2, 1988: Ord. 1304 § 1 (part), 1967: Ord. 1007 § 1, 1962:
Ord. 988 § 1 (part), 1962: Ord. 981 § 2 (part), 1962: Ord. 622 § 1 (part), 1954: Ord.
592 § 1 (part), 1954: Ord. 354 § 6(b), 1948: prior code § 10-3-6(B))

11.54.110.title: City-owned lots—Use of parking spaces/areas without meter activation
11.54.110.text:
Notwithstanding any other provision of this Title pertaining to metered parking, the
City Manager or a designee may establish and implement a policy under which specific
parking spaces or parking space areas within a City parking facility may be used without
the need to activate the corresponding parking meter in the manner otherwise required.
(Ord. No. 6703, § 15, 10-2-19; Ord. No. 6162, § 1, 9-2-11)

11.54.170.title: Collections
11.54.170.text:
It shall be the duty of the Parking Services Division of the Department of Economic
and Urban Development to designate some employee or employees, who shall be bonded,
to make regular collections of the money deposited in said meters and it shall be
the duty of such employees so designated to remove the coins so deposited in the meters
and deliver the same to the Director of Finance who shall count the funds contained
therein and deposit such funds with the Treasurer.
(Ord. No. 6184, § 13, 3-21-12; Ord. 3484 § 14, 1990: Ord. 2203 § 8, 1981: Ord. 981
§ 2 (part), 1962: Ord. 354 § 9, 1948: prior code § 10-3-8)

11.54.180.title: Use of funds
11.54.180.text:
The revenue generated by parking meters shall be used to defray the expense of proper
regulation of traffic and parking upon the public streets of the City, to provide
for the cost of supervision, regulation and control of the parking of vehicles in
parking meter zones and other areas in which parking is restricted and to cover the
cost of purchase, supervision, protection, inspection, installation, operation, maintenance,
control and use of parking meters as well as the public areas in the vicinity of the
parking meters and the zones in which parking is restricted.
(Ord. 5233 § 2, 2000: Ord. 3353 § 4, 1988: Ord. 354 § 10, 1948: prior code § 10-3-9)

11.54.190.title: Exemption permits
11.54.190.text:
(A)
Parking exemption permits shall authorize the persons to whom they are issued to park,
without violation and without the payment of a meter fee, the vehicles to which the
permits are affixed in any on-street parking space adjacent to any parking meter with
a time limit of one hour or more, or in any space in a one-hour time-limited parking
zone, while actually engaged in field work, subject to the limitations in Subsection
(C) of this Section.
(B)
The following groups of persons shall be eligible for parking exemption permits upon
application to the City Manager or his authorized designee:
(1)
Members of news media whether involved in television, radio or newspaper news preparation
or reporting, who are actually in the field preparing or reporting news stories for
their employers;
(2)
Public officers and employees of Federal, State or local governments who are required
by their employers to use private automobiles while actually engaged in field work
or business outside of their normal offices.
(C)
No parking exemption permit shall be approved by the City Manager under this Section
unless he receives a letter accompanying the application from the applicant's top
administrative officer describing such applicant's job responsibilities and his need
for an exempt parking permit and which shows to the City Manager's satisfaction that
the employee qualifies for the permit.
(D)
A fee shall be charged for each parking exemption permit issued, except as indicated
in Subsection (G) of this Section. The fee for a media employee exemption permit shall
be in the amount of twenty-five dollars. The fee for a governmental employee exemption
permit shall be in the amount of five hundred dollars.
(E)
Each parking exemption permit shall be valid for a period of one year. Once a parking
exemption permit is issued to a qualified applicant, it shall be unlawful for such
person to use the permit for other than official business, and in no case shall the
permit authorize any vehicle to park in any space adjacent to any parking meter or
in any space posted one-hour time-limited parking zone for more than two hours continuously.
(F)
Operators of City-owned vehicles with exempt plates issued pursuant to NRS 482.368
shall not be required to apply for, purchase or display parking exemption permits.
Vehicles displaying such license plates shall be authorized to park, without violation
and without the payment of a meter fee, in any space adjacent to any parking meter
with a time limit of one hour or more, or in any space posted as a one-hour or two-hour
time-limited parking zone, for not more than two hours continuously.
(G)
The City Manager or his designee, upon request, may issue parking exemption permits,
without charge, to the County Manager of Clark County, or the city manager of any
incorporated city within Clark County, for the use of elected officials, citizen board
members, or other government officials to whom those permits have been assigned by
the respective manager. The maximum number of permits that may be issued without charge
shall be as follows:
(1)
For use by Clark County, a maximum of fifteen permits.
(2)
For use by other cities, a maximum of seven permits per city.
(Ord. 5870 § 21, 2006: Ord. 3561 § 1, 1991: Ord. 3535 § 1, 1990: Ord. 3345 § 1, 1988:
Ord. 3088 § 1, 1983: Ord. 1860 § 1, 1977: Ord. 1836 § 1 (part), 1976: Ord. 1579 §
1, 1972: Ord. 1334 § 1, 1968: Ord. 1323 § 2 (part), 1968: Ord. 1306 § 1, 1967: Ord.
1007 § 2, 1962; Ord. 981 § 2 (part), 1962: Ord. 354 § 8, 1948: prior code § 10-3-11)

11.54.200.title: Violations
11.54.200.text:
It shall be a violation of the provisions of this Chapter for any person:
(A)
To cause, allow, permit or suffer any vehicle registered in the name of or operated
by such person, contractor or agency to be parked overtime, or beyond the period of
legal parking time established for any parking meter zone established under this Chapter.
(B)
To permit any vehicle to remain in any parking space adjacent to any parking meter
while said meter is displaying a signal indicating that the vehicle has already been
parked beyond the period prescribed for such parking space or beyond the period for
which the meter was activated.
(C)
To park any vehicle across any line or marking of a parking meter space or in such
position that the vehicle is not entirely within the area designated by such lines
or markings.
(D)
To park any vehicle for more than thirty minutes in a parking meter space that has
been posted as out of service because of malfunction.
(E)
To park any vehicle in a parking meter space that has been posted as reserved for
use by another person, company, contractor or agency pursuant to Section 11.54.230.
(Ord. 5870 § 22, 2006: Ord. 5233 § 3, 2000: Ord. 3989 § 17, 1996: Ord. 354 § 7, 1948:
prior code § 10-3-10)

11.54.202.title: Violation—Civil infraction
11.54.202.text:
Unless otherwise provided, a violation of this Chapter shall be a civil infraction
in accordance with the provisions of LVMC Ch. 11.10, for which both the registered owner and the operator of a vehicle are liable.
(Ord. 3989 § 19, 1996)

11.54.205.title: Misdemeanors
11.54.205.text:
It is a misdemeanor for any person:
(A)
To deface, injure, tamper with, open or wilfully break, destroy, remove, or impair
the usefulness of any parking meter installed under the provisions of this Chapter,
except as otherwise provided in this Chapter.
(B)
To deposit or cause to be deposited in any parking meter any slugs, device or metal
substances, or other substitute for lawful coins.
(C)
To attempt to activate any parking meter by means of a key or card which is not authorized
for use in that meter.
(Ord. 5233 § 4, 2000: Ord. 3989 § 20, 1996)

11.54.210.title: Erroneous citations—Malfunctioning meters
11.54.210.text:
Notices of Infractions whose issuance is based upon a malfunctioning parking meter
or is otherwise in error may be referred to the Parking Division of the Department
of Economic and Urban Development for formal withdrawal of the Notice of Infraction
and any enforcement-related documents previously processed.
(Ord. No. 6184, § 14, 3-21-12; Ord. 5870 § 23, 2006: Ord. 3829 § 14, 1994: Ord. 2203
§ 9, 1981: Ord. 1836 § 1 (part), 1976: Ord. 1323 § 2 (part), 1968: prior code § 10-3-12)

11.54.220.title: Transit and loading zones unaffected
11.54.220.text:
Nothing in this Chapter shall be construed as prohibiting the City from providing
for bus stops, for taxicab stands and other matters of similar nature, including the
loading or unloading of trucks, vans or other commercial vehicles.
(Prior code § 10-3-7)

11.54.230.title: Occupancy permit
11.54.230.text:
The Parking Division of the Department of Economic and Urban Development may issue
to a person, company, contractor or agency, upon application therefor, a parking space
occupancy permit authorizing the occupancy of one or more metered parking spaces for
extended periods of time in order to provide supplies, materials, or services, on
a temporary basis, in the immediate area of the parking spaces. Issuance of such an
occupancy permit shall be in the discretion of the Parking Division of the Department
of Economic and Urban Development. In connection with the issuance of an occupancy
permit, the City is authorized to charge an occupancy permit fee, which shall be paid
by the applicant before any permit is issued or space reserved for the applicant.
The amount of the occupancy permit fee shall be determined by the Parking Division
of the Department of Economic and Urban Development and shall be in an amount that
represents the sum of:
(A)
The maximum parking meter revenue otherwise collectible for parking a vehicle or vehicles,
for the period of time requested, in the metered parking spaces to be occupied under
the occupancy permit; and
(B)
An amount representing the costs of processing the application and occupancy permit.
(Ord. No. 6184, § 15, 3-21-12; Ord. 5870 § 25, 2006)

11.54.240.title: Pilot program
11.54.240.text:
(A)
The Traffic Engineer or the Parking Division of the Department of Economic and Urban
Development may establish on a temporary basis one or more pilot programs pursuant
to which persons licensed as mobile food vendors may occupy parking spaces located
on selected public rights-of-way for the purpose of vending. Such programs may include
one or more of the following elements:
(1)
A lottery or other system under which interested vendors, by means of an application
or similar process and the payment of a fee, may become eligible to participate in
the pilot vending program.
(2)
Payment by a mobile food vendor, by means of a parking meter, for the right to occupy
and vend within designated parking spaces.
(3)
A system of rotation or other method by which interested vendors may participate on
an equitable basis with other vendors and by which the public can have access to a
variety of dining categories and food products.
(B)
The use of a parking space in accordance with a pilot program established under this
Section is exempt from any prohibition on such use that otherwise would apply.
(C)
It is unlawful to do any of the following:
(1)
Park a vehicle that is eligible for the pilot program at the meter reserved for or
assigned to that vehicle in excess of the time for which the meter was activated or
without activating the meter.
(2)
Park a vehicle that is eligible for the pilot program at a meter other than one reserved
for or assigned to that vehicle under that program.
(3)
Park a vehicle that is ineligible for the pilot program at a meter assigned to be
used in connection with the pilot program.
(D)
The fines associated with a violation of Subsection (C) shall be as set forth in the
schedule of fines and penalties adopted under LVMC 11.10.140.
(Ord. No. 6437, § 11, 8-5-15; Ord. No. 6236, § 1, 2-6-13)

11.55.010.title: Definitions
11.55.010.text:
The following words, terms and phrases shall have the meaning indicated:
(A)
"Park" means to stand a vehicle for a period of time greater than is reasonably necessary
for the actual loading thereon or unloading therefrom of persons or property.
(B)
"Patron parking lot" means any building, structure, outdoor space, uncovered plot,
place, lot, parcel, yard, or enclosure or any portion thereof, on the same or adjacent
property and provided exclusively for the use and convenience of persons doing business
at or with a business establishment and for which no charge to park is made and whether
or not a ticket must be validated.
(C)
"Public parking lot" means any building, structure, outdoor space, uncovered plot,
place, lot, parcel, yard or enclosure, or any portion thereof, where motor vehicles
are parked, stored, housed or kept, for which any charge is made, and which is open
to the general public.
(D)
"Semipublic parking lot" means any building, structure, outdoor space, uncovered plot,
place, lot, parcel, yard or enclosure, or any portion thereof, where motor vehicles
are parked, stored, housed or kept, pursuant to agreement with the owner, operator,
or manager and for which a charge is made on a daily, weekly or monthly rate.
(Ord. 2210 § 2 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-32-1)

11.55.020.title: Space designation and restrictions
11.55.020.text:
When any person shall establish any parking lot as defined in Section 11.55.010 such person shall designate the space for parking and the manner of parking thereon,
the space thereon to be used for parking by different types of vehicles and may also
limit the time such vehicles may remain parked on the premises.
(Ord. 2210 § 2 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-32-2)

11.55.030.title: Sign and required information
11.55.030.text:
Such person in addition shall maintain at each entrance to such parking lot permanent
sign or signs suitable to apprise persons using the same of the following information:
(A)
The hours of the day or night during which the parking lot is open for business, unless
the parking lot is open for business twenty-four hours a day;
(B)
Rates charged for parking, if any charge is made, and when more than one rate is charged
or a sliding rate scale is charged, the figures and letters stipulating each rate
shall be of uniform size and dimensions, and shall be not less than six inches in
height and three inches in width;
(C)
If the parking lot is exclusively a patron parking lot, such information as to properly
advise the users of the terms and conditions of such use;
(D)
The name, address, and telephone number of the holder of the business license;
(E)
If the parking lot is a self-service public parking lot, such information as to properly
advise the users of the manner and place of fee payment;
(F)
That a patron parking a vehicle without paying the posted fee in the manner made available
is deemed a trespasser, for which a citation will be issued. Any vehicle receiving
two such citations will be subject to impound, and information concerning any impounded
vehicle may be obtained by calling the Metropolitan Police Department. Provide phone
number.
(Ord. 2210 § 2 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-32-3)

11.55.040.title: Emergency contact
11.55.040.text:
Every person establishing or maintaining a parking lot as defined in this Chapter
shall furnish to the Metropolitan Police Department the name and telephone number
of a responsible person who may be contacted in the event an emergency arises.
(Ord. 2210 § 2 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-32-4)

11.55.050.title: Violations—Log book
11.55.050.text:
There shall be maintained by each licensee a log book showing date and time and license
number of any vehicle issued a violation envelope.
(Ord. 2210 § 2 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-32-5 (part))

11.55.060.title: Violations—Envelope
11.55.060.text:
Vehicles in violation will be issued a violation envelope by the licensee on their
first offense, containing the date, time and place of violation, and giving the reason
for the violation and explaining the consequences.
(Ord. 2210 § 2 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-32-5(A))

11.55.070.title: Violations—Impoundment restriction
11.55.070.text:
No vehicle will be impounded on its first violation. Each twenty-four-hour period
after a violation has been issued may be considered a separate violation.
(Ord. 2210 § 2 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-32-5 (B))

11.55.080.title: Impoundment—Release at site—Report to Police
11.55.080.text:
Impound procedures:
(A)
If a tow truck has answered a call to impound a vehicle and the owner/driver of the
vehicle returns for the vehicle before it has been "raised" (attached), the vehicle
will be released upon payment of the parking fee due. If the vehicle has been raised,
the vehicle will be released to the owner/ driver upon payment of parking fees due
and one-half of the towing charge (seven dollars).
(B)
After the vehicle is raised, but before the truck removes the vehicle from the parking
lot, the tow truck operator will call the Metropolitan Police Department by radio
to advise:
(1)
The make of the car;
(2)
Registration number;
(3)
The name of the registered owner, if available;
(4)
The parking lot from which towed; and
(5)
The place of impound from which the vehicle may be recovered.
(Ord. 2210 § 2 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-32-5 (C))

11.55.090.title: Impoundment—Notice to owner
11.55.090.text:
It will be the duty of the Metropolitan Police Department to check the place of impound
after twenty-four hours have elapsed from the time the Department was notified that
a vehicle had been towed, to determine if the vehicle has been recovered, and the
fees due to release the vehicle. If the vehicle has not been recovered, the Metropolitan
Police Department will notify the parking lot licensee of that fact, and will further
notify the licensee of the name and address of the registered owner of the impounded
vehicle. It will then become the duty of the parking lot licensee to mail a certified
letter, return-receipt requested, to the address of the registered owner of the vehicle
advising him of the circumstances, place of impound, and fees due to release the vehicle.
(Ord. 2210 § 2 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-32-5 (D))

11.55.100.title: Trash and refuse
11.55.100.text:
Each parking lot will be free of trash and refuse. A suitable trash can will be made
available by the holder of the license, at or near the fee-collection device, which
will be emptied as often as required. Signs will be posted requesting that parking
patrons cooperate and put all trash in the proper trash receivers. Any patron observed
to ignore such notice will be reprimanded and cited if he should not replace the refuse
from the lot surface to the appropriate receptacle. Police may be called to assist,
if necessary.
(Ord. 2210 § 2 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-32-6)

11.55.110.title: Illumination
11.55.110.text:
Any parking lot open for business from dusk to dawn, or any portion thereof, will
be illuminated between the time with lamps and fixtures emitting a minimum of one
foot-candle. Parking lots open for business between dawn to dusk, or any portion thereof,
will not require illumination.
(Ord. 2210 § 2 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-32-7)

11.57.010.title: Definitions
11.57.010.text:
For purposes of this Chapter:
"Metro" means the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department.
"Motorized racing event" mean a race involving motorized vehicles that is held:
(1)
Pursuant to a written agreement between the sponsor or promoter and the City; and
(2)
Under the auspices or with the approval of a statewide, national or international
organization that regularly engages in the governance, supervision or sanctioning
of such events.
(Ord. 5877 § 1 (part), 2006)

11.57.020.title: Application—Provisions
11.57.020.text:
(A)
In order to stage a motorized racing event on any public street within the City, the
applicant must first obtain a permit approved by Metro and the City Manager. The application
for a permit must be filed at least sixty days prior to the date scheduled for the
racing event.
(B)
At the time an application for a permit is submitted pursuant to Subsection (A), the
applicant must submit a traffic control plan to Metro and to the City Traffic Engineer.
The traffic control plan shall describe the proposed placement of any temporary barricades,
temporary traffic signs or similar traffic control devices. The approval of a permit
shall be contingent on:
(1)
The approval of the traffic control plan by Metro and the City Traffic Engineer;
(2)
The provision of liability insurance in accordance with LVMC 11.56.030, subject to
the minimum policy limits listed therein or such higher limits as Metro and the City
may require; and
(3)
Compliance with any special requirements imposed by Metro, the City Manager or the
City Traffic Engineer.
(C)
The City may close public streets in connection with the staging of a motorized racing
event for which a permit has been approved under this Section. Such action may take
the form of a resolution adopted by the City Council, or the Council may delegate
to the City Traffic Engineer the authority to close such streets by means of a street
closure order.
(D)
In connection with a motorized racing event for which a permit has been approved and
streets have been closed pursuant to this Section, certain provisions of City ordinances
and the Municipal Code which otherwise would prohibit, or be violated by, the motorized
racing event shall be deemed suspended for the period of time specified in the street
closure resolution or order. The suspension shall include the following regulations,
as well as any others specified in the resolution or order:
(1)
Any traffic regulations set forth in LVMC Title 11 that would prohibit or unduly interfere with conducting the event.
(2)
Any noise regulations set forth in LVMC Chapter 9.16 that would prohibit or limit the noise emanating from the vehicles participating
in the event.
(3)
Any fueling regulations set forth in the Fire Code adopted pursuant to LVMC Chapter 16.16 that would prohibit the outdoor fueling activities, including the storage and dispensing
of methanol and other fuels at the racing track, paddock area, pit row or any other
fueling site required for the racing event, provided that event participants and sponsors
have complied with the conditions and requirements imposed by the Fire Chief for the
safety of spectators, event participants and owners of neighboring properties.
(Ord. 5877 § 1 (part), 2006)

11.58.010.title: Oversize or overweight permits—Types
11.58.010.text:
The Department of Public Works may, at its discretion, upon application in writing,
issue a special permit in writing authorizing the applicant to operate or move a vehicle,
combination of vehicles, special self-propelled equipment, special mobile equipment,
or load thereon of a size or weight in excess of the legal maximums, in the following
instances:
(A)
Continuous special permits may be issued for the operation or movement of a vehicle
or combination of vehicles of a size or weight in excess of the legal maximum when
such vehicle or combination of vehicles does not exceed one hundred forty-four inches
in overall width, or when the total gross weight imposed on any single axle or group
of two or more consecutive axles does not exceed the legal maximum weight for such
vehicle or combination of vehicles by more than twenty-five percent.
(B)
Single-trip special permits may be issued for the operation or movement of vehicles
or combinations of vehicles of an overall width in excess of one hundred forty-four
inches, or when the total gross weight of such vehicle or combination of vehicles
exceeds by more than twenty-five percent the legal maximum weight for such vehicle
or combination of vehicles; provided, however, that in the event several movements
to and from the same points in the City with the same vehicles or combinations of
vehicles may be required, continuous special permits for that specific operation may
be issued.
(C)
Continuous or single-trip special permits may be issued for the operation or movement
of special self-propelled equipment, such as truck cranes, truck shovels, loaders
and similar equipment, of a size or weight in excess of the legal maximums.
(Ord. No. 6816, § 114, 8-17-22; Ord. 1021 § 8(1), 1963: prior code § 10-29-8(A))

11.58.020.title: Oversize or overweight permits—Conditions
11.58.020.text:
In issuing any of the special permits provided for in Section 11.58.010, the Department of Public Works may impose such conditions thereon, such as routes
to be followed, place of operation or movement, time of operation or movement or other
matters, as it shall deem necessary or proper to protect the streets, highways and
alleys from damage or to minimize the inconvenience or delays to the general public.
(Ord. No. 6816, § 115, 8-17-22; Ord. 1021 § 8(2), 1963: prior code § 10-29-8(B))

11.58.030.title: Oversize or overweight permits—Application
11.58.030.text:
The application for any of the special permits provided for in Section 11.58.010 shall:
(A)
Specifically describe the vehicles, combinations of vehicles, special self-propelled
equipment or special mobile equipment, and load thereon, and the particular streets,
highways or alleys over which the special permit to operate or move the same is requested.
(B)
State whether such special permit is requested for a single trip or for continuous
operation.
(Ord. 1021 § 8(3), 1963: prior code § 10-29-8(C))

11.58.040.title: Oversize or overweight permits—Structures
11.58.040.text:
Nothing contained in Sections 11.58.010 through this Section shall be deemed to authorize the issuance of special permits
for the movement of buildings or other structures of a size or weight in excess of
legal maximums, within, into or through the City. In the event such a permit is sought,
application therefor shall be made to the Sheriff and to the Chief of the Department
of Fire and Rescue in accordance with Section 11.58.060 et seq.
(Ord. No. 6816, § 116, 8-17-22; Ord. 1021 § 8(4), 1963: prior code § 10-29-8(D))

11.58.050.title: Oversize or overweight permits—Revocation of continuous
11.58.050.text:
If, after the issuance of a continuous special permit by the Department of Public
Works, pursuant to the provisions of Section 11.58.010 et seq., such Department determines that the traffic authorized by such continuous
special permit has caused substantial highway distress, then such permit may be revoked
summarily, but such revocation shall not operate to prevent a subsequent filing of
a new application for another continuous special permit.
(Ord. No. 6816, § 117, 8-17-22; Ord. 1021 § 10, 1963: prior code § 10-29-10)

11.58.060.title: Structure permits—Authorized for single trips
11.58.060.text:
The Sheriff and Chief of the Department of Fire and Rescue may, in their discretion,
upon application in writing filed with their respective departments at least forty-eight
hours in advance of the requested movement, issue a special permit in writing authorizing
the applicant to operate or move a vehicle, combination of vehicles or special mobile
equipment for the purpose of transporting a building or other structure of a size
or weight in excess of the legal maximums set forth in this Chapter, within, into
or through the City. Such permits shall be issued on a single trip basis only.
(Ord. No. 6816, § 118, 8-17-22; Ord. 1021 § 9(1, 2), 1963: prior code § 10-29-9(A,
B))

11.58.070.title: Structure permits—Conditions
11.58.070.text:
In issuing such special permits as are contemplated in Section 11.58.060, the Sheriff and Chief of the Department of Fire and Rescue may impose such conditions
thereon, such as routes to be followed, place of operation or movement, time of operation
or movement or other matters, as they shall deem necessary or proper to protect the
streets, highways and alleys from excessive damage or to minimize the dangers, inconveniences
or delays to the general public.
(Ord. No. 6816, § 119, 8-17-22; Ord. 1021 § 9(3), 1963: prior code § 10-29-9(C))

11.58.080.title: Structure permits—Application
11.58.080.text:
The application for a special permit provided for in Section 11.58.060 shall:
(A)
Specifically describe the vehicle, combination of vehicles or special mobile equipment,
and load thereon, including the width, length, total gross weight with load imposed
and number of axles of the vehicle or equipment and the width, length and height of
the building or other structure to be moved thereby;
(B)
Indicate the particular streets, highways or alleys over which the special permit
to operate or move is requested;
(C)
State the date and time for which such special permit is requested.
(Ord. 1021 § 9(4), 1963: prior code § 10-29-9(D))

11.58.090.title: Structure permits—Prerequisites
11.58.090.text:
Before a special permit may be issued under Section 11.58.060, the applicant shall first have obtained from the Department of Community Development
the permit required in Chapter 16.04 of this Code and shall have paid to and deposited with the Director of the Department
of Community Development the license fee and bond required by Chapter 6.02.
(Ord. No. 6816, § 120, 8-17-22; Ord. 1021 § 9(5), 1963: prior code § 10-29-9(E))

11.58.100.title: Permit display for inspection
11.58.100.text:
Every special permit or a photocopy thereof, issued pursuant to this Chapter, shall:
(A)
Be carried in each vehicle, combination of vehicles, special self-propelled equipment
or special mobile equipment to which it refers.
(B)
Be open to inspection at all times by any officer of the Metropolitan Police Department
or agent of the Department of Public Works.
(Ord. No. 6816, § 121, 8-17-22; Ord. 1021 § 11, 1963: prior code § 10-29-11)

11.58.110.title: Violation—Misdemeanor
11.58.110.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person to operate or move any vehicle or equipment contemplated
in this Chapter over any public street, highway or alley within the City without first
obtaining a special permit pursuant to the provisions of this Chapter, or to violate
or evade any of the terms or conditions of such permit when issued, and any person
violating any of the provisions of this Chapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
(Ord. 1021 § 12, 1963: prior code § 10-29-12)

11.60.010.title: Designation authority generally
11.60.010.text:
The City Traffic Engineer is authorized and required to establish:
(A)
Bus stops, bus stands, taxicab stands and stands for other passenger common carrier
motor vehicles; and
(B)
Points for the origin and destination of the routes of transit buses on such public
streets or public property, in such places and in such number, and he may designate
the length of time that a bus may stand or park at each, as he shall determine to
be of the greatest benefit and convenience to the public, and every such bus stop,
bus stand, taxicab stand, other stand or origin or destination point shall be designated
by appropriate signs.
(Ord. 3285 § 1, 1987: Ord. 1589 § 11 (part), 1972: prior code § 10-18-7)

11.60.020.title: Use by other vehicles
11.60.020.text:
No person shall stop, stand or park a vehicle other than a bus in a bus stop, or other
than a taxicab in a taxicab stand when any such stop or stand has been officially
designated and appropriately signed.
(Ord. No. 6829, § 9, 2-1-23; Ord. 5870 § 26, 2006: Ord. 1589 § 11 (part), 1972: prior
code § 10-18-9)

11.60.030.title: Bus parking, loading and unloading
11.60.030.text:
(A)
The operator of a bus, other than a tour bus, shall:
(1)
Not stand or park such vehicle upon any street at any place other than a bus stop,
bus stand or the origin or destination point for the route to which such vehicle is
assigned which has been designated in accordance with Section 11.60.010 of this Chapter;
(2)
Not stop such vehicle upon any street at any place for the purpose of loading or unloading
passengers or their baggage other than at a bus stop, bus stand, passenger loading
zone or the origin or destination point for the route to which such vehicle is assigned
which has been designated in accordance with Section 11.60.010, except in case of an emergency;
(3)
Not use any location as the point of origin or destination of the route of such vehicle
other than the origin or destination point for the route to which such vehicle is
assigned which has been designated in accordance with Section 11.60.010;
(4)
Enter a bus stop, bus stand, passenger loading zone or origin or destination point
on a public street in such a manner that the bus when stopped to load or unload passengers
or baggage shall be in a position with the right-hand front wheel of such vehicle
not farther than eighteen inches from the curb and the bus approximately parallel
to the curb so as not to unduly impede the movement of other vehicular traffic;
(5)
Not stand or park a bus at a bus stop or an origin or destination point for a period
of time longer than has been designated for such bus stop or origin or destination
point in accordance with Section 11.60.010.
(B)
(1)
Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (2) of this Subsection, the operator of
a tour bus shall not stand or park such vehicle, except while actually and expeditiously
engaged in the loading or unloading of passengers, upon any street except at a location
which has been duly designated and marked as a tour bus loading zone in accordance
with Section 11.44.080.
(2)
The prohibition contained in paragraph (1) of this Subsection does not apply:
(a)
To any tour bus when it is being used to transport passengers on a "celebrity home"
tour or to any function of a duly established and recognized nonprofit organization
for which function the organization has complied with any applicable requirements
of State law regarding charitable solicitations; provided, however, that no such vehicle
shall be allowed to stand or park in any one location for a period in excess of thirty
minutes,
(b)
In the case of an emergency which requires the standing or parking of such vehicle
contrary to the provisions of paragraph (1) of this subsection.
(Ord. No. 6296, § 33, 2-5-14; Ord. 3285 § 2, 1987: Ord. 3173 § 1 1985: Ord. 1589 §
11 (part), 1972: prior code § 10-18-8(A—C))

11.60.040.title: Taxi stopping, standing or parking
11.60.040.text:
The operator of a taxicab shall not stand or park such vehicle upon any street at
any place other than in a taxicab stand so designated as provided herein. This provision
shall not prevent the operator of a taxicab from temporarily stopping in accordance
with other stopping or parking regulations at any place for the purpose of and while
actually engaged in the expeditious loading or unloading of passengers.
(Ord. 1589 § 11 (part), 1972: prior code § 10-18-8(D))

11.60.050.title: Taxistands—Use required
11.60.050.text:
It is unlawful for any person to park a vehicle, as herein defined, for the purpose
of seeking or awaiting employment in any place upon the streets in the City, other
than at stands designated therefor, as herein provided, and marked by appropriate
signs and curb painting by the Traffic Engineer.
(Ord. 2203 § 27 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-17-34 (part))

11.60.060.title: Taxistands—Establishment—Use rules
11.60.060.text:
The Traffic Engineer shall, upon the order of the City Manager, establish taxistands
in such places on the streets and in such number as the City Manager shall determine
to be of the greatest benefit and convenience to the public. All taxistands established
under this Section shall be "open stands," meaning that no given cab company shall
have any superior right to occupy any particular stand over any other cab company.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 42, 6-18-14; Ord. 2203 § 27 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-17-34
(part))

11.60.070.title: Reserved
11.60.070.text:
Editor's note—
Ord. No. 6326, § 43, adopted June 18, 2014, repealed § 11.60.070, which pertained
to taxistands—permits to use and derived from prior code § 10-17-34; Ord. No. 2203,
1981 and Ord. No. 5241, 2000.

11.60.080.title: Taxistands—Use by others
11.60.080.text:
Except for authorized emergency vehicles it is unlawful to stop, stand or park a vehicle
of any description for any purpose or period of time at any area designated as a taxistand
in accordance with the provisions of Section 11.60.050 et seq.; provided, however, that any such other vehicle may temporarily stop thereat,
subject to the provisions of this Code, only for the purpose of and while actually
and expeditiously engaged in unloading passengers, when such stopping does not interfere
with any cab lawfully entitled to occupy such stand, waiting to enter or about to
enter upon such stand.
(Ord. 2203 § 27 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-17-34 (part))

11.60.090.title: Taxistands—Right turn after exiting
11.60.090.text:
Any cab, upon leaving any stand designated in accordance with the provisions of this
Section, shall execute a right-hand turn, when a sign is posted giving notice of this
requirement, at the first street intersection after it leaves such stand.
(Ord. 2203 § 27 (part), 1981: prior code § 10-17-34 (part))

11.62.010.title: Purpose
11.62.010.text:
This Chapter is adopted pursuant to Chapter 76, Statutes of Nevada 1991, to provide
for the issuance of permits to charitable organizations to solicit charitable contributions
on the median strips of highways or on sidewalks adjacent to highways.
(Ord. 3600 § 2, 1991)

11.62.020.title: Definitions
11.62.020.text:
As used in this Chapter, unless the context otherwise indicates, the following terms
shall have the meanings that are ascribed to them as follows:
(A)
"Charitable organization" means an organization which:
(1)
The Secretary of the Treasury has determined is an exempt organization pursuant to
the provisions of Section 501(c) of the Internal Revenue Code; and
(2)
Holds a current certificate of organization or is currently qualified by the Secretary
of State to do business in this State.
(B)
"Highway" means the entire width between the boundary lines of every way maintained
by a public authority when any part thereof is open to the use of the public for purposes
of vehicular traffic. The term does not include a "freeway" as that term is defined
in NRS 408.060.
(C)
"Highway solicitation permit" means a certificate of authority issued by the Department
of Public Works to a charitable organization which allows the holder of the permit
to solicit charitable contributions for its organization while standing on the median
strip of any highway or the sidewalk adjacent to the highway within the jurisdiction
of the City.
(Ord. No. 6296, § 34, 2-5-14; Ord. 3600 § 3, 1991)

11.62.030.title: Permit required
11.62.030.text:
No charitable organization shall solicit contributions from the median strip of any
highway or the sidewalk adjacent to the highway within the jurisdiction of the City
without first obtaining and thereafter maintaining a valid unexpired highway solicitation
permit and proof of compliance with any State law requirements regarding charitable
organizations.
(Ord. No. 6296, § 35, 2-5-14; Ord. 3600 § 4, 1991)

11.62.040.title: Liability
11.62.040.text:
Every charitable organization that applies for and receives a highway solicitation
permit shall:
(A)
Indemnify the City against any injury to any person or damage to any property during
the solicitation which arises from or is incident to the act of solicitation; and
(B)
Be liable for any injury to any person or damage to any property during the solicitation
which arises from negligence of the soliciting agent.
(Ord. 3600 § 5, 1991)

11.62.050.title: Application contents
11.62.050.text:
(A)
An application for a highway solicitation permit shall be made to the Department of
Public Works upon forms provided by the Department.
(B)
An application shall be filed with the Department at least five business days prior
to the date on which the solicitation is to begin and shall contain the following
information:
(1)
The name, street address, and telephone number of the applicant and the charitable
organization of behalf of which the application is made;
(2)
The name, street address, and telephone number of the person who will be responsible
for the conduct of the solicitation;
(3)
The date on which the solicitation is to begin and the time of day when the solicitation
is to begin and end for each day requested;
(4)
The location(s) of the solicitation;
(5)
The purpose of the solicitation;
(6)
Proof of being a charitable organization as defined herein; and
(7)
A declaration that no one less than eighteen years of age will be permitted to participate
in the solicitation.
(C)
A post office box address shall be unacceptable as a street address on an application
where a street address is required; provided, however, an applicant may identify and
designate on his application a post office box address as the address to which he
prefers correspondence to be mailed.
(Ord. No. 6296, § 36, 2-5-14; Ord. 3600 § 6, 1991)

11.62.060.title: Application approval requirements
11.62.060.text:
Upon receipt of:
(A)
A completed application for a highway solicitation permit;
(B)
Payment of a permit fee in the sum of fifty dollars; and
(C)
Satisfactory proof that the applicant has procured a comprehensive general liability
insurance policy in the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars that names the City as
an additional assured;
The Director of the Department shall review the application for approval.
(Ord. 3600 § 7, 1991)

11.62.070.title: Permit—Time limit
11.62.070.text:
Upon approval of an application, the Director shall issue a highway solicitation permit
for the period requested which may not exceed three days in a calendar year.
(Ord. 3600 § 8, 1991)

11.62.080.title: Permit—Hours of use
11.62.080.text:
Highway solicitation permits shall be issued for solicitation between the hours of
sunrise and sunset.
(Ord. 3600 § 9, 1991)

11.62.090.title: Permit—Age requirement
11.62.090.text:
No person whose age is less than eighteen years may be permitted to participate in
any highway solicitation.
(Ord. 3600 § 10, 1991)

11.62.100.title: Solicitation—Unlawful when
11.62.100.text:
It is unlawful for any person engaged in highway solicitation to:
(A)
Solicit unless he wears an orange vest as safety clothing pursuant to Nevada Revised
Statutes;
(B)
Solicit on a median strip that is less than four feet wide; provided, however, that
if a median strip of adequate width is not available, solicitors may start and end
their solicitation on a sidewalk;
(C)
Solicit while:
(1)
Standing within that portion of a highway specifically designated for travel and use
by vehicles.
(2)
Walking from vehicle to vehicle within that portion of a highway specifically designated
for travel and use by vehicles;
(D)
Solicit at any location that is under construction or repair if such person must,
because of the construction or repair, solicit from a position other than on the median
strip of the highway or sidewalk adjacent to the highway.
(Ord. 3600 § 11, 1991)

11.62.110.title: Violation—Penalty
11.62.110.text:
Whenever in this Chapter any act is prohibited or is made or declared to be unlawful
or an offense or a misdemeanor, or whenever in this Chapter the doing of any act is
required or the failure to do any act is made or declared to be unlawful or an offense
or a misdemeanor, the doing of such prohibited act or the failure to do any such required
act shall constitute a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished
by a fine of not more than one thousand dollars or by imprisonment for a term of not
more than six months, or by any combination of such fine and imprisonment. Any day
of any violation of this Chapter shall constitute a separate offense.
(Ord. 3600 § 13, 1991)

11.65.010.title: Definitions
11.65.010.text:
To provide clarification of terminology used herein the following definitions are
provided:
(A)
"Residential area" means a contiguous or nearly contiguous area containing public
streets and highways or parts thereof where residents dwell.
(B)
"Residential parking permit" means a sticker, decal or placard with a unique color
that:
(1)
Defines an area or unique address to which it pertains;
(2)
Is identified by a number;
(3)
Includes an expiration date;
(4)
Lists the license plate number of the vehicle to which it pertains; and
(5)
Is to be placed on a resident's vehicle to identify that vehicle as exempt from the
parking restrictions contained in this Chapter.
(C)
"Residential permit parking zone" means a residential area designated as herein provided
where resident motor vehicles displaying a valid permit as described herein shall
be exempt from parking time restrictions established pursuant to this Chapter.
(D)
"Visitor parking permit" means a placard issued to a residence to be used in the vehicles
of visitors to a residence to exempt that vehicle from the parking restrictions contained
in this Chapter.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 44, 6-18-14; Ord. 5870 § 27, 2006: Ord. 3647 § 1 (part), 1992)

11.65.020.title: Parking zones and parking permits authorized when
11.65.020.text:
With respect to any residential parking permit zone established pursuant to this Chapter:
(A)
The City Traffic Engineer is authorized to establish within the residential parking
permit zone one or more time limited parking zones, in each case for time periods
up to three hours;
(B)
For purposes of Subsection (A) of LVMC 11.65.050, the City Traffic Engineer is authorized to establish other parking restrictions
within the residential parking permit zone, including the times, locations and conditions
under which parking shall be by permit only.
(C)
The Parking Services Division of the Department of Economic and Urban Development
is authorized to issue residential parking permits and visitor permits to residents
who qualify for such permits in accordance with this Chapter.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 45, 6-18-14; Ord. No. 6089, § 1, 4-21-10; Ord. 5672 § 1, 2004: Ord.
3647 § 1 (part), 1992)

11.65.030.title: Parking zones—Qualifications
11.65.030.text:
Any residential area within the City shall be deemed eligible to apply for a residential
permit parking zone providing the area in question meets the requirements of Subsections
(A), (B) and (C) and, in addition, the requirements of either Subsection (D) or Subsection
(E):
(A)
The residential area requesting a residential permit parking zone is in close proximity
to a commercial or other development with a high parking demand;
(B)
The streets for which a residential permit parking zone is requested are primarily
residential streets;
(C)
A signed petition requesting the zone which contains signatures representing fifty-one
percent of the residences affected is submitted to the City Traffic Engineer;
(D)
A parking study has been submitted which shows that seventy percent or more of the
available on-street spaces are occupied, for a period in excess of two hours between
the hours of eight a.m. and six p.m. and that twenty-five percent of the parked vehicles
are nonresident vehicles;
(E)
The residential area is in close proximity to an area or development that, on an annual
basis, hosts at least five special events with a high parking demand.
(Ord. No. 6394, § 1, 1-21-15; Ord. 3647 § 1 (part), 1992)

11.65.040.title: Parking zones—Approval criteria
11.65.040.text:
The approval of a residential area for a residential permit parking zone will be carried
out in the following manner:
(A)
A request for a residential permit parking zone shall be submitted in writing to the
City Traffic Engineer by a resident or residents of the affected residential area.
(B)
A survey, as described in this Chapter, will be conducted by the Transportation Engineering
Division to determine if the area qualifies for a residential permit parking zone.
(C)
The residents of the area shall be notified by the Transportation Engineering Division
of the results of the survey and of future action to be taken.
(D)
A petition prepared by the Transportation Engineering Division shall be delivered
to the requestor(s) for them to contact all of the affected residences and obtain
signatures and addresses supporting the establishment of a residential permit parking
zone.
(E)
Upon completion and verification as to the accuracy of the petition by the City Traffic
Engineer, the proposal shall be taken to the next regular meeting of the Traffic and
Parking Commission for its recommendation to the City Traffic Engineer.
(1)
If the recommendation of the City Traffic and Parking Commission is favorable, the
City Traffic Engineer must grant the request, and amend Schedule 17-VI by written
finding subject to LVMC 11.65.020.
(2)
If the recommendation of the City Traffic and Parking Commission is not favorable,
the City Traffic Engineer must deny the request and give the requestor written notice
of such decision within fifteen days of the recommendation.
(3)
The written notice required in Subsection (E)(2) of this Section must state that the
requestor may appeal such decision by filing a notice of appeal with the City Clerk's
office within forty-five days of the date of said notice.
(4)
The City Council shall hear the appeal at the next regularly scheduled meeting following
the expiration of ten days after the filing of the notice of appeal, and either affirm,
reverse or modify the decision of the City Traffic Engineer, or take such other action
it deems warranted.
(Ord. No. 6394, § 2, 1-21-15; Ord. 3990 § 20, 1996: Ord. 3647 § 1 (part), 1992)

11.65.050.title: Parking zones—Signposting—Parking permit eligibility and resource
11.65.050.text:
(A)
The approval of a residential permit parking zone is within the discretion of the
City Council. Once a residential permit parking zone has been approved by the City
Council:
(1)
The Transportation Engineering Division shall install parking signs on the streets
designated as a residential permit parking zone. The signs, as they may be updated
or supplemented from time to time by the Parking Services Division of the Department
of Economic and Urban Development, shall indicate the times, locations and conditions
under which parking shall be by permit only;
(2)
The Parking Services Division shall issue a maximum of three permanent residential
parking permits and a maximum of two visitor placards per residence for a designated
residential permit parking zone upon application and payment of the application fee
by a person eligible for such permit; and
(3)
In the case of permits designed to be used during special events in the area, the
Parking Services Division shall provide to permit holders such advance notice of those
events as is deemed feasible and appropriate.
(B)
A person is eligible to apply for a residential parking permit if he/she owns or operates
a motor vehicle and resides on property immediately adjacent to a street, avenue or
other location within the residential permit parking zone. Proof of residency in the
residential permit parking zone on a block designated for implementation must be presented
at the time application is made.
(C)
The application for a permit shall contain the name of the owner or operator of the
motor vehicle; residential address; the make, model, registration and license plate
number of the motor vehicle; and the number of the driver's license of the applicant.
The motor vehicle registration and the driver's license of the applicant must be presented
at the time of making said application in order to verify the contents thereof. The
owner or operator of any motor vehicle applying for a residential parking permit shall
have a valid Nevada motor vehicle license. The motor vehicle registration must show
the applicant's present address.
(Ord. No. 6394, § 1, 1-21-15; Ord. 5870 § 28, 2006: Ord. 4074 § 1, 1997: Ord. 3647
§ 1 (part), 1992)

11.65.060.title: Parking permit—Fee—Renewal—Exemption
11.65.060.text:
(A)
Each as otherwise provided in this Section, each person who applies for a residential
parking permit pursuant to LVMC 11.65.050 shall be charged a fee of twenty dollars to cover the administrative costs of permits,
studies and signing of the zone. The fee shall entitle the applicant to a maximum
of three residential parking permits for vehicles housed at the residence of the applicant
and two visitor parking placards.
(B)
Upon presentation of adequate proof, persons sixty-five years of age or older who
otherwise qualify for the permit shall be exempt from paying the application fee.
(C)
The City Council may waive the application fee in other particular cases for good
cause shown and in the public interest.
(Ord. 5212 § 1, 2000: Ord. 4074 § 2, 1997: Ord. 3647 § 1 (part), 1992)

11.65.070.title: Parking permit—Use procedure and restrictions
11.65.070.text:
(A)
Notwithstanding any provisions of this Chapter to the contrary, the holder of a residential
parking permit shall be permitted to stand or park a motor vehicle for which a permit
has been issued in the residential permit parking zone designated by the permit without
being subjected to the limitations imposed on vehicles lacking the permit; provided,
however, that parking at that location is otherwise permitted. While a vehicle for
which a residential parking permit has been issued is so parked, such permit shall
be displayed so as to be clearly visible either on the lower left hand corner of the
rear window or hanging from the rear view mirror of the vehicle.
(B)
A residential parking permit shall not authorize the holder thereof to stand or park
a motor vehicle in such places, or during such times, as the stopping, standing, or
parking of motor vehicles is prohibited or set aside for specific types of vehicles,
and does not exempt the holder from the observance of any traffic regulation other
than the parking time limit.
(C)
A residential parking permit shall not guarantee or reserve to the holder thereof
an on-street parking space within the designated residential permit parking area.
(Ord. 5870 § 29, 2006: Ord. 3647 § 1 (part), 1992)

11.65.080.title: Service vehicle parking procedures
11.65.080.text:
Service companies making service calls to residential dwellings within the residential
permit parking zone shall notify the Parking Services Division of the Department of
Economic and Urban Development of company vehicles which will be parked in residential
parking zones in order to be exempt from holding a residential parking zone permit
and exempt from the posted time limits. Such service vehicles shall display the name
of the company on the vehicle or identify the vehicle by an approved placard placed
on the left side of the dash.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 46, 6-18-14; Ord. 3647 § 1 (part), 1992)

11.65.090.title: Temporary permits
11.65.090.text:
Temporary residents of a residential permit parking zone whose vehicles are registered
in another state may apply for a visitor permit for the duration of the thirty-day
reciprocity period allowed under Nevada law. Applicants must have a valid driver's
license and motor vehicle registration from the home state and a rent or utility bill
receipt or some other adequate proof of residence in a residential permit parking
zone. The fee shall be five dollars and may be applied toward a resident sticker for
the balance of the year when the registration of the vehicle is matched to the local
address.
(Ord. 3647 § 1 (part), 1992)

11.65.100.title: Visitor's permit requirements
11.65.100.text:
In a residential permit parking zone the holder of a residential parking permit may
apply for a visitor's permit which shall be valid for the current calendar year and
shall be renewable but not transferable. The application shall be signed by the permit
holder host. No permit holder shall be issued more than two visitors' permits at any
given time.
(Ord. 3647 § 1 (part), 1992)

11.65.110.title: Unlawful activities designated
11.65.110.text:
(A)
It shall constitute a violation of this regulation for any person to falsely represent
himself as eligible for a residential parking permit or to furnish any false information
in an application to the Parking Services Division of the Department of Economic and
Urban Development in order to obtain a residential parking permit.
(B)
No person other than the permittee named shall use a residential parking permit or
display it on a vehicle operated or parked, and any such use or display by a person
other than the permittee shall constitute a violation of this Section by the permittee
and by the person who so used or displayed such parking permit.
(Ord. No. 6394, § 4, 1-21-15; Ord. 3647 § 1 (part), 1992)

11.65.120.title: Parking permit—Revocation conditions
11.65.120.text:
(A)
The Parking Services Division of the Department of Economic and Urban Development
is authorized to revoke the residential parking permit of any permittee found to be
in violation of Section 11.65.110, and upon written notification thereof the permittee shall surrender such permit
to the Parking Services Division.
(B)
Any person who shall violate any provision of Section 11.65.110 shall, upon conviction, be subject to punishment by a fine of not more than one hundred
dollars or imprisonment of not more than ninety days, or both.
(C)
Any person parking a motor vehicle not displaying a valid permit in a residential
permit parking zone for a period exceeding the time limitation established shall be
subjected to the fine established for overtime parking in Section 11.10.150 of the Las Vegas Municipal Code.
(D)
Any vehicle parked in a residential permit parking zone in violation of these provisions
causing a severe hazard to traffic conditions shall be subject to immediate impoundment.
(Ord. No. 6326, § 47, 6-18-14; Ord. 3647 § 1 (part), 1992)

11.68.010.title: Findings
11.68.010.text:
(A)
In connection with the adoption of LVMC Chapter 11.68 in 1995, the City Council made the following findings: That there has been a progressive
decline in the economic growth and vitality of businesses located in the central business
district of the City which is attributable to the decrease in tourists and other visitors
to the central business district, that a special effort is needed on the part of the
City to create new jobs, maintain existing employment opportunities, attract new businesses,
tourists and visitors to the central business district and thereby restore the economic
growth and vitality thereof and that the closure of certain streets or parts thereof
to vehicular traffic and the creation of a Pedestrian Mall for the movement, safety,
convenience, enjoyment, entertainment, recreation and relaxation of pedestrians is
in the best interest of the City and beneficial to the owners of adjacent property
and the businesses located in the central business district.
(B)
The Council incorporates and makes the same findings in connection with the readoption
of this Chapter in 2006 and subsequent amendments thereto.
(C)
In 1995, the City Council further found, and continues to find, that it is in the
best interest of the public to select and contract with a private operating entity
for the acquisition, construction, improvement, operation, management or maintenance
of the Pedestrian Mall.
(D)
Since the creation of the Pedestrian Mall, the City has enacted various ordinances
attempting to maintain the Pedestrian Mall's principal purpose, which is to serve
as an economic and entertainment venue that will enhance the historical central business
district. Prior to the Mall's creation, the former Fremont Street area had become
known as unseemly and crime ridden, with tourists and businesses leaving the area
for a safer and more hospitable environment. The Pedestrian Mall was created to reverse
that declining environment, and provide a safe and enjoyable entertainment experience
to attract tourism and thereby support surrounding economic growth.
(E)
Over the years, the City has amended its ordinances endeavoring to facilitate and
enhance the Mall's purpose. Most recently, in 2011, the City and the American Civil
Liberties Union of Nevada settled a long-standing lawsuit concerning expressive activities
within the Mall. Specifically, the City, Fremont Street Experience, LLC and the ACLU
endeavored to jointly reach a compromise as to various ordinance amendments to address
what types of restrictions upon expressive activity would be appropriate. Although
those amendments were created by a cooperative effort and ultimately adopted, it was
understood and expressly discussed before the City Council that those amendments and
restrictions may not be adequate to address public safety and preservation of the
Mall's purpose, considering its unique environment. The City would test the effectiveness
of those ordinance amendments to determine whether additional or lesser restrictions
were warranted.
(F)
Since those 2011 amendments, the Mall's environment and function has deteriorated.
The 2011 amendments principally imposed various distance restrictions from specific
uses where expressive activity could occur. However, considering the Pedestrian Mall's
congested nature, it appears that the distance restrictions have created uncertainty
among the general public and thus have led to confusion as well as in-fighting as
to where expressive activity may or may not occur. Indeed, the environment of the
Pedestrian Mall has become such that certain persons or groups have attempted to monopolize
certain locations, have been the recipients of threats and other forms of intimidation
in an attempt to control certain areas where expressive activity is presently allowed.
Unfortunately, the 2011 amendments have facilitated an inhospitable environment that
is incompatible with the Mall's entertainment and commercial purposes, and has further
resulted in a deterioration of public safety and well-being.
(G)
Considering the confusion as to where expressive activity is appropriate, particularly
activity engaged in by street performers, and to combat infighting and competition
for the most desirable locations, to enhance access for all desired users of the Mall,
including those seeking to engage in expressive activity, the City determines that
it is necessary and appropriate to create designated areas for the activities of street
